old: The Greek pronoun αὐτός ("he") is masculine, although its antecedent σπέρμα ("seed") is neuter. Early Christian readers noticed this. τηρέω means "watch, guard, keep watch for"; the Greek uses it in both clauses, so both get "watch for."
new: The Greek pronoun αὐτός ("he") is masculine, although its antecedent σπέρμα ("seed") is neuter. τηρέω means "watch, guard, keep watch for"; the Greek uses it in both clauses, so both get "watch for."
reason: Reception-history remark is not about the Greek; removed to keep the note neutral and factual.

old: And to Adam He said, "Because you listened to the voice of your wife and ate from the tree that I commanded you, this one alone, not to eat from, and you ate from it, cursed is the earth in your labors; in pains you will eat from it all the days of your life;
new: And to Adam He said, "Because you listened to the voice of your wife and ate from the tree that I commanded you, this one alone, not to eat from, and you ate from it, cursed is the earth in your labors; in pains you will eat it all the days of your life;
reason: ἐν λύπαις φάγῃ αὐτήν has a direct object (αὐτήν, the earth) with no ἀπό; "from" is supplied.

old: And Adam knew Eve his wife, and she conceived and gave birth to a son. And she called his name Seth, saying, "For God has raised up for me another offspring in place of Abel, whom Cain killed."
new: And Adam knew Eve his wife, and she conceived and gave birth to a son. And she called his name Seth, saying, "For God has raised up for me another seed in place of Abel, whom Cain killed."
reason: σπέρμα is rendered "seed" throughout (3:15; 12:7; 13:15-16; 15:3-18; 17:7-19); keep the same English here.

old: In 5:22 and 5:24, the Septuagint translates Enoch's walking with God as "pleased God" and adds "was not found, because God transferred him," the wording echoed in Hebrews 11:5.
new: In 5:22 and 5:24, the Septuagint translates Enoch's walking with God as "pleased God" and renders "he was not, for God took him" as "was not found, because God transferred him," the wording echoed in Hebrews 11:5.
reason: The Greek does not add the clause; it renders the Hebrew "he was not, for God took him" differently, so "adds" is inaccurate.

old: Therefore, make for yourself an ark out of squared timbers; you will make nests in the ark, and you will coat it inside and outside with bitumen.
new: Therefore, make for yourself an ark out of squared timbers; you will make nests in the ark, and you will coat it inside and outside with asphalt.
reason: ἄσφαλτος is rendered "asphalt" in 11:3 and 14:10; use the same English here.

old: And God blessed Noah and his sons, and said to them, "Increase and multiply, and fill the earth and exercise dominion over it.
new: And God blessed Noah and his sons, and said to them, "Increase and multiply, and fill the earth and gain mastery over it.
reason: κατακυριεύσατε αὐτῆς is the same phrase rendered "gain mastery over it" in 1:28, which this verse echoes.

old: The Septuagint adds "and exercise dominion over it" at the end of the blessing (echoing Gen 1:28), a clause absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
new: The Septuagint adds "and gain mastery over it" at the end of the blessing (echoing Gen 1:28), a clause absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
reason: Updated quoted wording to match the revised verse.

old: "Look, I am establishing My covenant with you and with your offspring after you,
new: "Look, I am establishing My covenant with you and with your seed after you,
reason: τῷ σπέρματι ὑμῶν μεθ᾽ ὑμᾶς is the same formula rendered "your seed after you" in 17:7-10, 19.

old: And he moved away from there to the mountain east of Bethel, and he pitched his tent there, with Bethel toward the sea and Ai toward the east; and he built an altar there to the Lord and called upon the name of the Lord.
new: And he moved away from there to the mountain east of Bethel, and he pitched his tent there in Bethel toward the sea, with Ai toward the east; and he built an altar there to the Lord and called upon the name of the Lord.
reason: This Greek reads ἐν Βαιθὴλ κατὰ θάλασσαν, "in Bethel toward the sea"; "with Bethel toward the sea" follows the Hebrew/Rahlfs form without ἐν.

old: Both here and in the well's name in 16:14 (Φρέαρ οὗ ἐνώπιον εἶδον, corresponding to Hebrew Beer-lahai-roi), the Greek uses ἐνώπιον ("in person" or "face to face") to express Hagar's marvel at having seen God directly.
new: Both here and in the well's name in 16:14 (Φρέαρ οὗ ἐνώπιον εἶδον, corresponding to Hebrew Beer-lahai-roi), the Greek uses ἐνώπιον ("in person" or "face to face").
reason: Interpretive comment about Hagar's feelings is not about the Greek; note trimmed to the lexical fact.

old: And Sarah laughed within herself, saying, "It has not yet happened to me until now, and my lord is old."
new: And Sarah laughed within herself, saying, "It has not yet happened to me until now, but my lord is old."
reason: Οὔπω μέν ... ὁ δὲ κύριός μου πρεσβύτερος is a μέν ... δέ contrast; "and" loses the adversative δέ.

old: Come, therefore, let us give our father wine to drink and let us lie with him, and let us raise up offspring from our father."
new: Come, therefore, let us give our father wine to drink and let us lie with him, and let us raise up seed from our father."

new: And it happened on the next day that the older one said to the younger one, "Look, yesterday I lay with our father; let us give him wine to drink this night also, and go in and lie with him, and let us raise up seed from our father."

old: And God came in to Abimelech in a dream at night, and said to him, "Look, you are about to die because of the woman whom you took, for she is married to a husband."
new: And God came in to Abimelech in his sleep at night, and said to him, "Look, you are about to die because of the woman whom you took, for she is married to a husband."

new: Greek ἐν ὕπνῳ means "in sleep" (Hebrew "in a dream"); likewise καθ᾽ ὕπνον in 20:6; 31:11, 24.
reason: One-sentence explanation for rendering ὕπνος literally where familiar English follows the Hebrew "dream."

old: And God said to him in a dream, "I also knew that you did this with a pure heart, and I Myself spared you from sinning against Me; because of this I did not allow you to touch her.
new: And God said to him in his sleep, "I also knew that you did this with a pure heart, and I Myself spared you from sinning against Me; because of this I did not allow you to touch her.

old: The Greek text explicitly adds "playing with her own son Isaac," specifying the object of Ishmael's playing (absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text).
new: The Greek text adds "with her own son Isaac," specifying with whom Ishmael was playing (absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text).

old: But God said to Abraham, "Do not let the matter be harsh before you concerning the child and concerning the maidservant; whatever Sarah says to you, listen to her voice, because in Isaac offspring will be called for you.
new: But God said to Abraham, "Do not let the matter be harsh before you concerning the child and concerning the maidservant; whatever Sarah says to you, listen to her voice, because in Isaac seed will be called for you.

old: And as for the son of this maidservant also, I will make him into a great nation, because he is your offspring."
new: And as for the son of this maidservant also, I will make him into a great nation, because he is your seed."

old: Now therefore, swear to me by God that you will not wrong me, nor my offspring, nor my name; but according to the righteousness that I have done with you, you will do with me, and to the land in which you have lived as a foreigner."
new: Now therefore, swear to me by God that you will not wrong me, nor my seed, nor my name; but according to the righteousness that I have done with you, you will do with me, and to the land in which you have lived as a foreigner."

old: surely blessing I will bless you, and multiplying I will multiply your offspring like the stars of heaven and like the sand along the shore of the sea; and your offspring will inherit the cities of the adversaries.
new: surely blessing I will bless you, and multiplying I will multiply your seed like the stars of heaven and like the sand along the shore of the sea; and your seed will inherit the cities of the adversaries.

new: The Greek text reads "the God of heaven and the God of the earth" and "to you I will give this land and to your offspring," where the Hebrew Masoretic Text omits "and the God of the earth" and "to you."

old: And she said, "Drink, sir." And she hurried and lowered the water jar onto her arm, and gave him a drink until he finished drinking.
new: And she said, "Drink, lord." And she hurried and lowered the water jar onto her arm, and gave him a drink until he finished drinking.

old: The Greek reads nominative εὐλογητὸς Κύριος ("Blessed is the Lord") as an exclamation of praise, rather than the Hebrew "blessed of the LORD" addressed to the servant.
new: The Greek reads nominative εὐλογητὸς Κύριος ("Blessed is the Lord") as an exclamation of praise, rather than the Hebrew "blessed of the Lord" addressed to the servant.

old: Now Isaac was journeying through the wilderness by the Well of Vision; for he was dwelling in the land toward the south.
new: Now Isaac was journeying through the wilderness by the Well of Vision; and he was dwelling in the land toward the south.

old: The Greek reads "Isaac entered the house of his mother" and ends with "concerning Sarah his mother," whereas the Hebrew reads "brought her into the tent of Sarah his mother" and "after his mother's death."
new: The Greek reads "Isaac entered the house of his mother" and ends with "concerning Sarah his mother," whereas the Hebrew reads "brought her into the tent of Sarah his mother" and "after his mother."
reason: The Hebrew literally reads "after his mother"; "death" is an interpretive supplement, so the note misquoted it.

old: Now Jacob cooked a stew, and Esau came from the plain, fainting.
new: Now Jacob cooked a stew, and Esau came from the field, fainting.
reason: πεδίον as Esau's hunting ground is "field" in 27:3 and 27:5 (and 24:63); keep the same English here.

old: And sojourn in this land, and I will be with you and bless you; for to you and to your offspring I will give all this land, and I will establish My oath that I swore to Abraham your father.
new: And sojourn in this land, and I will be with you and bless you; for to you and to your seed I will give all this land, and I will establish My oath that I swore to Abraham your father.

new: And the Lord appeared to him in that night and said, "I am the God of Abraham your father. Do not be afraid, for I am with you, and I will bless you and multiply your seed for the sake of Abraham your father."

old: and may He give you the blessing of Abraham your father, to you and to your offspring after you, to inherit the land of your sojourning, which God has given to Abraham."
new: and may He give you the blessing of Abraham your father, to you and to your seed after you, to inherit the land of your sojourning, which God has given to Abraham."

old: And the Lord stood firmly upon it and said, "I am the God of Abraham your father and the God of Isaac. Do not be afraid: the land on which you are sleeping, to you I will give it and to your offspring.
new: And the Lord stood firmly upon it and said, "I am the God of Abraham your father and the God of Isaac. Do not be afraid: the land on which you are sleeping, to you I will give it and to your seed.

old: And your offspring will be like the sand of the sea, and will spread out toward the sea and toward the south and toward the north and toward the east; and in you all the tribes of the earth will be blessed, and in your offspring.
new: And your seed will be like the sand of the sea, and will spread out toward the sea and toward the south and toward the north and toward the east; and in you all the tribes of the earth will be blessed, and in your seed.

old: And Jacob rose early in the morning, and took the stone that he had put there at his head and set it up as a pillar, and poured oil on the top of it.
new: And Jacob rose in the morning, and took the stone that he had put there at his head and set it up as a pillar, and poured oil on the top of it.
reason: The Greek has ἀνέστη ... τὸ πρωί ("rose in the morning"), not ὤρθρισεν; "early" follows the Hebrew (cf. the edition's 21:14; 22:3).

old: And Jacob called the name of that place House of God; yet Oulammaus was the name of the city previously.
new: And Jacob called the name of that place House of God; and Oulammaus was the name of the city previously.
reason: The Greek has plain καί; "yet" reproduces the Hebrew ulam ("however"), which the Greek has already absorbed into the name Oulammaus (as the note explains).

old: If he spoke like this, 'The speckled ones will be your wages,' then all the sheep would bear speckled ones; and if he said, 'The white ones will be your wages,' then all the sheep would bear white ones.
new: If he spoke like this, 'The variegated ones will be your wages,' then all the sheep would bear variegated ones; and if he said, 'The white ones will be your wages,' then all the sheep would bear white ones.
reason: ποικίλος is "variegated" in 30:37, 39, 40; "speckled" is the edition's word for ῥαντός, so using it here blurs the Greek color terms.

old: And it came about at the time when the sheep were conceiving, that I saw with my eyes in my sleep, and look, the male goats and the rams were mounting the sheep and the goats, streaked with white, and speckled, and ash-colored dappled.
new: And it came about at the time when the sheep were conceiving, that I saw with my eyes in my sleep, and look, the male goats and the rams were mounting the sheep and the goats, white-streaked, and variegated, and ash-colored speckled.
reason: διάλευκοι καὶ ποικίλοι καὶ σποδοειδεῖς ῥαντοί is the same phrase as 30:39 ("white-streaked and variegated and ash-colored speckled"); here ποικίλοι became "speckled" and ῥαντοί "dappled".

old: And the angel of God said to me in a dream, 'Jacob, Jacob.' And I said, 'What is it?'
new: And the angel of God said to me in my sleep, 'Jacob, Jacob.' And I said, 'What is it?'
reason: καθ᾽ ὕπνον is "in sleep" (as ἐν τῷ ὕπνῳ in v. 10 is rendered "in my sleep"); "dream" follows the Hebrew.

old: And He said, 'Look up with your eyes and see the male goats and the rams mounting the sheep and the goats, streaked with white, and speckled, and ash-colored dappled; for I have seen all that Laban is doing to you.
new: And he said, 'Look up with your eyes and see the male goats and the rams mounting the sheep and the goats, white-streaked, and variegated, and ash-colored speckled; for I have seen all that Laban is doing to you.
reason: Color terms as in 30:39 (ποικίλους = "variegated", ῥαντούς = "speckled"); the subject of εἶπεν is ὁ ἄγγελος (v. 11), lowercased as for the angel's speech in 22:12, so the capital does not settle the referent.

old: And God came to Laban the Syrian in a dream during the night and said to him, "Guard yourself so that you never speak evil things with Jacob."
new: And God came to Laban the Syrian in his sleep during the night and said to him, "Guard yourself so that you never speak evil things with Jacob."
reason: καθ᾽ ὕπνον is "in sleep," not "in a dream" (Hebrew reading); consistent with 31:10.

old: Now Laban rose early in the morning, kissed his sons and his daughters, and blessed them; and Laban turned back and departed to his place.
new: Now Laban rose in the morning, kissed his sons and his daughters, and blessed them; and Laban turned back and departed to his place.
reason: ἀναστὰς ... τὸ πρωί is simply "rising in the morning"; "early" reflects the Hebrew verb "rose early," not this Greek.

old: two hundred female goats, twenty male goats, two hundred ewes, twenty rams,
new: two hundred female goats, twenty male goats, two hundred sheep, twenty rams,
reason: πρόβατα is the generic "sheep" (so rendered elsewhere, e.g. 31:38); "ewes" follows the Hebrew word, not the Greek.

old: Then Esau said, "Let me leave with you some of the people who are with me." But he said, "Why this? It is enough that I have found favor before you, lord."
new: Then Esau said, "I will leave with you some of the people who are with me." But he said, "Why this? It is enough that I have found favor before you, lord."
reason: Καταλείψω is future indicative "I will leave"; the hortatory "Let me leave" reflects the Hebrew cohortative, not the Greek.

old: Then Judah said to Onan, "Go in to your brother's wife and marry her as brother-in-law, and raise up offspring for your brother."
new: Then Judah said to Onan, "Go in to your brother's wife and marry her as brother-in-law, and raise up seed for your brother."
reason: σπέρμα → "seed" (OT-wide)

old: And Onan, knowing that the offspring would not be his, it happened that whenever he went in to his brother's wife, he poured it out on the ground so as not to give offspring to his brother.
new: And Onan, knowing that the seed would not be his, it happened that whenever he went in to his brother's wife, he poured it out on the ground so as not to give seed to his brother.
reason: σπέρμα → "seed" (OT-wide)

old: And Judah said, "Let her keep them, so that we may not be ridiculed; I indeed have sent this young goat, and you have not found her."
new: And Judah said, "Let her keep them, so that we may not be ridiculed; I indeed have sent this young goat, but you have not found her."
reason: ἐγὼ μὲν ... σὺ δέ sets up a contrast; the adversative δέ is "but," not "and."

old: Only remember me by yourself when it goes well for you, and show mercy toward me, and make mention of me to Pharaoh, and bring me out of this stronghold.
new: But remember me by yourself when it goes well for you, and show mercy toward me, and make mention of me to Pharaoh, and bring me out of this stronghold.
reason: The Greek opens with ἀλλά "but"; "Only" reflects the Hebrew "only remember me" and adds a limiting sense not in the Greek.

old: And Pharaoh said to all his servants, "Can we find a man like this, who has the Spirit of God in him?"
new: And Pharaoh said to all his servants, "Can we find a man like this, who has the spirit of God in him?"
reason: Anarthrous πνεῦμα θεοῦ on Pharaoh's lips is ambiguous; capital "Spirit" decides the referent, lowercase keeps the Greek's ambiguity.

old: Send one from among you, and fetch your brother, while you are led away until your words become evident, whether you are telling the truth or not; otherwise, by the health of Pharaoh, surely you are spies."
new: Send one from among you, and fetch your brother, but as for you, be led away until your words become evident, whether you are telling the truth or not; otherwise, by the health of Pharaoh, surely you are spies."
reason: ὑμεῖς δὲ ἀπάχθητε is an imperative ("but you, be led away"); "while you are led away" turns the command into a subordinate statement and drops the contrastive δέ.

old: if you are peaceable, let one of your brothers be held in prison, while you yourselves walk on and carry away the purchase of your grain supply,
new: if you are peaceable, let one of your brothers be held in prison, but you yourselves go and carry away the purchase of your grain supply,
reason: αὐτοὶ δὲ βαδίσατε καὶ ἀπαγάγετε are imperatives with adversative δέ; "while you yourselves walk on" recasts the commands as a subordinate clause.

old: And he said to his brothers, "My silver has been returned to me, and look, here it is in my bag." And their heart failed them, and they were troubled, saying to one another, "What is this that God has done to us?"
new: And he said to his brothers, "My silver has been returned to me, and look, here it is in my bag." And their heart was astonished, and they were troubled, saying to one another, "What is this that God has done to us?"
reason: ἐξέστη ἡ καρδία means the heart was astounded (ἐξίστημι, rendered "astonished" in 43:33); "failed them" is a traditional English idiom, not the Greek sense.

old: Then Israel their father said to them, "If it is so, do this: take some of the fruits of the land in your vessels, and bring down gifts to the man—some resin and honey, incense and stacte and terebinth and walnuts.
new: Then Israel their father said to them, "If it is so, do this: take some of the fruits of the land in your vessels, and bring down gifts to the man—some resin and honey, incense and myrrh oil and terebinth and walnuts.
reason: στακτή is rendered "myrrh oil" in 37:25 in the same list (θυμίαμα, ῥιτίνη, στακτή); the transliteration "stacte" is inconsistent and obscure.

old: And Joseph commanded the one who was over his house, saying, "Fill the men's sacks with as much food as they are able to carry, and put each one's silver at the mouth of his sack,
new: And Joseph commanded the one who was over his house, saying, "Fill the men's bags with as much food as they are able to carry, and put each one's silver at the mouth of his bag,
reason: μάρσιππος is rendered "bag" throughout 42:27–43:23, with "sack" reserved for σάκκος (42:25, 35); keep the distinction here.

old: and put my silver cup into the sack of the youngest, and the price of his grain." And it was done according to the word of Joseph, just as he spoke.
new: and put my silver cup into the bag of the youngest, and the price of his grain." And it was done according to the word of Joseph, just as he spoke.
reason: μάρσιππον is "bag" in 42:27–43:23; "sack" is this edition's rendering of σάκκος.

old: If we returned to you from the land of Canaan the silver that we found in our sacks, how could we steal silver or gold from the house of your lord?
new: If we returned to you from the land of Canaan the silver that we found in our bags, how could we steal silver or gold from the house of your lord?
reason: μαρσίπποις is "bags" in 42:27–43:23 (the same returned silver); "sacks" renders σάκκος.

old: And they hurried and each one lowered his sack to the ground, and each one opened his sack.
new: And they hurried and each one lowered his bag to the ground, and each one opened his bag.
reason: μάρσιππον is "bag" in 42:27–43:23; "sack" is reserved for σάκκος.

old: And he searched, beginning from the oldest until he came to the youngest, and he found the cup in Benjamin's sack.
new: And he searched, beginning from the oldest until he came to the youngest, and he found the cup in Benjamin's bag.

old: And they tore their garments, and each one placed his sack upon his donkey, and they returned to the city.
new: And they tore their garments, and each one placed his bag upon his donkey, and they returned to the city.
reason: μάρσιππον is "bag" in 42:27–43:23; "sack" is reserved for σάκκος.

old: And you command these things: for them to take wagons from the land of Egypt for your little ones and your wives, and taking up your father, come.
new: And you, command these things: for them to take wagons from the land of Egypt for your little ones and your wives, and taking up your father, come.
reason: σὺ δὲ ἔντειλαι is an aorist imperative addressed to Joseph; without the comma 'And you command these things' reads as an indicative statement.

old: And having taken their possessions and all the property that they had acquired from the land of Canaan, Jacob entered into Egypt, and all his offspring with him,
new: And having taken their possessions and all the property that they had acquired from the land of Canaan, Jacob entered into Egypt, and all his seed with him,

old: sons and the sons of his sons with him, daughters and daughters of his sons with him; and he brought all his offspring into Egypt.

old: The Septuagint expands Joseph's genealogy with five additional descendants through Manasseh and Ephraim (Machir, Gilead, Sutalaam, Taam, and Edem; cf. Num 26:29–36), which accounts for Rachel's total of eighteen in v. 22.

old: and He said to me, 'Look, I will cause you to grow and multiply you, and I will make you into assemblies of nations, and I will give this land to you and to your offspring after you for an everlasting possession.'
new: and He said to me, 'Look, I will cause you to grow and multiply you, and I will make you into assemblies of nations, and I will give this land to you and to your seed after you for an everlasting possession.'

old: But the children whom you may father after these will be under the name of their brothers; they will be called in their allotments.

old: And Israel said to Joseph, "Look, I have not been deprived of your face, and look, God has shown me your offspring as well."
new: And Israel said to Joseph, "Look, I have not been deprived of your face, and look, God has shown me your seed as well."
reason: σπέρμα → "seed" (OT-wide)

old: And their bows were shattered with might, and the sinews of the arms of their hand were loosened by the hand of the Mighty One of Jacob; from there is the One who strengthened Israel, from the God of your father.
new: And their bows were shattered with might, and the sinews of the arms of their hand were loosened by the hand of the Mighty One of Jacob; from there is the one who strengthened Israel, from the God of your father.
reason: ὁ κατισχύσας Ἰσραήλ is an unspecified 'the one who strengthened Israel', said to come 'from the God of your father'; capital 'One' silently identifies the referent as God.

old: The Greek reads "their bows were shattered with might" and "the One who strengthened Israel," differing from the Masoretic Text's "his bow remained steady" and "the Shepherd, the Stone of Israel."
new: The Greek reads "their bows were shattered with might" and "the one who strengthened Israel," differing from the Masoretic Text's "his bow remained steady" and "the Shepherd, the Stone of Israel."
reason: Brings the quoted wording into line with the corrected verse (lowercase 'one' for the unspecified ὁ κατισχύσας).

old: Now Moses was shepherding the sheep of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian; and he led the sheep beyond the wilderness and came to Mount Horeb.
new: Now Moses was shepherding the sheep of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian; and he led the sheep toward the wilderness and came to Mount Horeb.
reason: ὑπὸ τὴν ἔρημον (ὑπό + accusative with a verb of motion) means 'toward/up to' the wilderness, not 'beyond'; 'beyond' follows the Hebrew 'behind the wilderness'.

old: And God spoke to Moses, saying, "I will be with you; and this will be the sign for you that I will send you out: when you bring My people out of Egypt, you will also worship God on this mountain."
new: And God spoke to Moses, saying, "I will be with you; and this will be the sign for you that I will send you out: when you bring My people out of Egypt, you will worship God on this mountain."
reason: The καί before λατρεύσετε simply introduces the main clause after ἐν τῷ ἐξαγαγεῖν; it does not mean 'also'.

old: And the scribes of the sons of Israel saw themselves in trouble, as it was said, "You shall not fall short of the daily requirement of brickmaking."
new: And the scribes of the sons of Israel saw themselves in trouble, saying, "You shall not fall short of the daily requirement of brickmaking."
reason: λέγοντες is a nominative participle agreeing with οἱ γραμματεῖς ('saying'); 'as it was said' replaces it with an impersonal passive not in the Greek.

old: Chapter 8 verse numbering follows the Septuagint, where 8:1 corresponds to 8:5 in the Hebrew Masoretic Text (the preceding four verses close chapter 7).
new: Chapter 8 verse numbering follows the Greek and Hebrew numbering, in which 8:1 corresponds to 8:5 in most English versions (the preceding four verses close chapter 7).
reason: The Masoretic Text also numbers this verse 8:1 (as the note at 7:26 says); the four-verse offset is against common English versification, not against the Hebrew.

old: Therefore forgive my sin just this once more, and pray to the Lord your God, and let Him remove this death from me."
new: Therefore accept my sin now once more, and pray to the Lord your God, and let Him remove this death from me."
reason: προσδέξασθε is 'accept/receive' (cf. δέξαι 'accept' in Gen 50:17) and ἔτι νῦν is 'now once more/yet now'; 'forgive ... just this once' follows the Hebrew.

old: And Moses said, "Rather, you yourself will also give us burnt offerings and sacrifices that we will offer to the Lord our God,
new: And Moses said, "Rather, you yourself will also give us whole burnt offerings and sacrifices that we will offer to the Lord our God,
reason: ὁλοκαυτώματα is "whole burnt offerings" elsewhere in Exodus (18:12, 20:24, 24:5, 32:6).

old: and our livestock will go with us, and we will not leave behind a hoof; for from them we will take to serve the Lord our God, and we do not know with what we are to serve the Lord our God until we arrive there."
new: and our livestock will go with us, and we will not leave behind a hoof; for from them we will take to serve the Lord our God, but we do not know with what we are to serve the Lord our God until we arrive there."
reason: ἡμεῖς δὲ οὐκ οἴδαμεν is contrastive (they will take animals, but do not yet know which); the adversative δέ was flattened to "and."

old: and every firstborn in the land of Egypt will die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sits on the throne even to the firstborn of the maidservant who is beside the mill, and even to the firstborn of every animal;
new: and every firstborn in the land of Egypt will die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sits on the throne even to the firstborn of the maidservant who is beside the mill, and even to the firstborn of all livestock;
reason: παντὸς κτήνους is "all livestock" in the parallel 12:29, and κτῆνος is "livestock" throughout these chapters.

old: And among all the sons of Israel not a dog will snarl with its tongue, not from man to animal, so that you may see how wondrously the Lord makes a distinction between the Egyptians and Israel.'
new: And among all the sons of Israel not a dog will snarl with its tongue, not from man to livestock, so that you may see how wondrously the Lord makes a distinction between the Egyptians and Israel.'
reason: ἀπὸ ἀνθρώπου ἕως κτήνους is "from man to livestock" in 12:12 and 13:2.

old: And they shall take some of the blood and put it on the two doorposts and on the lintel, on the houses in which they eat them.
new: And they shall take some of the blood and put it on the two doorposts and on the lintel, in the houses in which they eat them.
reason: ἐν τοῖς οἴκοις is "in the houses"; "on" is not in the Greek.

old: You shall not leave any of it until morning, and you shall not break a bone of it; and what remains of it until morning you shall burn with fire.
new: None of it shall be left until morning, and a bone of it shall not be broken; and what remains of it until morning you shall burn with fire.
reason: This Greek has third-person ἀπολείψεται and συντρίψεται ("shall be left," "shall be broken"); "you shall not leave/break" follows the second-person -ετε reading of other editions instead of this text.

old: The clause "and you shall not break a bone of it" appears here in the Septuagint in addition to 12:46 (absent from the Masoretic Text in v. 10). The Greek spelling of the first two verbs (-εται) is an orthographic variant for the second-person plural future (-ετε), matching the third verb and 12:46.
new: The clause "and a bone of it shall not be broken" appears here in the Septuagint in addition to 12:46 (absent from the Masoretic Text in v. 10). The first two verbs here are third-person forms (ἀπολείψεται, συντρίψεται); other editions read second-person plural forms (-ετε), matching the third verb and 12:46.
reason: Note rewritten to match the verse now translating the Greek as it stands rather than treating -εται as a spelling of -ετε.

old: And I will go through the land of Egypt on this night, and I will strike every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from man to livestock, and against all the gods of the Egyptians I will execute vengeance; I am the Lord.
new: And I will come into the land of Egypt on this night, and I will strike every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from man to livestock, and against all the gods of the Egyptians I will execute vengeance; I am the Lord.
reason: This Greek reads ἐλεύσομαι ("I will come"), not διελεύσομαι; "go through" reflects the Hebrew "pass through."

old: And this day shall be to you a memorial, and you shall celebrate it as a feast to the Lord throughout all your generations; as a perpetual statute you shall celebrate it.
new: And this day shall be to you a memorial, and you shall celebrate it as a feast to the Lord throughout all your generations; as an eternal statute you shall celebrate it.
reason: νόμιμον αἰώνιον is "eternal statute" everywhere else in the edition (23 occurrences).

old: And you shall keep this commandment, for on this day I will bring out your host from the land of Egypt; and you shall observe this day throughout your generations as a perpetual statute.
new: And you shall keep this commandment, for on this day I will bring out your host from the land of Egypt; and you shall observe this day throughout your generations as an eternal statute.
reason: νόμιμον αἰώνιον is "eternal statute" everywhere else in the edition (23 occurrences).

old: And if any proselyte comes to you to observe the Passover to the Lord, you shall circumcise every male belonging to him; and then he shall come near to observe it, and he shall be just like the native of the land. No uncircumcised person shall eat of it.
new: And if any resident alien comes to you to observe the Passover to the Lord, you shall circumcise every male belonging to him; and then he shall come near to observe it, and he shall be just like the native of the land. No uncircumcised person shall eat of it.
reason: προσήλυτος is "resident alien" in 20:10, 22:20, 23:9, 23:12 and throughout the law books.

old: There shall be one law for the native-born and for the proselyte who has come among you."
new: There shall be one law for the native-born and for the resident alien who has come among you."
reason: προσήλυτος is "resident alien" in 20:10, 22:20, 23:9, 23:12 and throughout the law books.

old: The Septuagint renders the altar's name "The Lord is my refuge" (Kyrios kataphyge mou), differing from the Hebrew MT "Yahweh-Nissi" ("The Lord is my banner").
new: The Septuagint renders the altar's name "The Lord is my refuge" (Kyrios kataphyge mou), differing from the Hebrew MT name meaning "The Lord is my banner."
reason: House style never uses "Yahweh"; the Hebrew name is described by its meaning instead.

old: And now if you truly listen to My voice and keep My covenant, you shall be to Me a treasured people from among all the nations; for all the earth is Mine,
new: And now if you carefully listen to My voice and keep My covenant, you shall be to Me a treasured people from among all the nations; for all the earth is Mine,
reason: ἀκοῇ ἀκούσητε (cognate dative) is "carefully listen" in 15:26; "truly" is an intensifier not matching the edition's rendering.

old: The Greek apallaxe ap' auton most naturally means "depart from them" (though some render it "remove some of them"), differing from the Hebrew MT "break out against them."
new: The Greek apallaxe ap' auton is taken as "depart from them" (the verb can also mean "remove [some] of them"), differing from the Hebrew MT "break out against them."
reason: Removed the claim about what others render; kept the lexical alternative.

old: In the Septuagint, verses 13–15 order the prohibitions as adultery, theft, and murder, differing from the Masoretic Text order (murder, adultery, theft) and matching citations in Luke 18:20 and Romans 13:9.
new: In the Septuagint, verses 13–15 order the prohibitions as adultery, theft, and murder, differing from the Masoretic Text order (murder, adultery, theft).
reason: Luke 18:20 and Romans 13:9 both read adultery, murder, theft, so the claimed match with this order (adultery, theft, murder) is false; removed.

old: You will make an altar of earth for Me, and you will sacrifice upon it your whole burnt offerings and your deliverance offerings, your sheep and your calves, in every place where I name My name; and I will come to you and bless you.
new: You will make an altar of earth for Me, and you will sacrifice upon it your whole burnt offerings and your deliverance offerings and your sheep and your calves, in every place where I name My name; and I will come to you and bless you.
reason: καὶ τὰ πρόβατα καὶ τοὺς μόσχους ὑμῶν is joined by καί as further items, not set in apposition to the offerings.

old: The Greek converts the Hebrew weight unit into thirty didrachmas of silver; note also that verse 37 of this chapter corresponds to Exodus 22:1 in the Masoretic Text.
new: The Greek converts the Hebrew weight unit into thirty didrachmas of silver.
reason: The Masoretic Text itself numbers this law 21:37 (22:1 is an English versification), so the claim that 21:37 corresponds to MT 22:1 is false; removed.

old: The Greek renders Hebrew Elohim as plural "gods" (θεούς), a well-known Septuagint reading that prohibits reviling deities in general alongside rulers.
new: The Greek has the plural "gods" (θεούς) for Hebrew Elohim.
reason: Removed the evaluative "well-known" and the interpretive gloss on what the law prohibits; kept the textual fact.

old: From every unjust matter you shall stay away; the innocent and the righteous you shall not kill, and you shall not acquit the ungodly for the sake of gifts.
new: From every unjust matter you shall stay away; the innocent and the righteous you shall not kill, and you shall not justify the ungodly for the sake of gifts.
reason: δικαιώσεις is from δικαιόω, rendered "justify" in this edition (cf. Gen 44:16); the legal sense is kept by "justify the ungodly."

old: If you truly listen to My voice, and do all things that I command you, and keep My covenant, you shall be to Me a treasured people above all the nations; for all the earth is Mine, and you shall be to Me a royal priesthood and a holy nation. These words you shall speak to the sons of Israel. If you truly listen to My voice, and do all things that I say to you, I will be an enemy to your enemies and oppose those who oppose you.
new: If you carefully listen to My voice, and do all things that I command you, and keep My covenant, you shall be to Me a treasured people from among all the nations; for all the earth is Mine, and you shall be to Me a royal priesthood and a holy nation. These words you shall speak to the sons of Israel. If you carefully listen to My voice, and do all things that I say to you, I will be an enemy to your enemies and oppose those who oppose you.
reason: ἀκοῇ ἀκούσητε is "carefully listen" (15:26), and λαὸς περιούσιος ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν ἐθνῶν is "from among all the nations" in the parallel 19:5; ἀπό does not mean "above."

old: The Greek reads "they saw the place where the God of Israel stood" rather than the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "they saw the God of Israel," avoiding a direct visual depiction of God.
new: The Greek reads "they saw the place where the God of Israel stood" rather than the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "they saw the God of Israel."
reason: The added motive ("avoiding a direct visual depiction of God") is interpretation, not a fact about the Greek; removed.

old: And you shall make a mercy seat of pure gold, two and a half cubits in length, and a cubit and a half in width.
new: And you shall make a mercy seat, a cover of pure gold, two and a half cubits in length, and a cubit and a half in width.
reason: ἱλαστήριον ἐπίθεμα has two nouns; ἐπίθεμα ("cover, lid") was not represented.

old: "Mercy seat" translates Greek hilastērion epithema (literally "propitiatory cover"), shortened to hilastērion in verses 18–22 and rendered consistently as "mercy seat" across Exodus, Leviticus, and Numbers.
new: "A mercy seat, a cover" renders Greek hilastērion epithema (literally "a propitiatory cover"); verses 18–22 use hilastērion alone.
reason: Updated to match the verse, and removed the claim about the edition's renderings in other books.

old: And there shall be eight pillars, and their bases shall be sixteen silver ones: two bases for the one pillar for both of its sides, and two bases for the other pillar.
new: And there shall be eight pillars, and their bases shall be sixteen silver ones: two bases for the one pillar for both of its sides, and two bases for the one pillar.
reason: καὶ δύο βάσεις τῷ στύλῳ τῷ ἑνί repeats "the one pillar" (distributive, as in vv. 19, 21); "the other" is not in the Greek and implies only two pillars.

old: And you shall make a veil of blue and purple and twisted scarlet and spun fine linen; you shall make it a woven work with cherubim.
new: And you shall make a curtain of blue and purple and twisted scarlet and spun fine linen; you shall make it a woven work with cherubim.
reason: καταπέτασμα is rendered "curtain" in this edition (as in the NT and Leviticus); "veil" here is inconsistent with 35:12, 38:18, 39:4, 39:20.

old: And you shall place the veil upon the pillars, and you shall bring in there, inside the veil, the ark of the testimony; and the veil shall separate for you between the holy place and the Holy of Holies.
new: And you shall place the curtain upon the pillars, and you shall bring in there, inside the curtain, the ark of the testimony; and the curtain shall separate for you between the holy place and the Holy of Holies.
reason: καταπέτασμα is rendered "curtain" in this edition (as in the NT and Leviticus); "veil" here is inconsistent with 35:12, 38:18, 39:4, 39:20.

old: And you shall cover the ark of the testimony with the veil in the Holy of Holies.
new: And you shall cover the ark of the testimony with the curtain in the Holy of Holies.
reason: καταπέτασμα is rendered "curtain" in this edition (as in the NT and Leviticus); "veil" here is inconsistent with 35:12, 38:18, 39:4, 39:20.

old: The Greek instructs covering the ark of the testimony with the veil (κατακαλύψεις τῷ καταπετάσματι), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text instructs placing the mercy seat upon the ark.
new: The Greek instructs covering the ark of the testimony with the curtain (κατακαλύψεις τῷ καταπετάσματι), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text instructs placing the mercy seat upon the ark.
reason: Keep the note's wording in line with the verse (καταπέτασμα → "curtain").

old: And you shall place the table outside the veil, and the lampstand opposite the table on the side of the tabernacle toward the south; and the table you shall put on the side of the tabernacle toward the north.
new: And you shall place the table outside the curtain, and the lampstand opposite the table on the side of the tabernacle toward the south; and the table you shall put on the side of the tabernacle toward the north.
reason: καταπέτασμα is rendered "curtain" in this edition (as in the NT and Leviticus); "veil" here is inconsistent with 35:12, 38:18, 39:4, 39:20.

old: And you shall make five pillars for the veil, and you shall overlay them with gold; and their capitals shall be of gold; and you shall cast five bronze bases for them.
new: And you shall make five pillars for the curtain, and you shall overlay them with gold; and their capitals shall be of gold; and you shall cast five bronze bases for them.
reason: καταπέτασμα is rendered "curtain" in this edition (as in the NT and Leviticus); "veil" here is inconsistent with 35:12, 38:18, 39:4, 39:20.

old: in the tabernacle of the testimony, outside the veil that is over the covenant; Aaron and his sons shall burn it from evening until morning before the Lord. It shall be a perpetual statute for your generations from the sons of Israel.
new: in the tent of the testimony, outside the curtain that is over the covenant; Aaron and his sons shall burn it from evening until morning before the Lord. It shall be an eternal statute for your generations from the sons of Israel.
reason: σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου is "tent of (the) testimony" elsewhere (28:43; 29:4ff.); καταπέτασμα is "curtain"; νόμιμον αἰώνιον is "eternal statute" in 28:43, 29:28, 30:21 (αἰώνιος → "eternal").

old: in the tent of the testimony, outside the curtain that is over the covenant; Aaron and his sons shall burn it from evening until morning before the Lord. It shall be an eternal statute for your generations from the sons of Israel.
new: in the tent of testimony, outside the curtain that is over the covenant; Aaron and his sons shall burn it from evening until morning before the Lord. It shall be an eternal statute for your generations from the sons of Israel.
reason: σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου → "tent of testimony" (Pentateuch-wide)

old: And these are the garments which they shall make: the breastpiece and the shoulder-garment and the full-length tasseled tunic and a turban and a sash. And they shall make holy garments for Aaron and for his sons to serve as priests to Me.
new: And these are the garments which they shall make: the breastpiece and the shoulder-garment and the full-length tasseled tunic and a headdress and a sash. And they shall make holy garments for Aaron and for his sons to serve as priests to Me.
reason: κίδαρις and μίτρα are different Greek words that this book merges as "turban"; κίδαρις → "headdress" (as in 36:35 and Lev 8:13) keeps "turban" for μίτρα (29:6; 36:35, 38).

old: And you shall place it upon twisted blue, and it shall be upon the miter; on the front of the miter it shall be.
new: And you shall place it upon twisted blue, and it shall be upon the turban; on the front of the turban it shall be.
reason: μίτρα is "turban" in 29:6, 36:35, 36:38 (and Lev 8:9), the same headpiece the plate is set on; "miter" here is inconsistent.

old: And the tasseled parts of the tunics shall be of fine linen; and you shall make a turban of fine linen, and you shall make a sash, the work of an embroiderer.
new: And the tasseled parts of the tunics shall be of fine linen; and you shall make a headdress of fine linen, and you shall make a sash, the work of an embroiderer.
reason: κίδαριν, not μίτραν: κίδαρις → "headdress" (36:35) to distinguish it from μίτρα "turban".

old: And for the sons of Aaron you shall make tunics and sashes, and turbans you shall make for them, for honor and glory.
new: And for the sons of Aaron you shall make tunics and sashes, and headdresses you shall make for them, for honor and glory.
reason: κιδάρεις → "headdresses" (as in 36:35 and Lev 8:13), distinct from μίτρα "turban".

old: And Aaron and his sons shall wear them whenever they enter into the tent of the testimony, when they approach to minister at the altar of the sanctuary; and they shall not bring sin upon themselves, so that they may not die; an eternal statute for him and for his seed after him.
new: And Aaron and his sons shall wear them whenever they enter into the tent of testimony, when they approach to minister at the altar of the sanctuary; and they shall not bring sin upon themselves, so that they may not die; an eternal statute for him and for his seed after him.
reason: σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου → "tent of testimony" (Pentateuch-wide)

old: And you shall bring Aaron and his sons to the doors of the tent of the testimony, and you shall wash them with water.
new: And you shall bring Aaron and his sons to the doors of the tent of testimony, and you shall wash them with water.
reason: σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου → "tent of testimony" (Pentateuch-wide)

old: And taking the robes, you shall clothe Aaron your brother with the full-length tunic and the shoulder garment and the oracle piece against the shoulder garment.
new: And taking the robes, you shall clothe Aaron your brother with the full-length tunic and the shoulder-garment and the oracle against the shoulder-garment.
reason: ἐπωμίς is "shoulder-garment" and λόγιον is "oracle" in ch. 28 and 35-36; "oracle piece" adds a word.

old: Greek ἐπωμίδα ("shoulder garment") and λόγιον ("oracle piece") are the Septuagint terms corresponding to the Hebrew ephod and breastpiece; the Greek text here also omits the mention of Aaron's sash found in the Masoretic Text.
new: Greek ἐπωμίδα ("shoulder-garment") and λόγιον ("oracle") are the Septuagint terms corresponding to the Hebrew ephod and breastpiece; the Greek text here also lacks the Masoretic Text's clause about girding Aaron with the woven band of the ephod.
reason: Note's terms updated to match the verse; the MT element missing here is the girding with the ephod's woven band (ḥēšeb), not Aaron's sash.

old: And you shall bind them with the sashes, and you shall put the caps on them; and the priesthood to Me shall be theirs forever. And you shall consecrate the hands of Aaron and the hands of his sons.
new: And you shall bind them with the sashes, and you shall put the headdresses on them; and the priesthood to Me shall be theirs forever. And you shall consecrate the hands of Aaron and the hands of his sons.
reason: τὰς κιδάρεις is "turbans/headdresses" elsewhere (28:40; 36:35), not "caps"; κίδαρις → "headdress".

old: And you shall bring the calf to the doors of the tent of the testimony, and Aaron and his sons shall place their hands on the head of the calf before the Lord beside the doors of the tent of the testimony.
new: And you shall bring the calf to the doors of the tent of testimony, and Aaron and his sons shall place their hands on the head of the calf before the Lord beside the doors of the tent of testimony.
reason: σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου → "tent of testimony" (Pentateuch-wide)

old: And you shall slaughter the calf before the Lord beside the doors of the tent of the testimony.
new: And you shall slaughter the calf before the Lord beside the doors of the tent of testimony.
reason: σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου → "tent of testimony" (Pentateuch-wide)

old: And you shall take them from their hands, and you shall offer them up on the altar of the whole burnt offering for a fragrant aroma before the Lord; it is a sacrificial offering to the Lord.
new: And you shall take them from their hands, and you shall offer them up on the altar of the whole burnt offering for a fragrant aroma before the Lord; it is a fire offering to the Lord.
reason: κάρπωμα → "fire offering" (Pentateuch-wide)

old: For seven days the priest among his sons who is in his place shall put them on, who will enter into the tent of the testimony to minister in the holy places.
new: For seven days the priest among his sons who is in his place shall put them on, who will enter into the tent of testimony to minister in the holy places.
reason: σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου → "tent of testimony" (Pentateuch-wide)

old: And Aaron and his sons shall eat the flesh of the ram and the loaves that are in the basket beside the doors of the tent of the testimony.
new: And Aaron and his sons shall eat the flesh of the ram and the loaves that are in the basket beside the doors of the tent of testimony.
reason: σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου → "tent of testimony" (Pentateuch-wide)

old: And these are the things that you shall offer on the altar: two unblemished year-old lambs each day on the altar continually, a continual sacrificial offering.
new: And these are the things that you shall offer on the altar: two unblemished year-old lambs each day on the altar continually, a continual fire offering.
reason: κάρπωμα → "fire offering" (Pentateuch-wide)

old: And the second lamb you shall offer in the evening; according to the morning sacrifice and according to its drink offering you shall offer it, as a fragrant aroma, a sacrificial offering to the Lord,
new: And the second lamb you shall offer in the evening; according to the morning sacrifice and according to its drink offering you shall offer it, as a fragrant aroma, a fire offering to the Lord,
reason: κάρπωμα → "fire offering" (Pentateuch-wide)

old: a continual sacrifice throughout your generations, at the doors of the tent of the testimony before the Lord, by which I will be made known to you from there, so as to speak to you.
new: a continual sacrifice throughout your generations, at the doors of the tent of the testimony before the Lord, in which I will be made known to you from there, so as to speak to you.
reason: ἐν οἷς is "in which" (as the identical phrase in 30:6); "by which" makes the sacrifice the means, an interpretation.

old: a continual sacrifice throughout your generations, at the doors of the tent of the testimony before the Lord, in which I will be made known to you from there, so as to speak to you.
new: a continual sacrifice throughout your generations, at the doors of the tent of testimony before the Lord, in which I will be made known to you from there, so as to speak to you.
reason: σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου → "tent of testimony" (Pentateuch-wide)

old: And I will sanctify the tent of the testimony and the altar, and I will sanctify Aaron and his sons to serve as priests to Me.
new: And I will sanctify the tent of testimony and the altar, and I will sanctify Aaron and his sons to serve as priests to Me.
reason: σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου → "tent of testimony" (Pentateuch-wide)

old: And you shall place it in front of the veil that is over the ark of the testimonies, in which I will make Myself known to you from there.
new: And you shall place it in front of the curtain that is over the ark of the testimonies, in which I will make Myself known to you from there.
reason: καταπέτασμα is rendered "curtain" in this edition (as in the NT and Leviticus); "veil" here is inconsistent with 35:12, 38:18, 39:4, 39:20.

old: And he shall not offer up on it other incense, an offering by fire, or a sacrifice; you shall not pour out a drink offering on it.
new: And he shall not offer up on it other incense, a sacrificial offering, or a sacrifice; you shall not pour out a drink offering on it.
reason: κάρπωμα is "sacrificial offering" in 29:25, 38, 41; "offering by fire" is inconsistent.

old: And he shall not offer up on it other incense, a sacrificial offering, or a sacrifice; you shall not pour out a drink offering on it.

old: And he shall remove a handful from it, from the fine flour of the sacrifice with its oil and with its frankincense, the things that are on the sacrifice, and he shall offer it up on the altar as an offering, a fragrant aroma, its memorial to the Lord.

old: It shall not be baked leavened; I have given it to them as a portion from the offerings of the Lord; it is most holy, just like the sin offering and just like the trespass offering.

old: Every male among the priests shall eat it; it is an eternal statute for your generations from the offerings of the Lord. Everyone who touches them shall become holy.'"
new: Every male among the priests shall eat it; it is an eternal statute for your generations from the fire offerings of the Lord. Everyone who touches them shall become holy.'"

old: And every sacrifice that is prepared in the oven, and every one that is prepared on a grill or on a griddle, belongs to the priest who offers it; it shall be his.
new: And every sacrifice that is prepared in the oven, and every one that is prepared on a hearth or on a griddle, belongs to the priest who offers it; it shall be his.

old: If he offers it for praise, then he shall offer with the sacrifice of praise loaves of fine flour mixed with oil, unleavened wafers spread with oil, and fine flour kneaded with oil;
new: If he offers it for praise, then he shall offer with the sacrifice of praise loaves of fine flour mixed with oil, unleavened flat cakes spread with oil, and fine flour kneaded with oil;

old: as for everyone who eats fat from the livestock from which one presents an offering of the Lord, that soul shall be destroyed from its people.
new: as for everyone who eats fat from the livestock from which one presents a fire offering of the Lord, that soul shall be destroyed from its people.

old: his own hands shall offer the offerings to the Lord: the fat that is on the breast and the lobe of the liver, he shall offer them so as to place them as a gift before the Lord.
new: his hands shall offer the fire offerings to the Lord: the fat that is on the breast and the lobe of the liver, he shall offer them so as to place them as a gift before the Lord.

old: This is the anointing of Aaron and the anointing of his sons from the offerings of the Lord, on the day when He brought them near to serve as priests to the Lord,
new: This is the anointing of Aaron and the anointing of his sons from the fire offerings of the Lord, on the day when He brought them near to serve as priests to the Lord,

old: And he clothed them with the tunic and fastened the sash around them; and he clothed him with the robe and placed the shoulder-piece upon him,

old: and he wrapped him according to the workmanship of the shoulder-piece and fastened him tightly with it; and he placed the oracle upon it, and placed the manifestation and the truth upon the oracle.

old: And he washed the belly and the feet with water, and Moses offered up the whole ram on the altar; a whole burnt offering that is for a fragrance of sweet aroma, it is a sacrificial offering to the Lord, just as the Lord commanded Moses.
new: And he washed the belly and the feet with water, and Moses offered up the whole ram on the altar; a whole burnt offering that is for an aroma of sweet fragrance, it is a fire offering to the Lord, just as the Lord commanded Moses.

old: And from the basket of consecration that was before the Lord he took one unleavened loaf, and one loaf made with oil, and one flat cake, and he placed them on the fat, and he placed the right shoulder on top.
new: And from the basket of consecration that was before the Lord he took one unleavened loaf, and one loaf made with oil, and one flat cake, and he placed them on the fat, and he placed the right shoulder.

old: And Moses took them from their hands, and Moses offered them up on the altar, upon the whole burnt offering of consecration, which is a fragrance of sweet aroma; it is a sacrificial offering to the Lord.

old: This verse in the Saints Greek Critical Text repeats only the closing phrase of verse 29 ('and the garments of his sons with him'); like the Septuagint generally, it lacks the closing sanctification clause found in the Hebrew text.

old: and speak to the council of elders of Israel, saying, 'Take one male goat from the goats for a sin offering, and a calf and a year-old lamb for a whole offering, without blemish,
new: and speak to the council of elders of Israel, saying, 'Take one male goat from the goats for a sin offering, and a calf and a year-old lamb for a whole fire offering, without blemish,

old: and a young bull and a ram for a sacrifice of deliverance before the Lord, and fine flour mixed with oil; for today the Lord will appear among you.'"
new: and a young bull and a ram for a sacrifice of deliverance before the Lord, and fine flour kneaded with oil; for today the Lord will appear among you.'"

old: And Moses said to Aaron and to Eleazar and Ithamar, the sons of Aaron who were left, "Take the offering that was left from the offerings by fire of the Lord, and eat it unleavened beside the altar; it is most holy.
new: And Moses said to Aaron and to Eleazar and Ithamar, the sons of Aaron who were left, "Take the sacrifice that was left from the fire offerings of the Lord, and eat it unleavened beside the altar; it is most holy.

old: And you shall eat it in a holy place, for this is an eternal ordinance for you and an ordinance for your sons from the offerings by fire of the Lord; for so it has been commanded to me.

old: The shoulder of the contribution and the breast of the separated offering they shall bring along with the offerings by fire of the fat portions, to set apart as a separated offering before the Lord; and it shall be for you and for your sons and for your daughters with you an eternal ordinance, just as the Lord commanded Moses."
new: The shoulder of the contribution and the breast of the separated offering they shall bring along with the fire offerings of the fat portions, to set apart as a separated offering before the Lord; and it shall be for you and for your sons and for your daughters with you an eternal ordinance, just as the Lord commanded Moses."
reason: τῶν καρπωμάτων is 'fire offerings' throughout the book.

old: Greek makes the priest the explicit active subject of καθαριεῖ αὐτήν ("he shall cleanse her"), whereas the Hebrew text reads "and she shall be clean."
new: Greek καθαριεῖ αὐτήν ("he shall cleanse her") is active, with the priest as its implied subject, whereas the Hebrew text reads "and she shall be clean."
reason: The subject of καθαριεῖ is not explicit in the Greek; it is carried over from ὁ ἱερεύς in the previous clause.

old: "If a bright scar of a mark occurs on any person in the skin of his flesh, and it becomes an affliction of leprosy in the skin of his flesh, then he shall be brought to Aaron the priest or one of his sons, the priests.
new: "If a bright scar of a mark occurs on any person in the skin of his flesh, and an affliction of leprosy occurs in the skin of his flesh, then he shall be brought to Aaron the priest or one of his sons, the priests.
reason: In καὶ γένηται ἐν δέρματι χρωτὸς αὐτοῦ ἁφὴ λέπρας the subject is ἁφὴ λέπρας ('an affliction of leprosy occurs'); 'it becomes' follows the Hebrew construction.

old: and the priest shall go outside the camp, and the priest shall look, and indeed, the plague of leprosy is healed from the leper.
new: and the priest shall go outside the camp, and the priest shall see, and look, the affliction of leprosy is healed from the leper.
reason: ὄψεται... καὶ ἰδού is 'shall see, and look' throughout ch. 13 ('indeed' is not a rendering of ἰδού); ἁφή is 'affliction' throughout ch. 13 (ἁφὴ λέπρας 'affliction of leprosy').

old: And on the eighth day he shall take two unblemished year-old lambs, and an unblemished year-old sheep, and three tenths of fine flour for a sacrifice, mixed with oil, and one cup of oil;
new: And on the eighth day he shall take two unblemished year-old lambs, and an unblemished year-old sheep, and three tenths of fine flour for a sacrifice, kneaded with oil, and one cup of oil;
reason: πεφυραμένης ἐν ἐλαίῳ is 'kneaded with oil' in 2:4-5, 6:14, 7:12, where 'mixed' renders the different verb ἀναπεποιημένη.

old: And the priest shall take the one lamb, and he shall bring it for the trespass offering, and the cup of oil, and he shall set it apart as a set-apart offering before the Lord.
new: And the priest shall take the one lamb, and he shall bring it for the trespass offering, and the cup of oil, and he shall set it apart as a separated offering before the Lord.
reason: ἀφόρισμα is 'separated offering' in 10:14-15, while 'set-apart offering' is this edition's rendering of the different term ἀφαίρεμα (8:26, 9:21).

old: But if his hand is poor and does not find enough, he shall take one lamb for that in which he trespassed as a set-aside offering, so as to make atonement for him, and a tenth of fine flour mixed with oil for a sacrifice, and one cup of oil,
new: But if his hand is poor and does not find enough, he shall take one lamb for that in which he incurred guilt as a set-apart portion, so as to make atonement for him, and a tenth of fine flour kneaded with oil for a sacrifice, and one cup of oil,
reason: εἰς ὃ ἐπλημμέλησεν is 'for that in which he incurred guilt' in 5:15, 5:25; ἀφαίρεμα is 'set-apart portion' in 7:14, 7:32, 7:34; πεφυραμένης is 'kneaded' elsewhere.

old: This is the law of the one in whom is the plague of leprosy and of the one who does not find with his hand for his cleansing."
new: This is the law of the one in whom is the affliction of leprosy and of the one who does not find with his hand for his cleansing."
reason: ἁφὴ λέπρας is 'affliction of leprosy' throughout ch. 13.

old: "When you enter into the land of the Canaanites, which I give to you as a possession, and I put a plague of leprosy in the houses of the land possessed by you,
new: "When you enter into the land of the Canaanites, which I give to you as a possession, and I put an affliction of leprosy in the houses of the land possessed by you,
reason: ἁφὴ λέπρας is 'affliction of leprosy' throughout ch. 13, including garments (13:47-59).

old: then the one whose house it is shall come and report to the priest, saying, 'Something like a plague has appeared in my house.'
new: then the one whose house it is shall come and report to the priest, saying, 'Something like an affliction has appeared in my house.'
reason: ἁφή is 'affliction' throughout ch. 13, including garments (13:47-59).

old: And he shall look at the plague in the walls of the house, greenish depressions, and their appearance is lower than the walls;
new: And he shall look at the affliction in the walls of the house, greenish depressions, and their appearance is lower than the walls;
reason: ἁφή is 'affliction' throughout ch. 13.

old: And the priest shall return on the seventh day and look at the house, and see, the plague has not spread in the walls of the house;
new: And the priest shall return on the seventh day and look at the house, and see, the affliction has not spread in the walls of the house;
reason: ἁφή is 'affliction' throughout ch. 13.

old: and the priest shall command, and they shall remove the stones; there is the plague; and they shall throw them outside the city into an unclean place.
new: and the priest shall command, and they shall remove the stones; there is the affliction; and they shall throw them outside the city into an unclean place.
reason: ἁφή is 'affliction' throughout ch. 13.

old: This Greek text reads τοὺς λίθους· ἔστιν ἡ ἁφή· ("the stones; there is the plague;"), omitting the relative pronoun ἐν οἷς ("in which") found in other Greek witnesses and the Hebrew text.
new: This Greek text reads τοὺς λίθους· ἔστιν ἡ ἁφή· ("the stones; there is the affliction;"), omitting the relative pronoun ἐν οἷς ("in which") found in other Greek witnesses and the Hebrew text.
reason: Keeps the note's quotation in step with the verse's rendering of ἁφή.

old: But if a plague comes again and springs up in the house after removing the stones and after the house has been scraped and after it has been plastered,
new: But if an affliction comes again and springs up in the house after removing the stones and after the house has been scraped and after it has been plastered,
reason: ἁφή is 'affliction' throughout ch. 13.

old: then the priest shall enter and look: if the plague has spread in the house, it is a persistent leprosy in the house; it is unclean.
new: then the priest shall enter and look: if the affliction has spread in the house, it is a persistent leprosy in the house; it is unclean.
reason: ἁφή is 'affliction' throughout ch. 13 (cf. λέπρα ἔμμονος with ἁφή in 13:51).

old: But if the priest comes and enters and looks, and see, the plague is not spreading at all in the house after the house has been plastered, then the priest shall cleanse the house, because the plague has been healed.
new: But if the priest comes and enters and looks, and see, the affliction is not spreading at all in the house after the house has been plastered, then the priest shall cleanse the house, because the affliction has been healed.
reason: ἁφή is 'affliction' throughout ch. 13.

old: This is the law concerning every plague of leprosy and scab,
new: This is the law concerning every affliction of leprosy and scab,
reason: ἁφὴ λέπρας is 'affliction of leprosy' throughout ch. 13 (and in the parallel summary 13:59).

old: And this shall be a perpetual statute for you: in the seventh month, humble your souls and you shall not do any work, the native and the proselyte who is joined among you.
new: And this shall be an eternal statute for you: in the seventh month, humble your souls and you shall not do any work, the native and the resident alien who is settled among you.
reason: νόμιμον αἰώνιον is "eternal statute" elsewhere in Leviticus (17:7; 23:14, 21, 31, 41), and ὁ προσήλυτος ὁ προσκείμενος ἐν ὑμῖν is rendered "the resident alien who is settled among you" in 17:12.

old: Following the Codex Vaticanus tradition, the Greek text omits "on the tenth day of the month" after "in the seventh month" and uses an aorist imperative ("humble your souls") rather than a future verb; it also renders the resident alien as proselutos ho proskeimenos ("the proselyte who is joined").
new: The Greek text lacks "on the tenth day of the month" (present in the Hebrew Masoretic Text) after "in the seventh month" and uses an aorist imperative ("humble your souls") rather than a future verb.
reason: The manuscript attribution is unsupported by the input, and the remark on "proselyte" no longer matches the verse after the consistency change.

old: This shall be a Sabbath of Sabbaths, a rest for you, and you shall humble your souls; it is a perpetual statute.
new: This shall be a Sabbath of Sabbaths, a rest for you, and you shall humble your souls; it is an eternal statute.
reason: νόμιμον αἰώνιον is rendered "eternal statute" throughout the rest of Leviticus (αἰώνιος → "eternal").

old: And this shall be a perpetual statute for you, to make atonement for the sons of Israel from all their sins." Once a year it shall be done, just as the Lord commanded Moses.

old: And you shall not give any of your offspring to serve a ruler, and you shall not profane the holy name; I am the Lord.

old: And you shall keep My ordinances, so that you may not do any of all the abominable statutes that has been done before you, and you shall not be defiled by them; for I am the Lord your God.'"
new: And you shall keep My ordinances, so that you may not do any of all the abominable statutes that have been done before you, and you shall not be defiled by them; for I am the Lord your God.'"

old: "Speak to the assembly of the sons of Israel, and you shall say to them, 'You shall be holy, because I am holy, the Lord your God.
new: "Speak to the congregation of the sons of Israel, and you shall say to them, 'You shall be holy, because I am holy, the Lord your God.

old: The Greek reads "upon the mountains" (ἐπὶ τῶν ὀρέων), reflecting a different vocalization of the Hebrew consonants than the Masoretic Text's "with the blood."
new: The Greek reads "upon the mountains" (ἐπὶ τῶν ὀρέων), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "with the blood."
reason: The two readings differ in their consonants, not only in vocalization; the speculative explanation is inaccurate and is removed.

old: And I will set My face against that man and I will destroy him from his people, because he gave of his offspring to a ruler, so as to defile My holy places and profane the name of those consecrated to Me.

reason: The Greek word is μόνορχις, transliterated monorchis, not "monarchis".

old: no one from the offspring of Aaron the priest who has a blemish in him shall come near to offer the sacrifices to your God; because a blemish is in him, he shall not approach to offer the gifts of God.

old: however, he shall not approach the veil, and he shall not come near to the altar, because he has a blemish; and he shall not profane the sanctuary of his God, because I am the Lord who sanctifies them.'"
new: however, he shall not approach the curtain, and he shall not come near to the altar, because he has a blemish; and he shall not profane the sanctuary of his God, because I am the Lord who sanctifies them.'"

old: Tell them, 'Throughout your generations, any man from your offspring who approaches the holy things, whatever the sons of Israel sanctify to the Lord, while his uncleanness is upon him, that person shall be utterly destroyed from Me; I am the Lord your God.

old: And if a daughter of a priest becomes a widow cast out, and she had no offspring, she shall return to her paternal house as in her youth; she may eat from the loaves of her father. And no outsider shall eat from them.

old: and bring upon themselves iniquity of trespass when they eat their holy things; because I am the Lord who sanctifies them.'"

old: And Israel served the Lord all the days of Joshua and all the days of the elders who prolonged their time after Joshua and who saw all the works of the Lord, all that He did for Israel.

old: And they buried him by the borders of his inheritance in Timnath-serah, in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gilead; there they placed with him in the tomb in which they buried him the stone knives with which he circumcised the sons of Israel in Gilgal, when He brought them out from Egypt, just as the Lord commanded them; and they are there to this day.
new: And they buried him by the borders of his inheritance in Timnath-serah, in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gilead; there they placed with him in the tomb in which they buried him the stone knives with which he circumcised the sons of Israel in Gilgal, when he brought them out from Egypt, just as the Lord commanded them; and they are there to this day.

old: And they buried him within the border of his inheritance in Timnath-heres, in Mount Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
new: And they buried him within the border of his inheritance in Timnath-heres, in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.

old: And they abandoned Him, and served Baal and the Ashtaroth.
new: And they abandoned Him, and served Baal and the Astartes.

old: And the Lord was angry with fury against Israel, and He sold them into the hand of Cushan-rishathaim, king of the rivers of Syria. And the sons of Israel served Cushan-rishathaim eight years.
new: And the Lord became angry with wrath against Israel, and He sold them into the hand of Cushan-rishathaim, king of the rivers of Syria. And the sons of Israel served Cushan-rishathaim eight years.

old: And he gathered to himself all the sons of Ammon and Amalek, and he went and struck Israel, and he took possession of the city of palm trees.
new: And he gathered to himself all the sons of Ammon and Amalek, and he went and struck Israel, and he took possession of the City of Palms.

old: And Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth, she was judging Israel at that time.

old: The Greek text consistently refers to the Philistines as allophyloi ("foreigners") throughout Judges.

old: Look, here are my virgin daughter and his concubine. I will bring them out, and humiliate them, and do to them what is good in your eyes; and to this man you will not do this matter of folly."

old: And Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, "Blessed is he by the Lord, because He has not forsaken His mercy toward the living and toward the dead." And Naomi said to her, "The man is close to us; he is one of our kinsman-redeemers."

old: Greek reads 'in all these consecrated places' where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads simply 'in all these places'; in v. 17 (and 8:4) Greek reads 'Ramathaim' where the Masoretic Text reads 'Ramah.'

old: and the Lord will deliver you up today into my hand, and I will kill you and remove your head from you, and I will give your limbs and the limbs of the camp of the foreigners on this day to the birds of the sky and to the wild beasts of the earth; and all the earth will know that there is a God in Israel.

old: The Greek verb περιέπεσαν is morphologically third-person plural ("they happened/fell"), here reflecting an early uncial spelling (or dittography before ἐν) of first-person singular περιέπεσα ("I happened by chance"), as required by the speaker's eyewitness narrative in vv. 6-7.

reason: The note justified emending the Greek; restated neutrally to describe the reading actually translated.

old: And Abner spoke to the elders of Israel, saying, "In earlier times you were seeking David to reign over you.
new: And Abner spoke to the elders of Israel, saying, "Yesterday and the day before you were seeking David to reign over you.

old: The Greek renders the Hebrew place name Baale-judah as "from the rulers of Judah in an ascent" and translates the divine title as "Lord of powers" (Kyrios ton dynameon, also in 6:18; MT: "LORD of hosts"). In 6:3, the Greek reads "to the house of Amminadab" (MT: "from the house of Abinadab"; cf. 1 Sam 7:1) and translates the Hebrew name Ahio as "his brothers" (also in 6:4).
new: The Greek renders the Hebrew place name Baale-judah as "from the rulers of Judah in an ascent" and translates the divine title as "Lord of powers" (Kyrios ton dynameon, also in 6:18; MT: "Lord of hosts"). In 6:3, the Greek reads "to the house of Amminadab" (MT: "from the house of Abinadab"; cf. 1 Sam 7:1) and translates the Hebrew name Ahio as "his brothers" (also in 6:4).
reason: House style forbids LORD in capitals.

old: And now thus you will say to My servant David: 'Thus says the Lord Almighty: I took you from the sheepfold for you to be a ruler over My people, over Israel,

old: And David perceived that his attendants were whispering, and David realized that the child was dead. And David said to his attendants, "Is the child dead?" And they said, "He is dead."

new: And his servants said to him, "What is this thing that you have done? For the sake of the child while he was still alive, you were fasting and weeping and staying awake; yet when the child died, you arose and ate bread and have drunk."

new: And Absalom came to the king and said, "See now, they are shearing for your servant; please let the king and his servants go with your servant."

old: Therefore this is what I myself firmly counsel: let all Israel surely be gathered to you, from Dan even to Beersheba, like the sand that is by the sea in multitude, and your own presence going in their midst;

old: But the man said to Joab, "Even if I were weighing out a thousand shekels of silver into my hands, I would by no means lay my hand on the king's son; for in our ears the king commanded you and Abishai and Ittai, saying, 'Guard for me the young man Absalom,

old: The Septuagint begins chapter 19 here (corresponding to 18:33 in most English Bibles) and renders the Hebrew wish idiom literally as "Who would grant my death in place of you?" (Greek tis doe). Its wording of David's lament is also shorter than the Hebrew Masoretic Text.

new: The Greek reads "the ailam" (transliterating Hebrew ulam, the porch) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text mentions casting the two bronze pillars, and gives the pillar's circumference as fourteen cubits rather than twelve.

old: And also concerning the foreigner who is not from Your people,

old: And Pharaoh said to Hader, "What do you lack with me, that look, you seek to depart to your land?" And Hader said to him, "Yet you must surely send me away." And Hader returned to his land.

old: This was the evil that Hader did: he abhorred Israel, and he reigned in Edom.

old: "Your father made our yoke heavy; and now, lighten the harsh service of your father and his heavy yoke that he laid on us, and we will serve you."

old: And Rehoboam slept with his fathers, and he was buried with his fathers in the city of David; and Abijah his son reigned in his place.

old: Greek reads "grove" (Hebrew: Asherah) and "to provoke his own soul to anger, so as to be utterly destroyed," where the Hebrew reads "to provoke the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger."

old: for this is what the Lord says: 'The jar of flour will not fail and the flask of oil will not diminish until the day that the Lord gives rain upon the land.'"
