new: In the Kohathite and Gershonite city lists (vv. 53-61), the Greek omits Bileam (v. 55) and differs from the Masoretic Text (MT 6:68-76) in several names: Ikaam (v. 53; MT Jokmeam), Esebaon and Gezer (v. 54; MT Aijalon and Gath-rimmon), Amar (v. 55; MT Aner), Aseroth (v. 56; MT Ashtaroth), Deberi and Dabor (v. 57; MT Daberath), Jeththar and Debir (v. 58; MT Ramoth and Anem), Maasa and Abaran (v. 59; MT Mashal and Abdon), and Hammoth (v. 61; MT Hammon).
reason: The Greek of v. 54 does not omit a city; it reads Ἐσεβαών and Γαζέρ where MT has Aijalon and Gath-rimmon, so the note's omission claim was false for this text.

old: And Ner fathered Kish, and Kish fathered Saul, and Saul fathered Jonathan, and Malchishua, and Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
new: And Ner fathered Kish, and Kish fathered Saul, and Saul fathered Jonathan, and Malchishua, and Amminadab, and Eshbaal.
reason: The Greek reads τὸν Ἀμειναδάβ (Amminadab, as rendered in 8:33 with its note); "Abinadab" restores the Hebrew name.

old: And Azel had six sons, and these were their names: Azrikam his firstborn, and Ishmael, and Sheariah, and Obadiah, and Hanan; these were the sons of Azel.
new: And Azel had six sons, and these were their names: Azrikam his firstborn, and Ishmael, and Seraiah, and Obadiah, and Hanan; these were the sons of Azel.
reason: The Greek reads Σαραιά, rendered "Seraiah" for the identical Greek in the parallel 8:38; "Sheariah" follows the Hebrew.

old: And the foreigners pursued after Saul and after his sons; and the foreigners struck down Jonathan, and Abinadab, and Malchishua, the sons of Saul.
new: And the foreigners pursued after Saul and after his sons; and the foreigners struck down Jonathan, and Amminadab, and Malchishua, the sons of Saul.
reason: The Greek reads τὸν Ἀμειναδάβ (Amminadab, as in 8:33); "Abinadab" restores the Hebrew name.

old: And they stripped him, and took his head and his armor, and sent word into the land of the foreigners all around to proclaim the good news to their idols and to the people.
new: And they stripped him, and took his head and his armor, and sent into the land of the foreigners all around to proclaim the good news to their idols and to the people.
reason: ἀπέστειλαν has no object in the Greek; "word" is a supplied interpretation of what was sent.

old: And David and all Israel were playing before God with all might, and with psalm-singers and with lyres and with harps, with tambourines and with cymbals and with trumpets.
new: And David and all Israel were playing before God with all might, and with singers and with lyres and with harps, with tambourines and with cymbals and with trumpets.
reason: ψαλτῳδοί is rendered "singers" in 15:16, 15:19 and 15:27; use the same English here.

old: offspring of Israel, His servants, sons of Jacob, His chosen ones.
new: seed of Israel, His servants, sons of Jacob, His chosen ones.
reason: σπέρμα is rendered with the literal collective "seed" in this edition (cf. 17:11 "your seed"), not "offspring".

old: And now thus you will say to My servant David, 'This is what the Lord Almighty says: I took you from the sheepfold, from behind the flocks, to be ruler over My people Israel,
new: And now thus you will say to My servant David, 'Thus says the Lord Almighty: I took you from the sheepfold, from behind the flocks, to be ruler over My people Israel,
reason: τάδε λέγει → "Thus says …" (OT-wide)

old: The Greek reads "I will increase you, and the Lord will build you," whereas the Hebrew reads "I declare to you that the LORD will build a house for you."
new: The Greek reads "I will increase you, and the Lord will build you," whereas the Hebrew reads "I declare to you that the Lord will build a house for you."
reason: house style: "Lord" in notes

old: Now the tabernacle of the Lord, which Moses had made in the wilderness, and the altar of burnt offerings were at that time in Bamoth in Gibeon.
new: Now the tent of the Lord, which Moses had made in the wilderness, and the altar of burnt offerings were at that time in Bamoth in Gibeon.
reason: σκηνὴ Κυρίου is rendered "tent of the Lord" in 16:39 (and σκηνή "tent" in 15:1, 16:1, 23:26); keep the same English here.

old: He will build a house for My name, and he will be to Me as a son, and I to him as a father, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom in Israel forever.'
new: He will build a house for My name, and he will be to Me as a son, and I to him as a father, and I will set upright the throne of his kingdom in Israel forever.'
reason: ἀνορθώσω θρόνον is rendered "set his throne upright" in 17:12 (cf. 17:14, 17:24); "establish" is used for κατορθόω (28:7).

old: For David said, "The Lord God of Israel has given rest to His people, and dwells in Jerusalem forever."
new: For David said, "The Lord God of Israel has given rest to His people, and has settled in Jerusalem forever."
reason: κατεσκήνωσεν is aorist, parallel to κατέπαυσεν ("has given rest"); present "dwells" follows the Hebrew rather than the Greek tense.

old: And they shall keep the charges of the tent of the testimony and the charges of the sons of Aaron their brothers, to serve in the house of the Lord.
new: And they shall keep the charges of the tent of testimony and the charges of the sons of Aaron their brothers, to serve in the house of the Lord.
reason: σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου has the established rendering "tent of testimony".

old: The Greek text omits the fifteenth course of the Hebrew list (Bilgah), shifting the remaining courses so that the list ends at twenty-three rather than twenty-four (v. 18); across vv. 7-18 it also preserves distinctive Greek name forms (Jarim, Anaidiah, Hareb, Benjamin, Ischaniah, Eliabiei, Hocchoppha, Gelba, Hezin, Aphese, Achim, Adallai, and Maasai).
new: The Greek text omits the fourteenth course of the Hebrew list (Jeshebeab; Gelba corresponds to Bilgah), shifting the remaining courses so that the list ends at twenty-three rather than twenty-four (v. 18); across vv. 7-18 it also preserves distinctive Greek name forms (Jarim, Anaidiah, Hareb, Benjamin, Ischaniah, Eliabiei, Hocchoppha, Gelba, Hezin, Aphese, Achim, Adallai, and Maasai).
reason: In this Greek, Gelba (14th, = Bilgah) is followed by Immer (15th), so the course with no counterpart is Hebrew Jeshebeab (14th), not Bilgah.

old: concerning all his kingdom and his might, which came upon him and upon Israel and upon all the kingdoms of the earth. Solomon the son of David grew strong over his kingdom, and the Lord his God was with him and exalted him to the heights.
new: concerning all his kingdom and his might, which came upon him and upon Israel and upon all the kingdoms of the earth. Solomon the son of David grew strong over his kingdom, and the Lord his God was with him and made him grow to the heights.
reason: ηὔξησεν αὐτὸν is "increased/made him grow" (αὐξάνω), not "exalted" (ὑψόω).

old: And Solomon began to build the house of the Lord in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where the Lord had appeared to David his father, in the place that David had prepared, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
new: And Solomon began to build the house of the Lord in Jerusalem on Mount Hamoria, where the Lord had appeared to David his father, in the place that David had prepared, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
reason: The Greek has the distinct form Ἁμορειά (rough breathing rendered H, as with Hasam, Hanami, Hader); "Moriah" restores the Hebrew name.

new: Greek reads Hamoria (Hamoreia), corresponding to Hebrew ha-Moriah ("the Moriah") with the article taken as part of the name.
reason: One-sentence explanation of the Greek place-name form adopted in the verse.

old: And he made the veil of blue and purple and crimson and fine linen, and he wove cherubim into it.
new: And he made the curtain of blue and purple and crimson and fine linen, and he wove cherubim into it.
reason: καταπέτασμα → "curtain" (OT-wide)

old: then You will listen from heaven and act, and judge Your servants, to repay the lawless one and return his ways upon his head, to vindicate the righteous one, to repay him according to his righteousness.
new: then You will listen from heaven and act, and judge Your servants, to repay the lawless one and return his ways upon his head, to justify the righteous one, to repay him according to his righteousness.
reason: δικαιῶσαι δίκαιον: δικαιόω is rendered "justify" in this edition (so the parallel 1 Kings 8:32 "to justify the righteous one").

old: And when Solomon finished praying, fire came down from heaven and consumed the whole burnt offerings and the sacrifices, and the glory of the Lord filled the house.
new: And when Solomon finished praying, fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offerings and the sacrifices, and the glory of the Lord filled the house.
reason: ὁλοκαυτώματα is "burnt offerings" everywhere else in 2 Chronicles (2:3, 4:6, 8:12, 9:4, 13:11); only 7:1 and 7:7 have "whole burnt offerings".

old: And Solomon consecrated the middle of the courtyard that was in the house of the Lord; for he offered there the whole burnt offerings and the fat portions of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar that Solomon had made was not sufficient to receive the whole burnt offerings and the grain offerings and the fat portions.
new: And Solomon consecrated the middle of the courtyard that was in the house of the Lord; for he offered there the burnt offerings and the fat portions of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar that Solomon had made was not sufficient to receive the burnt offerings and the grain offerings and the fat portions.
reason: τὰ ὁλοκαυτώματα (twice): the book's established rendering is "burnt offerings".

old: and on the twenty-third day of the seventh month he sent the people away to their tents, rejoicing and with a glad heart for the good things that the Lord had done for David and for Solomon and for Israel His people.
new: and on the twenty-third day of the seventh month he sent the people away to their tents, rejoicing and with a good heart for the good things that the Lord had done for David and for Solomon and for Israel His people.
reason: ἀγαθῇ καρδίᾳ is "with a good heart" (cf. καρδίαν ἀγαθήν "a good heart" in 1 Chr 29:19); "glad" follows the Hebrew idiom.

old: and if My people, upon whom My name has been called, are humbled and pray and seek My face, and turn away from their evil ways, then I will listen from heaven and pardon their sins and heal their land.
new: and if My people, upon whom My name has been called, feel shame and pray and seek My face, and turn away from their evil ways, then I will listen from heaven and pardon their sins and heal their land.
reason: ἐντραπῇ (ἐντρέπομαι) means "feel shame" and is so rendered in 12:7 and 12:12; "are humbled" follows the Hebrew.

old: And when he felt shame, the anger of the Lord turned away from him, and not to complete destruction; for indeed in Judah there were good words.
new: And when he felt shame, the anger of the Lord turned away from him, and not to complete destruction; for indeed in Judah there were good things.
reason: λόγοι ἀγαθοί here has the same sense as in 19:3, where it is rendered "good things" (λόγος = matter, as in 9:2).

old: Or did you not drive out the priests of the Lord, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and make for yourselves priests from the people of the whole land? Whoever came forward to fill his hands with calves from the cattle and with seven rams became a priest to that which is not God.
new: Or did you not drive out the priests of the Lord, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and make for yourselves priests from the people of the whole land? Whoever came forward to fill his hands with calves from the cattle and with seven rams became a priest to that which is not a god.
reason: τῷ μὴ ὄντι θεῷ has anarthrous predicate θεῷ: "to what is not a god" (the idols), not "not God".

old: they offer up in smoke to the Lord a burnt offering morning and evening, and compound incense, and arrangements of bread on the pure table, and the golden lampstand and the lamps for burning to light in the evening; for we ourselves keep the charges of the Lord, the God of our fathers, and you have abandoned Him.
new: they offer up in smoke to the Lord a burnt offering morning and evening, and compound incense, and presentations of bread on the pure table, and the golden lampstand and the lamps for burning to light in the evening; for we ourselves keep the charges of the Lord, the God of our fathers, and you have abandoned Him.
reason: πρόθεσις is rendered "presentation" in 2:3 and 4:19 ("loaves of presentation"); keep the same term for προθέσεις ἄρτων.

old: Fortified cities were in the land of Judah, because the land was at peace; and he had no war in those years, because the Lord gave him rest.
new: Walled cities were in the land of Judah, because the land was at peace; and he had no war in those years, because the Lord gave him rest.
reason: πόλεις τειχήρεις is "walled cities" in 11:5, 11:10, 11:11; "fortified" is kept for ὀχυρός.

old: The Greek text lacks a verb before 'fortified cities in the land of Judah' (where the Hebrew and some other witnesses read 'and he built fortified cities'), leaving a verbless clause following verse 4.
new: The Greek text lacks a verb before 'walled cities in the land of Judah' (where the Hebrew and some other witnesses read 'and he built fortified cities'), leaving a verbless clause following verse 4.
reason: Keeps the note's quotation of the verse in step with the corrected rendering of τειχήρεις.

old: And he assembled Judah and Benjamin and the proselytes who were residing with him from Ephraim and from Manasseh and from Simeon, because many of Israel joined themselves to him when they saw that the Lord his God was with him.
new: And he assembled Judah and Benjamin and the resident aliens who were residing with him from Ephraim and from Manasseh and from Simeon, because many of Israel joined themselves to him when they saw that the Lord his God was with him.
reason: προσηλύτους here are Israelites from Ephraim, Manasseh and Simeon living as aliens in Judah, not religious converts; "resident aliens" is the edition's rendering (2:16 and the Law).

old: And at the end of some years he went down to Ahab in Samaria, and Ahab slaughtered many sheep and calves for him and for the people who were with him, and he coaxed him to go up with him to Ramoth of Gilead.
new: And at the end of some years he went down to Ahab in Samaria, and Ahab slaughtered many sheep and calves for him and for the people who were with him, and he showed him affection so that he would go up with him to Ramoth of Gilead.
reason: This Greek reads ἠγάπα ("loved, showed affection to") with purpose τοῦ συναναβῆναι; "coaxed" reflects the Hebrew ("incited") or the variant ἠπάτα.

old: The Greek text lacks a verb and repeats "spirit" (pneuma) three times in an apparent textual conflation (contrast MT "Which way did the Spirit of the LORD go from me to speak to you?").
new: The Greek text lacks a verb and repeats "spirit" (pneuma) three times in an apparent textual conflation (contrast MT "Which way did the Spirit of the Lord go from me to speak to you?").
reason: House style never uses "LORD" in capitals, even when citing the Hebrew.

old: Greek reads passive "one hated by the Lord" where MT has active "those who hate the LORD," and places "King Jehoshaphat" as a direct vocative opening Jehu's speech.
new: Greek reads passive "one hated by the Lord" where MT has active "those who hate the Lord," and places "King Jehoshaphat" as a direct vocative opening Jehu's speech.
reason: House style never uses "LORD" in capitals, even when citing the Hebrew.

old: And King Joash called Jehoiada the leader and said to him, "Why have you not inquired concerning the Levites, to bring in from Judah and Jerusalem what was decreed by Moses the man of God, because he assembled Israel to the tent of the testimony?"
new: And King Joash called Jehoiada the leader and said to him, "Why have you not inquired concerning the Levites, to bring in from Judah and Jerusalem what was decreed by Moses the man of God, because he assembled Israel to the tent of testimony?"
reason: σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου is "tent of testimony" elsewhere in this book (e.g. 1:3); align the one outlier.

old: And they forsook the Lord, the God of their fathers, and served the Astartes and the idols; and wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem on that day.
new: And they forsook the Lord, the God of their fathers, and served the Astartes and the idols; and wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem on this day.
reason: ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ταύτῃ is "on this day" (cf. 21:10 ἕως τῆς ἡμέρας ταύτης "until this day"); "that" changes the demonstrative.

old: The Greek text reads "the Astartes" (MT "the Asherim") and "on that day" (MT "for this guilt of theirs").
new: The Greek text reads "the Astartes" (MT "the Asherim") and "on this day" (MT "for this guilt of theirs").
reason: Note must match the Greek ταύτῃ ("this") and the corrected verse.

old: For if you think you will prevail with these, then the Lord will rout you before the enemies, because it belongs to the Lord both to give strength and to rout."
new: For if you think you will prevail with these, then the Lord will rout you before the enemies, because it is from the Lord both to be strong and to rout."
reason: ἐστὶν παρὰ Κυρίου καὶ ἰσχῦσαι is "it is from the Lord both to be strong"; ἰσχῦσαι is intransitive, so "give strength" makes it causative and "belongs to" rephrases παρά.

old: And at the time when Amaziah turned away from the Lord, they laid a plot against him, and he fled from Jerusalem to Lachish; and they sent after him to Lachish and put him to death there.
new: And at the time when Amaziah turned away from the Lord, they laid a plot against him, and he fled from Jerusalem to Lachish; and he sent after him to Lachish and put him to death there.
reason: ἀπέστειλεν and ἐθανάτωσεν are singular in this Greek; the plural "they" follows the Hebrew.

old: The Greek closing question literally asks whether it is not for them "with yourselves to bear witness to the Lord our God," diverging from the Hebrew text's reference to "guilts against the LORD your God."
new: The Greek closing question literally asks whether it is not for them "with yourselves to bear witness to the Lord our God," diverging from the Hebrew text's reference to "guilts against the Lord your God."
reason: House style never uses LORD in capitals, also when citing the Hebrew.

old: And now do not be negligent, for He has chosen you to stand before Him to minister, and to be ministering and burning incense to Him."
new: And now do not cease, for He has chosen you to stand before Him to minister, and to be ministering and burning incense to Him."
reason: μὴ διαλίπητε (διαλείπω) means "do not leave off/cease"; "be negligent" reproduces the Hebrew verb.

old: And Hezekiah did not repay according to the benefit that He gave him, but his heart was lifted up; and wrath came upon him and upon Judah and Jerusalem.
new: And Hezekiah did not repay according to the recompense that He gave him, but his heart was lifted up; and wrath came upon him and upon Judah and Jerusalem.
reason: ἀνταπόδομα is "recompense, repayment" (matching ἀπέδωκεν "repay"); "benefit" follows the Hebrew gemul.

old: And after these things he built a wall outside the city of David on the west toward Gihon in the torrent valley, and as one goes out through the surrounding gate, and up to Ophel itself, and he raised it very high; and he stationed commanders of the army in all the walled cities in Judah.
new: And after these things he built a wall outside the city of David on the west toward Gihon in the torrent valley, and as one goes out through the surrounding gate, and up to Opla itself, and he raised it very high; and he stationed commanders of the army in all the walled cities in Judah.
reason: The Greek has Ὄπλα, which the edition renders "Opla" at 27:3 and the note here says so; "Ophel" restores the Hebrew name.

old: Look, I am gathering you to your fathers, and you will be gathered to your tombs in peace, and your eyes will not look upon all the evils that I am bringing upon this place and upon those who live in it.'" And they brought back word to the king.
new: Look, I am adding you to your fathers, and you will be added to your tombs in peace, and your eyes will not look upon all the evils that I am bringing upon this place and upon those who live in it.'" And they brought back word to the king.
reason: προστίθημι / προστεθήσῃ is "add / be added", as the edition renders this idiom elsewhere (e.g. 2 Kings 22:20 "I am adding you to your fathers", Gen 25:8); "gather" follows the Hebrew asaph.

old: And he did what was evil in the sight of the Lord his God; he did not humble himself before Jeremiah the prophet and from the mouth of the Lord,
new: And he did what was evil in the sight of the Lord his God; he did not feel shame before Jeremiah the prophet and from the mouth of the Lord,
reason: οὐκ ἐνετράπη (ἐντρέπομαι) is "was not ashamed/did not feel shame", as the book renders it at 12:7, 12:12 and 30:15; "humble himself" follows the Hebrew nikhna.

old: And as for everyone who remains from all the places where he resides, the men of his place will assist him with silver and gold and goods and livestock, along with the freewill offering for the house of the God who is in Jerusalem."
new: And as for everyone who remains from all the places where he resides, the men of his place will receive him with silver and gold and goods and livestock, along with the freewill offering for the house of the God who is in Jerusalem."
reason: λήμψονται αὐτόν is "will take/receive him"; "assist" imports the sense of the Hebrew verb (nasa', support) rather than translating the Greek.

old: And after the events, in the reign of Artaxerxes, king of the Persians, Ezra went up, the son of Seraiah, the son of Azariah, the son of Hilkiah,
new: And after the events, in the reign of Artaxerxes, king of the Persians, Ezra went up, the son of Seraiah, the son of Zerahiah, the son of Hilkiah,
reason: This critical text reads υἱοῦ Ζαρείου (it explicitly adopts Ζαρείου over Ἀζαρίου); "Azariah" restores the Hebrew/Sixtine name. The edition renders Ζαρειά as "Zerahiah" (Ezra 8:4).

new: The Greek reads Zareiou (Zerahiah) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has Azariah.
reason: One-sentence explanation for the changed name in the genealogy.

old: And I weighed out to them the silver and the gold and the vessels of the offering of the house of our God, which the king and his counselors and his leaders and all Israel who were present had offered up.
new: And I weighed out to them the silver and the gold and the vessels of the firstfruits of the house of our God, which the king and his counselors and his leaders and all Israel who were present had offered up.
reason: ἀπαρχῆς is "firstfruits" (the edition's rendering of ἀπαρχή, e.g. Exod 25:2-3, Neh 10:38, 12:44); "offering" follows the Hebrew terumah.

old: And I returned word to them and said to them, "The God of heaven, He will grant us success, and we are His pure servants, and let us build; but for you there is no portion, nor right, nor memorial in Jerusalem."
new: And I returned word to them and said to them, "The God of heaven, He will grant us success, and we are His pure servants, and let us build; but for you there is no portion, nor righteousness, nor memorial in Jerusalem."
reason: δικαιοσύνη is rendered "righteousness" in this edition; "right" (legal claim) reflects the Hebrew tsedaqah sense rather than the Greek word.

old: And I entered the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah, son of Meitael, and he was shut in; and he said, "Let us gather into the house of God, in the midst of it, and let us shut its doors, because they are coming by night to kill you."
new: And I entered the house of Shimei son of Delaiah, son of Meitael, and he was shut in; and he said, "Let us gather into the house of God, in the midst of it, and let us shut its doors, because they are coming by night to kill you."
reason: The Greek name is Σεμεεί, which the edition renders "Shimei" (Ezra 10:33, 38; Σαμαιά is "Shemaiah"); "Shemaiah" restores the Hebrew name.

old: Greek "Meitael" is a distinctive Septuagint form of the name corresponding to Hebrew "Mehetabel."
new: Greek Semeei ("Shimei") and "Meitael" are distinctive Septuagint forms corresponding to Hebrew "Shemaiah" and "Mehetabel."
reason: Note updated to explain the Greek name Σεμεεί now rendered in the verse.

old: And on the second day the leaders of the fathers' houses gathered together with all the people, the priests, and the Levites to Ezra the scribe, to give attention to all the words of the law.
new: And on the second day the leaders of the ancestral families gathered together with all the people, the priests, and the Levites to Ezra the scribe, to give attention to all the words of the law.
reason: οἱ ἄρχοντες τῶν πατριῶν has no οἶκος; πατριῶν is rendered "ancestral families" elsewhere in this section (7:61, 7:70-71, 10:35, 11:13)

old: And in the days of Joiakim, his brothers the priests and the leaders of the ancestral houses were: for Seraiah, Meraiah; for Jeremiah;
new: And in the days of Joiakim, his brothers the priests and the leaders of the ancestral families were: for Seraiah, Meraiah; for Jeremiah;
reason: οἱ ἄρχοντες τῶν πατριῶν has no οἶκος; πατριῶν is rendered "ancestral families" in 7:70-71, 10:35, 11:13

old: The Levites in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Joa, Johanan, and Jaddua were recorded as leaders of ancestral houses, and the priests, in the reign of Darius the Persian.
new: The Levites in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Joa, Johanan, and Jaddua were recorded as leaders of ancestral families, and the priests, in the reign of Darius the Persian.
reason: ἄρχοντες πατριῶν has no οἶκος; same phrase is "leaders of ancestral families" in 11:13

old: The sons of Levi, leaders of the ancestral houses, were recorded in the book of the records of the days, even until the days of Johanan son of Eliashib.
new: The sons of Levi, leaders of the ancestral families, were recorded in the book of the records of the days, even until the days of Johanan son of Eliashib.
reason: ἄρχοντες τῶν πατριῶν has no οἶκος; πατριῶν is rendered "ancestral families" elsewhere in Nehemiah

old: And Esther said, "Today is my special day; if therefore it pleases the king, let both him and Haman come to the banquet that I will prepare today."
new: And Esther said, "Today is my special day; if therefore it seems good to the king, let both him and Haman come to the banquet that I will prepare today."
reason: εἰ οὖν δοκεῖ τῷ βασιλεῖ is "if it seems good to the king" (as in 1:19, 3:9, 8:5); "please" is used for ἀρέσκω in Esther

old: Greek xylon literally means "wood," "beam," or "pole" (used for hanging or impaling), traditionally rendered "gallows."
new: Greek xylon literally means "wood," "beam," or "pole" (used for hanging or impaling).
reason: Remove the claim about how other translations render ξύλον; keep the lexical explanation

old: And the king said, "What honor or favor have we done for Mordecai?" And the servants of the king said, "You have done nothing for him."
new: And the king said, "What honor or favor have we done for Mordecai?" And the attendants of the king said, "You have done nothing for him."
reason: οἱ διάκονοι τοῦ βασιλέως is "the attendants of the king" in 1:10 and 2:2; "servants" here also blurs it with οἱ παῖδες in 6:8

old: And the servants of the king said, "Look, Haman is standing in the courtyard." And the king said, "Call him."
new: And the attendants of the king said, "Look, Haman is standing in the courtyard." And the king said, "Call him."
reason: οἱ διάκονοι τοῦ βασιλέως is "the attendants of the king" in 1:10 and 2:2

old: let the king's attendants bring a fine linen robe that the king wears, and a horse on which the king rides,
new: let the king's servants bring a fine linen robe that the king wears, and a horse on which the king rides,
reason: οἱ παῖδες τοῦ βασιλέως: παῖς is "servant" in the OT by edition convention (cf. 7:4 παῖδας "servants"); "attendants" is used for διάκονοι

old: And the king said to Esther on the second day during the drinking banquet, "What is it, Queen Esther, and what is your request, and what is your petition? And let it be yours, up to half of my kingdom."
new: And the king said to Esther on the second day during the drinking feast, "What is it, Queen Esther, and what is your request, and what is your petition? And let it be yours, up to half of my kingdom."
reason: ἐν τῷ πότῳ: πότος is "drinking feast" throughout Esther (1:5, 1:8, 1:9, 2:18, 5:6, 6:14); "banquet" renders δοχή/συμπόσιον

old: and he established it; and the Jews accepted it upon themselves and upon their offspring and upon those joined to them, and they will certainly not act otherwise. And these days are a memorial observed generation after generation, and in every city, family, and province.
new: and he established it; and the Jews accepted it upon themselves and upon their seed and upon those joined to them, and they will certainly not act otherwise. And these days are a memorial observed generation after generation, and in every city, family, and province.
reason: ἐπὶ τῷ σπέρματι αὐτῶν: σπέρμα (descendants) is rendered "seed" by edition convention

old: The Greek text reads the verb "to profane" (bebelosai) rather than the adjective "profane" (bebelo) found in other witnesses; similarly 1:47 reads "idols" (eidola) rather than "idol shrines" (eidolia).
new: The Greek text reads the verb "to profane" (bebelosai) rather than the noun "profanation" (bebelosei) found in other witnesses; similarly 1:47 reads "idols" (eidola) rather than "idol shrines" (eidolia).
reason: The competing reading is the dative noun βεβηλώσει ("profanation"), not an adjective βεβήλῳ; the note misstates the variant.

old: yet I and my sons and my brothers will walk in the covenant of our fathers.
new: yet I and my sons and my brothers—let us walk in the covenant of our fathers.
reason: This Greek reads the aorist subjunctive πορευσώμεθα (hortatory "let us walk"), not the future πορευσόμεθα; "will walk" follows the other reading.

old: The Greek text includes hos ("as it were, into heaven"), echoing Septuagint 2 Kings 2:11, whereas some manuscripts omit it.
new: The Greek text reads hos ("as it were, into heaven"), echoing Septuagint 2 Kings 2:11, whereas other witnesses read heos ("up into heaven").
reason: The other witnesses do not omit the word; they read ἕως in place of ὡς, so the note's claim is inaccurate.

old: And Apollonius gathered Gentiles, and from Samaria a great force, to fight against Israel.
new: And Apollonius gathered nations, and from Samaria a great force, to fight against Israel.
reason: ἔθνη is rendered "nations" per the OT convention and elsewhere in this book (e.g. 1:11, 2:68, 5:10).

old: And the merchants of the country heard of their fame, and took a very great amount of silver and gold, and servants, and came into the camp to take the sons of Israel as slaves; and forces of Syria and of the land of the foreigners joined them.
new: And the merchants of the country heard of their fame, and took a very great amount of silver and gold, and servants, and came into the camp to take the sons of Israel as servants; and forces of Syria and of the land of the foreigners joined them.
reason: εἰς παῖδας uses the same word παῖδας rendered "servants" earlier in this verse; παῖς → "servant" is the OT convention.

old: And Jerusalem was uninhabited like a wilderness; there was not one of her children going in or going out; and the sanctuary was trampled down, and sons of foreigners were in the citadel, a lodging place among the Gentiles; and delight was taken away from Jacob, and flute and lyre ceased.
new: And Jerusalem was uninhabited like a wilderness; there was not one of her offspring going in or going out; and the sanctuary was trampled down, and sons of foreigners were in the citadel, a lodging place among the nations; and delight was taken away from Jacob, and flute and lyre ceased.
reason: γενημάτων is "offspring" as in 1:38 (τέκνα is "children"), and ἔθνεσιν is "nations" per the OT convention.

old: And they spread open the book of the law concerning the things about which the Gentiles were consulting the likenesses of their idols.
new: And they spread open the book of the law concerning the things about which the nations were consulting the likenesses of their idols.
reason: τὰ ἔθνη is rendered "nations" per the OT convention and elsewhere in this book.

old: This clause is debated; the Greek literally indicates that they spread open the book of the law concerning the matters about which the Gentiles consulted the likenesses of their idols.
new: This clause is debated; the Greek literally indicates that they spread open the book of the law concerning the matters about which the nations consulted the likenesses of their idols.
reason: Keeps the note in line with the verse's rendering of τὰ ἔθνη as "nations".

old: And look, the Gentiles have gathered together against us to destroy us; You know what they plot against us.
new: And look, the nations have gathered together against us to destroy us; You know what they plot against us.
reason: τὰ ἔθνη is rendered "nations" per the OT convention (cf. the same phrase in 5:10).

old: And Judas said, "Arm yourselves and be valiant men, and be ready for the morning to fight against these Gentiles who have assembled against us to destroy us and our sanctuary.
new: And Judas said, "Arm yourselves and be valiant men, and be ready for the morning to fight against these nations who have assembled against us to destroy us and our sanctuary.
reason: τοῖς ἔθνεσιν τούτοις is rendered with "nations" per the OT convention for ἔθνη.

old: And they saw an army of Gentiles, strong and clad in armor, and cavalry encircling it, and these were trained in war.
new: And they saw an army of nations, strong and clad in armor, and cavalry encircling it, and these were trained in war.
reason: ἐθνῶν is rendered "nations" per the OT convention and elsewhere in this book.

old: And they joined battle, and the Gentiles were crushed and fled into the plain.
new: And they joined battle, and the nations were crushed and fled into the plain.
reason: συνετρίβησαν τὰ ἔθνη is the same phrase rendered "the nations were crushed" in 5:21; ἔθνη → "nations" per the OT convention.

old: Deliver this army into the hands of Your people Israel, and let them be put to shame over their force and their cavalry.
new: Shut up this army in the hands of Your people Israel, and let them be put to shame over their force and their cavalry.
reason: σύνκλεισον is "shut up," the same idiom rendered "to be shut up in the hands of a few" (συνκλεισθῆναι) in 3:18; "deliver" drops the image.

old: And a good plan occurred to them, to tear it down, so that it would never become a reproach to them, because the Gentiles had defiled it; and they tore down the altar.
new: And a good plan occurred to them, to tear it down, so that it would never become a reproach to them, because the nations had defiled it; and they tore down the altar.
reason: τὰ ἔθνη is rendered "nations" per the OT convention (cf. 2:12 "nations have profaned them").

old: At the season, on the day on which the Gentiles had profaned it, on that day it was dedicated with songs and lyres and harps and with cymbals.
new: At the season, on the day on which the nations had profaned it, on that day it was dedicated with songs and lyres and harps and with cymbals.
reason: τὰ ἔθνη is rendered "nations" per the OT convention and elsewhere in this book.

old: And there was very great gladness among the people, and the reproach of the Gentiles was turned away.
new: And there was very great gladness among the people, and the reproach of the nations was turned away.
reason: ἐθνῶν is rendered "nations" per the OT convention and elsewhere in this book.

old: And at that time they built up Mount Zion with high walls and strong towers all around, so that the Gentiles would never come and trample them down as they had done before.
new: And at that time they built up Mount Zion with high walls and strong towers all around, so that the nations would never come and trample them down as they had done before.
reason: τὰ ἔθνη is rendered "nations" per the OT convention and elsewhere in this book.

old: The Greek text reads "the cities of Ptolemais" (ton poleon Ptolemaidos), whereas other witnesses read "the gates of Ptolemais" (ton pulon Ptolemaidos).
new: The Greek text reads "the cities of Ptolemais" (ton poleon Ptolemaidos), whereas other witnesses read "the gate of Ptolemais" (tes pyles Ptolemaidos).
reason: The competing reading is singular τῆς πύλης ("the gate"), not plural τῶν πυλῶν; the note misstates it.

old: And those from the citadel were hemming Israel in around the sanctuary, continually seeking evil, and they were a support for the Gentiles.
new: And those from the citadel were hemming Israel in around the sanctuary, continually seeking evil, and they were a support for the nations.
reason: τοῖς ἔθνεσιν is rendered "nations" per the OT convention and elsewhere in this book.

old: This Greek text connects the date directly to the preceding verse; other manuscripts insert "and they gathered together and besieged it" before "in the one hundred fiftieth year."
new: This Greek text connects the date directly to the preceding verse; other manuscripts insert "and they gathered together and besieged them" before "in the one hundred fiftieth year."
reason: The inserted clause in the other witnesses reads περιεκάθισαν ἐπ᾽ αὐτούς ("besieged them"), not "it".

old: And he gave himself to save his people and to acquire for himself an everlasting name.
new: And he gave himself to save his people and to acquire for himself an eternal name.
reason: αἰώνιον is rendered "eternal" per the edition's convention and in 2:51, 2:57 of this book.

old: But there was no food in the sanctuary, because it was the seventh year, and those who had been rescued into Judea from the Gentiles had eaten up the remainder of the supplies;
new: But there was no food in the sanctuary, because it was the seventh year, and those who had been rescued into Judea from the nations had eaten up the remainder of the supplies;
reason: τῶν ἐθνῶν is rendered "nations" per the OT convention and elsewhere in this book.

old: And they took the spoils and the plunder, and they cut off Nicanor's head and his right hand, which he had stretched out arrogantly, and brought them and displayed them beside Jerusalem.
new: And they took the spoils and the plunder, and they cut off Nicanor's head and his right hand, which he had stretched out arrogantly, and brought them and stretched them out beside Jerusalem.
reason: ἐξέτειναν repeats ἐξέτεινεν ("stretched out") from the same verse; "displayed" interprets and loses the Greek repetition.

old: and Antiochus the Great, king of Asia, who went against them to war having one hundred and twenty elephants, and cavalry, and chariots, and a very great force, was crushed by them;
new: and Antiochus, the great king of Asia, who went against them to war having one hundred and twenty elephants, and cavalry, and chariots, and a very great force, was crushed by them;
reason: In τὸν μέγαν βασιλέα τῆς Ἀσίας, μέγαν modifies βασιλέα ("the great king of Asia"); "Antiochus the Great" imports the historical epithet.

old: And he confirmed the high priesthood to him, and whatever other honors he had previously, and he made him chief of the first friends.
new: And he confirmed the high priesthood to him, and whatever other honors he had previously, and he made him chief of the First Friends.
reason: τῶν πρώτων φίλων is the same court title rendered "the First Friends" in 10:65; capitalize consistently.

old: "Give us pledges of peace, and let the Jews stop fighting against us and the city."
new: "Give us the right hand, and let the Jews stop fighting against us and the city."
reason: δεξιάς ("right hands") is kept literal as "the right hand" in 6:58, 13:45, 13:50; the idiom is clear and the note explains it.

old: And the people of Gaza appealed to Jonathan, and he gave them pledges of peace; and he took the sons of their rulers as hostages and sent them away to Jerusalem, and he passed through the country as far as Damascus.
new: And the people of Gaza appealed to Jonathan, and he gave them the right hand; and he took the sons of their rulers as hostages and sent them away to Jerusalem, and he passed through the country as far as Damascus.
reason: ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς δεξιάς: same idiom as 11:50 and 13:45 ("give the right hand"); render it the same way.

old: And they asked him that they might receive pledges of peace, and he gave them to them; and he expelled them from there, and seized the city, and placed a garrison over it.
new: And they asked him that they might receive the right hand, and he gave it to them; and he expelled them from there, and seized the city, and placed a garrison over it.
reason: τοῦ δεξιὰς λαβεῖν is the identical phrase rendered "to receive the right hand" in 13:50.

old: And they went to Rome, and they went into the senate house and said, "Jonathan the high priest and the nation of the Jews sent us to renew the friendship and the alliance for them as before."
new: And they went to Rome, and they went into the council chamber and said, "Jonathan the high priest and the nation of the Jews sent us to renew the friendship and the alliance for them as before."
reason: βουλευτήριον (the same Roman building) is "council chamber" in 8:15 and 8:19.

old: The Greek text ends with the lighting of the campfires, leaving the enemy's nighttime withdrawal implicit until 12:29-30; some later witnesses explicitly add 'and they departed.'
new: The Greek text ends with the lighting of the campfires, leaving the enemy's nighttime withdrawal implicit until 12:29-30; other witnesses add 'and they departed.'
reason: The claim that the witnesses adding the clause are "later" is unsupported; state the variant neutrally.

old: For he and his brothers and the house of his father stood firm, and they fought off the enemies of Israel from them and established freedom for it."
new: For he and his brothers and the house of his father stood firm, and they fought off the enemies of Israel from them." And they established freedom for it,
reason: The Greek ends the sentence at ἀπ᾽ αὐτῶν (full stop) and joins καὶ ἔστησαν αὐτῷ ἐλευθερίαν by a comma to the narrative of v. 27, so this clause is narrative, not part of the people's speech.

old: And they inscribed it on bronze tablets and placed them on a pillar on Mount Zion. And this is the copy of the writing: "On the eighteenth of Elul, in the one hundred and seventy-second year, and this is the third year under Simon the high priest,
new: and he inscribed it on bronze tablets, and they placed them on a pillar on Mount Zion. And this is the copy of the writing: "On the eighteenth of Elul, in the one hundred and seventy-second year, and this is the third year under Simon the high priest,
reason: κατέγραψεν is singular ("he inscribed") while ἔθεντο is plural; the sentence continues from v. 26 after the comma.

old: And in his days things prospered in his hands, so that the Gentiles were removed from their country, and also those in the city of David, those in Jerusalem, who had made for themselves a citadel from which they went out and defiled all around the sanctuary and inflicted a great blow upon purity.
new: And in his days things prospered in his hands, so that the nations were removed from their country, and also those in the city of David, those in Jerusalem, who had made for themselves a citadel from which they went out and defiled all around the sanctuary and inflicted a great blow upon purity.
reason: τὰ ἔθνη is "the nations" (OT convention and 12:53; 13:6, 41 in this section).

old: And their contents were in this manner: "King Antiochus to Simon, high priest and ethnarch, and to the nation of the Jews, greetings.
new: And their contents were in this manner: "King Antiochus to Simon, great priest and ethnarch, and to the nation of the Jews, greetings.
reason: ἱερεῖ μεγάλῳ is "great priest" in 12:20 and 14:20 (ἀρχιερεύς is "high priest"); keep the distinction.

old: And Simon answered and said to him, "We have neither taken foreign land nor held what belongs to others, but the inheritance of our fathers; yet it was wrongfully seized by our enemies for a certain time.
new: And Simon answered and said to him, "We have neither taken foreign land nor held what belongs to others, but the inheritance of our fathers; yet it was wrongfully seized by our enemies at a certain time.
reason: ἔν τινι καιρῷ marks a point in time ("at a certain time"), not duration.

old: For indeed, when our fathers were being led away into Persia, the devout priests secretly took some of the fire of the altar and hid it in a hollow having the form of a waterless cistern, in which they secured it so that the place was unknown to all.
new: For indeed, when our fathers were being led away into Persia, the devout priests secretly took some of the fire of the altar and hid it in the hollow of a cistern that was waterless, in which they secured it so that the place was unknown to all.
reason: ἔχοντος (genitive) agrees with φρέατος, so 'having a waterless state' describes the cistern, not the hollow: 'in a hollow of a cistern that was waterless (κοιλώματι φρέατος τάξιν ἔχοντος ἄνυδρον)'

old: And Antiochus was lifted up in his mind, not perceiving that because of the sins of those who inhabited the city the Sovereign had been angry for a brief time, and therefore a disregard had occurred concerning the place.
new: And Antiochus was lifted up in his mind, not perceiving that because of the sins of those who inhabited the city the Master had been angry for a brief time, and therefore a disregard had occurred concerning the place.
reason: ὁ δεσπότης is rendered 'the Master' per the OT divine-title convention and as this book does at 9:13; 'Sovereign' is reserved for δυνάστης (3:24; 12:15)

old: For if it had not happened that they were entangled in many sins, just as it was with Heliodorus who was sent by Seleucus the king for the inspection of the treasury, this man, upon advancing, would immediately have been scourged and turned back from his audacity.
new: For if it had not happened that they were entangled in many sins, just as it was with Heliodorus who was sent by Seleucus the king for the inspection of the treasury, this man, upon advancing, would immediately have been flogged and turned back from his audacity.
reason: μαστιγωθείς recalls the Heliodorus episode, where the same verb μαστιγόω is rendered 'flogged' (3:26, 3:34, 3:38)

old: Therefore the place itself also, having shared in the misfortunes that befell the nation, afterward shared in the benefits; and that which was overtaken in the wrath of the Almighty was restored again with all glory in the reconciliation of the great Sovereign.
new: Therefore the place itself also, having shared in the misfortunes that befell the nation, afterward shared in the benefits; and that which was overtaken in the wrath of the Almighty was restored again with all glory in the reconciliation of the great Master.
reason: τοῦ μεγάλου δεσπότου: δεσπότης is 'Master' per the OT divine-title convention and 9:13; 'Sovereign' is used for δυνάστης

old: For unlike with the other nations, where the Sovereign waits patiently to punish them until they have reached the full measure of their sins, He did not decide for it to be so with us,
new: For unlike with the other nations, where the Master waits patiently to punish them until they have reached the full measure of their sins, He did not decide for it to be so with us,
reason: ὁ δεσπότης is 'the Master' per the OT divine-title convention and 9:13; 'Sovereign' is used for δυνάστης

old: However, let these things be said by us by way of reminder; and after a few words we must proceed to the narrative.
new: However, let these things be said by us by way of reminder; and we must proceed briefly to the narrative.
reason: δι᾽ ὀλίγων here means 'in few words, briefly' (manner), not 'after a few words'; the narrative resumes immediately in v. 18

old: this one received the torture in turn, like the first. And when he was at his last breath, he said, "You indeed, accursed wretch, release us from this present life, but the King of the world will raise us up, since we have died for His laws, to an eternal renewal of life."
new: this one received the torture in turn, like the first. And when he was at his last breath, he said, "You indeed, accursed wretch, release us from this present life, but the King of the world will raise us up, who have died for His laws, to an eternal renewal of life."
reason: ἀποθανόντας is an attributive/circumstantial participle ('us who have died'); 'since' adds a causal relation the Greek does not state

old: But wait patiently, and watch His majestic power, how He will torture you and your offspring."
new: But wait patiently, and watch His majestic power, how He will torture you and your seed."
reason: τὸ σπέρμα σου: σπέρμα is rendered 'seed' per the edition's OT convention, not 'offspring'

old: while the others sold everything that remained, and at the same time begged the Lord to rescue those who had been sold by the impious Nicanor before they even met him,
new: while the others sold everything that remained, and at the same time begged the Lord to rescue those who had been sold by the impious Nicanor before they met him,
reason: πρὶν συντυχεῖν is simply 'before meeting (him)'; 'even' is an intensifier with no Greek basis

old: and as for the Jews, since he had resolved not even to consider them worthy of burial, to destroy them along with their infants for wild beasts as food for birds, he would make all of them equal to Athenians;
new: and as for the Jews, whom he had resolved not even to consider worthy of burial, but to destroy along with their infants for wild beasts as food for birds, he would make all of them equal to Athenians;
reason: ὡς διεγνώκει introduces what he had previously resolved about the Jews (not to deem them worthy of burial but to destroy them), not a cause of the new promise; 'since' wrongly makes it causal

old: And the king's letter to the nation was as follows: "King Antiochus to the senate of the Jews and to the other Jews, greetings.
new: And the king's letter to the nation was as follows: "King Antiochus to the council of elders of the Jews and to the other Jews, greetings.
reason: τῇ γερουσίᾳ: γερουσία is rendered 'council of elders' elsewhere in this book (1:10; 4:44)

old: And the Gentiles in Judea who had fled from Judas joined Nicanor in droves, thinking that the misfortunes and calamities of the Jews would be their own prosperity.
new: And the nations in Judea who had fled from Judas joined Nicanor in droves, thinking that the misfortunes and calamities of the Jews would be their own prosperity.
reason: ἔθνη is rendered "nations" in the OT convention and in this context (13:11; 15:8, 10).

old: Now when they heard of the advance of Nicanor and the assault of the Gentiles, sprinkling earth upon themselves, they implored Him who established His people forever and always with a manifestation comes to the aid of His own portion.
new: Now when they heard of the advance of Nicanor and the assault of the nations, sprinkling earth upon themselves, they implored Him who established His people forever and who always comes to the aid of His own portion with a manifestation.
reason: τῶν ἐθνῶν → "the nations" (cf. identical τὴν τῶν ἐθνῶν ἔφοδον in 15:8); the second participle ἀεὶ δὲ … ἀντιλαμβανόμενον needs its own "who" so it is not misread as "forever and always".

old: And having displayed the head of the vile Nicanor and the arm of the blasphemer, which he had stretched out against the holy house of the Almighty as he boasted arrogantly,
new: And having received the head of the vile Nicanor and the arm of the blasphemer, which he had stretched out against the holy house of the Almighty as he boasted arrogantly,
reason: This Greek reads ἐπιδεξάμενος (from ἐπιδέχομαι, "receive"), not ἐπιδείξας ("display") as in other editions.

new: The Greek text reads epidexamenos ('having received'), where other witnesses read epideixas ('having displayed').
reason: One-sentence explanation of the reading followed in the verse change.

old: And you will know that your offspring is numerous, and your children will be like all the vegetation of the field.
new: And you will know that your seed is numerous, and your children will be like all the vegetation of the field.
reason: τὸ σπέρμα σου → "your seed" per the OT convention (literal collective singular).

old: Or is it good to You if I act unjustly, that I should renounce the works of Your hands, while You have paid attention to the counsel of the ungodly?
new: Or is it good to You if I act unjustly, that You have renounced the works of Your hands, while You have paid attention to the counsel of the ungodly?
reason: ὅτι ἀπείπω is best read as aorist middle 2nd singular ("You renounced"; cf. middle ἀπείπατο in 6:14), parallel to προσέσχες; ὅτι with a first-person subjunctive is not a natural construction.

old: Both "if I act unjustly" and "that I should renounce" are first-person singular in the Greek, unlike the second-person verbs of the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
new: Greek "if I act unjustly" (adikeso) is first person, unlike the Hebrew; apeipo is read as second-person aorist middle ("You have renounced"), parallel to prosesches ("You have paid attention").
reason: The old note's claim that ἀπείπω is first person is doubtful for this Greek; the note is updated to match the verse.

old: Look, my eye has seen these things, and my ear has heard them.
new: "Look, my eye has seen these things, and my ear has heard them.
reason: Job's speech continues from 12:2 (closed at 12:25); the edition reopens the quotation at each new chapter (cf. 7:1, 10:1), but chapter 13 has no quotation marks.

old: which wears out like a wineskin, or like a moth-eaten garment.
new: which wears out like a wineskin, or like a moth-eaten garment."
reason: Closes the quotation opened at 13:1, following the edition's chapter-end convention (cf. 6:30, 9:35).

old: For a mortal born of a woman is short-lived and full of wrath,
new: "For a mortal born of a woman is short-lived and full of wrath,
reason: Job's speech continues through chapter 14; reopen the quotation (14:22, outside this part, needs the matching closing quote).

old: only his flesh feels pain, and his soul mourns.
new: only his flesh feels pain, and his soul mourns."
reason: Closes Job's speech opened at 14:1 (chapter-level quotation pattern).

old: For if I speak, I will not feel pain in the wound; and even if I keep silent, how much less will I be wounded?
new: For if I speak, I will not feel pain in the wound; and even if I keep silent, in what way will I be wounded less?
reason: τί ἔλαττον τρωθήσομαι asks "in what (way) will I be wounded less?"; English "how much less" reads as an a fortiori argument the Greek does not make.

old: For even if I remember, I am agitated, and pains grip my flesh.
new: For if I remember, I am agitated, and pains grip my flesh.
reason: ἐάν τε γὰρ μνησθῶ is a simple condition ("for if I remember"); "even" adds a concessive sense with no Greek basis.

old: Why do the ungodly live, and have they grown old even in wealth?
new: Why do the ungodly live, and why have they grown old even in wealth?
reason: διὰ τί governs both verbs (ζῶσιν ... πεπαλαίωνται δέ); "and have they grown old" wrongly turns the second clause into a separate yes/no question.

old: Their offspring is according to their desire, and their children are before their eyes.
new: Their seed is according to their desire, and their children are before their eyes.
reason: ὁ σπόρος is literally "seed"; the edition keeps the literal collective "seed" for descendants (cf. 5:25) rather than "offspring".

old: Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied and said:
new: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
reason: Same formula Ὑπολαβὼν δὲ ... λέγει is rendered "answered and said" everywhere else in Job (4:1, 15:1, 25:1, etc.).

old: For you kept taking pledges from your brothers for nothing, and you took away the clothing of the naked.
new: And you kept taking pledges from your brothers for nothing, and you took away the clothing of the naked.
reason: ἠνεχύραζες δέ is continuative δέ, not causal γάρ; "For" adds a causal link to v. 5 that the Greek lacks.

old: Then Job replied and said:
new: Then Job answered and said:
reason: Same formula Ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Ἰὼβ λέγει is rendered "answered and said" everywhere else in Job (16:1, 19:1, 21:1, 26:1).

old: surely, while my breath is still in me and the divine Spirit remains in my nostrils,
new: surely, while my breath is still in me and the divine spirit remains in my nostrils,
reason: πνεῦμα θεῖον "in my nostrils" parallels "my breath" (cf. lowercase "spirit in mortals" 32:8); capital "Spirit" silently decides the referent as the Holy Spirit.

old: This is the portion of an ungodly man from the Lord, and the possession of tyrants will come from the Almighty upon them.
new: This is the portion of an ungodly man from the Lord, and the possession of mighty ones will come from the Almighty upon them.
reason: δυναστῶν is rendered "mighty"/"mighty ones" elsewhere in Job (6:23, 15:5, 15:20, 29:12); "tyrants" adds a pejorative sense.

old: when I was exceedingly wooded, and my children were around me;
new: when I was exceedingly wooded, and my servants were around me;
reason: οἱ παῖδες follows the edition's OT convention παῖς → "servant", as in Job 1:15-17 (τοὺς παῖδας → "the servants").

old: If I smile at them, they will by no means believe it; and the light of my face did not fall away.
new: If I laugh at them, they will by no means believe it; and the light of my face did not fall away.
reason: γελάσω means "laugh" (as γελῶ in 19:7); "smile" follows familiar English Bibles rather than the Greek.

old: Yet I wept over every helpless person, and I groaned when I saw a man in distresses.
new: Yet I wept over every powerless person, and I groaned when I saw a man in distresses.
reason: ἀδυνάτῳ is rendered "powerless" throughout Job (5:15-16, 24:4, 24:6, 24:22, 29:16, 34:20, 36:19).

old: And the helpless did not fail to obtain whatever need they ever had, and I did not cause the eye of a widow to waste away;
new: And the powerless did not fail to obtain whatever need they ever had, and I did not cause the eye of a widow to waste away;
reason: ἀδύνατοι is rendered "powerless" throughout Job (24:4, 24:6, 29:16, 34:20, 36:19).

old: and if the helpless did not bless me, and their shoulders were warmed from the fleece of my lambs;
new: and if the powerless did not bless me, and their shoulders were warmed from the fleece of my lambs;
reason: ἀδύνατοι is rendered "powerless" throughout Job (24:4, 24:6, 29:16, 34:20, 36:19).

old: for I did not shrink from a throng of a multitude so as not to confess before them; and if I allowed a helpless person to go out my door with an empty bosom;
new: for I did not shrink from a throng of a multitude so as not to confess before them; and if I allowed a powerless person to go out my door with an empty bosom;
reason: ἀδύνατον is rendered "powerless" throughout Job (24:4, 24:6, 29:16, 34:20, 36:19).

old: Then Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite responded and said, "I am younger in time, while you are older; therefore I kept silent, fearing to declare to you my own knowledge.
new: Then Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said, "I am younger in time, while you are older; therefore I kept silent, fearing to declare to you my own knowledge.
reason: The formula ὑπολαβὼν δὲ ... εἶπεν is rendered "answered and said" elsewhere in Job (e.g. 34:1, 35:1 for Elihu).

old: Then Elihu responds and says:
new: Then Elihu answered and said:
reason: The identical formula Ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Ἐλιοῦς λέγει is rendered "Then Elihu answered and said" in 34:1 and 35:1, as are all the parallel speech introductions in Job.

old: It is the divine Spirit that made me, and the breath of the Almighty that teaches me.
new: It is the divine spirit that made me, and the breath of the Almighty that teaches me.
reason: πνεῦμα θεῖον as in Job 27:3

old: The Greek verb "has dealt falsely" (epseusato) is third-person singular referring to the Lord (unlike the first-person Hebrew), and "arrow" (belos) translates the Greek literally rather than "wound."
new: The Greek verb "has dealt falsely" (epseusato) is third-person singular referring to the Lord (unlike the first-person Hebrew), and "arrow" renders belos literally.
reason: Drop the comparison with other translations' "wound"; the note should describe only the Greek.

old: not having sinned nor acted impiously, or having shared a way with those who do lawless deeds, to walk with the impious?
new: not having sinned nor acted ungodly, or having shared a way with those who do lawless deeds, to walk with the ungodly?
reason: ἀσεβέω/ἀσεβής is rendered "act ungodly"/"ungodly" throughout Job (e.g. 10:2, 10:15, 36:12, 38:13); "impious" appears only in Elihu's ch. 34-35.

old: The Greek distinctively prefixes "not having sinned nor acted impiously" before "or having shared a way," softening Elihu's accusation against Job compared with the Hebrew text.
new: The Greek distinctively prefixes "not having sinned nor acted ungodly" before "or having shared a way," softening Elihu's accusation against Job compared with the Hebrew text.
reason: Keep the note's quotation in step with the revised verse wording for ἀσεβήσας.

old: Therefore, you of understanding heart, hear me: Far be it from me to act impiously before the Lord, and before the Almighty to disturb what is right;
new: Therefore, you of understanding heart, hear me: Far be it from me to act ungodly before the Lord, and before the Almighty to disturb what is right;
reason: ἀσεβῆσαι is rendered "act ungodly" elsewhere in Job (10:2, 10:15).

old: In the Greek text, Elihu declares "Far be it from me" to act impiously before the Lord, whereas the Hebrew reads "Far be it from God" to do wickedness.
new: In the Greek text, Elihu declares "Far be it from me" to act ungodly before the Lord, whereas the Hebrew reads "Far be it from God" to do wickedness.
reason: Keep the note in step with the revised verse wording for ἀσεβῆσαι.

old: Impious is the one who says to a king, 'You act lawlessly'; 'Most impious one,' to rulers,
new: Ungodly is the one who says to a king, 'You act lawlessly'; 'Most ungodly one,' to rulers,
reason: ἀσεβής / Ἀσεβέστατε: the book's established rendering of ἀσεβής is "ungodly".

old: And He extinguished the impious, and they are visible before Him,
new: And He extinguished the ungodly, and they are visible before Him,
reason: ἀσεβεῖς is "the ungodly" throughout Job (e.g. 18:5, 21:17, 36:12, 36:18).

old: Your impiety is for a man like yourself, and your righteousness is for a son of man.
new: Your ungodliness is for a man like yourself, and your righteousness is for a son of man.
reason: ἀσέβεια is rendered "ungodliness" in 36:18, in line with the book's "ungodly" for ἀσεβής.

old: Gird your waist like a man; I will ask, and you answer Me.
new: Gird your loins like a man; I will ask, and you answer Me.
reason: The identical phrase ζῶσαι ὥσπερ ἀνὴρ τὴν ὀσφύν σου is rendered "gird your loins like a man" in 40:7 (and ὀσφύς "loins" in 40:16).

old: The Greek refers to women's wisdom of weaving and knowledge of embroidery, diverging markedly from the obscure Hebrew terms often translated "inward parts" and "mind" (or "ibis" and "rooster").
new: The Greek refers to women's wisdom of weaving and knowledge of embroidery, diverging markedly from the obscure Hebrew terms, variously understood as "inward parts" and "mind" or as "ibis" and "rooster."
reason: Describe the Hebrew terms' disputed meanings rather than what translations often do.

old: And when a trumpet sounds, it says, 'Aha!' And from a distance it scents war with a leap and a shout.
new: And when a trumpet sounds, it says, 'Well done!' And from a distance it scents war with a leap and a shout.
reason: εὖγε means "well done/good" (rendered "Well done" in 31:29); "Aha" reproduces the Hebrew he'ah.

old: Then Job, responding, said to the Lord,
new: Then Job answered and said to the Lord,
reason: The identical Greek Ὑπολαβὼν δὲ Ἰὼβ λέγει τῷ κυρίῳ is rendered "Then Job answered and said to the Lord" in 42:1, matching the book's standard formula.

old: Will it make a covenant with you? And will you take it as a perpetual slave?
new: Will it make a covenant with you? And will you take it as a perpetual servant?
reason: δοῦλος is rendered "servant" in the OT under this edition's convention.

new: A psalm for David, when he was fleeing from the presence of Absalom his son.

old: In the Greek grammar, "His face" (to prosōpon autou) is unmistakably the nominative subject and "uprightness" (euthytēta) the accusative object, whereas many translations of the Hebrew make the upright the subject who see God's face.
new: In the Greek, "uprightness" (euthytēta) is accusative, so "His face" (to prosōpon autou) is the subject; the Hebrew is commonly read with the upright as those who see His face.
reason: Removes the claim about what other translations do and states the grammatical point (εὐθύτητα is unambiguously accusative, so neuter πρόσωπον is the subject) neutrally.

old: My God, His way is blameless; the oracles of the Lord are refined by fire; He is a protector of all who hope in Him.
new: My God, His way is blameless; the utterances of the Lord are refined by fire; He is a protector of all who hope in Him.
reason: τὰ λόγια Κυρίου ... πεπυρωμένα is the same phrase rendered "the utterances of the Lord ... refined by fire" in 11:7; "oracles" breaks that consistency.

old: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text (which shifts to third person, "the LORD in His wrath will swallow them up"), the Septuagint addresses the Lord directly in the vocative ("Lord, in Your anger You will throw them into confusion"), showing that 20:9-14 are addressed to God.
new: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text (which shifts to the third person, "the Lord in His wrath will swallow them up"), the Septuagint addresses the Lord directly in the vocative ("Lord, in Your anger You will throw them into confusion").
reason: House style forbids "LORD" in capitals; the added inference that all of 20:9-14 is addressed to God goes beyond what the vocative in v. 10 shows (v. 9 is ambiguous).

new: You who fear the Lord, praise Him; all the seed of Jacob, glorify Him; let all the seed of Israel fear Him.
reason: σπέρμα is rendered with the literal collective "seed" in this edition's OT (cf. 17:51, 20:11), not "offspring".

old: And my offspring will serve Him; the coming generation will be declared to the Lord,
new: And my seed will serve Him; the coming generation will be declared to the Lord,
reason: τὸ σπέρμα μου → "my seed" per the edition's OT convention for σπέρμα.

old: A Psalm of David. The Lord shepherds me, and nothing will be lacking to me.
new: A psalm of David. The Lord shepherds me, and nothing will be lacking to me.
reason: Ψαλμός in superscriptions is lowercase "psalm" everywhere else in the edition (e.g. 23:1, 24:1).

old: This is Psalm 23 in Hebrew and most English Bibles; the Greek (Septuagint) numbers it Psalm 22. ποιμαίνει ("shepherds") is a present-tense verb, and οὐδέν με ὑστερήσει has "nothing" as its subject, "nothing will be lacking to me."
new: This is Psalm 23 in the Hebrew numbering; the Greek (Septuagint) numbers it Psalm 22. ποιμαίνει ("shepherds") is a present-tense verb, and οὐδέν με ὑστερήσει has "nothing" as its subject, "nothing will be lacking to me."
reason: Notes should not make claims about what other translations do; the numbering fact is kept with reference to the Hebrew only.

old: A psalm of David. The Lord shepherds me, and nothing will be lacking to me.
new: A psalm for David. The Lord shepherds me, and nothing will be lacking to me.
reason: Psalm heading τῷ Δαυίδ → "for David" (Psalter-wide)

new: Lord, I have loved the beauty of Your house and the place of the tent of Your glory.
reason: σκήνωμα is rendered "tent" elsewhere in these Psalms (14:1 "Your tent", 18:6 "His tent"), as is σκηνή (26:5-6, 30:21).

old: Of David. To You, Lord, I have cried out; my God, do not keep silent toward me, so that You never keep silent toward me and I become like those who go down into a pit.
new: Of David. To You, Lord, I have cried out; my God, do not keep silent toward me, lest You keep silent toward me and I become like those who go down into a pit.
reason: μή ποτε governs both clauses ("lest You keep silent ... and I become like"); "so that You never keep silent ... and I become like" makes becoming like those who go down to the pit a purpose.

old: The Lord will inhabit the flood; and the Lord will sit as king forever.
new: The Lord will settle the flood; and the Lord will sit as king forever.
reason: κατοικιεῖ is the future of κατοικίζω "settle, cause to be inhabited" (rendered "settled" in 4:9), not of κατοικέω "inhabit" (future κατοικήσει).

old: Greek katoikiei is a future verb meaning "will inhabit" or "will settle," contrasting with the Hebrew past tense "sat enthroned."
new: Greek katoikiei is the future of katoikizō ("settle," "cause to be inhabited," as in 4:9), contrasting with the Hebrew past tense "sat enthroned."
reason: κατοικιεῖ is from causative κατοικίζω, not κατοικέω; "will inhabit" misidentifies the verb.

old: By the word of the Lord the heavens were made firm, and by the breath of His mouth all their host.
new: By the word of the Lord the heavens were made firm, and by the breath of His mouth all their power.
reason: πᾶσα ἡ δύναμις αὐτῶν is "all their power"; "host" follows the Hebrew (cf. the edition's "Lord of powers" for κύριος τῶν δυνάμεων, 23:10).

old: Pour out a sword and close off the way against those who pursue me; say to my soul, "I am your salvation."

reason: σύνκλεισον ἐξ ἐναντίας has no word for "the way"; "close off the way" follows the Hebrew-based English tradition rather than this Greek.

old: The Greek literally reads "Pour out a sword" (ἔκχεον ῥομφαίαν) and "close off" (σύνκλεισον), reflecting the Septuagint's distinct rendering of the Hebrew weaponry and blocking imagery.
new: The Greek literally reads "Pour out a sword" (ἔκχεον ῥομφαίαν) and "close in" (σύνκλεισον), reflecting the Septuagint's distinct rendering of the Hebrew weaponry and blocking imagery.
reason: Keeps the note in step with the corrected verse wording.

new: The nominative ὁ θεός is read here as a vocative ('God') addressing the royal figure; pronouns in vv. 7-8 are therefore capitalized. Verses 7-8 are quoted in Hebrews 1:8-9.
reason: The note grounded the capitalization in a Christological reading ("quoted of Christ ... accordingly capitalized"); restated neutrally on the Greek vocative, keeping the factual Hebrews reference.

old: For this is our God forever and to the age of the age.

old: The Greek text ends at 'to the age of the age,' without the concluding clause ('He will guide us...') present in some witnesses and the Hebrew Masoretic Text.

reason: Updated to match the corrected verse wording; the added clause in the other Greek witnesses is αὐτὸς ποιμανεῖ ἡμᾶς ("He will shepherd us"), not "guide".
