reason: λοιμοὶ ἀπὸ ἐθνῶν is rendered "pestilent ones from the nations" in 28:7 and 30:11 (and "pestilent foreigners from the nations" in 31:12); "scourges" is an isolated variant.

old: and I will fill hills and your ravines with those struck down, and in all your plains those fatally wounded by the sword will fall in you.
new: and I will fill hills and your ravines with the wounded, and in all your plains those wounded by the sword will fall in you.
reason: τετραυματισμένοι μαχαίρᾳ is simply "wounded by the sword" (as in 28:23); "fatally" has no Greek basis, and τῶν τραυματιῶν is rendered "the wounded" throughout these chapters.

old: therefore, mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord: This is what the Lord says to the mountains and to the hills and to the ravines and to the torrents and to the desolated and ruined places and to the forsaken cities, and they have become a plunder and a trampling for the remaining nations all around:
new: therefore, mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord: Thus says the Lord to the mountains and to the hills and to the ravines and to the torrents and to the desolated and ruined places and to the forsaken cities, and they have become a plunder and a trampling for the remaining nations all around:
reason: τάδε λέγει → "Thus says …" (OT-wide)

old: Therefore prophesy concerning the land of Israel, and say to the mountains and to the hills and to the ravines and to the valleys, "This is what the Lord says: Look, I have spoken in My jealousy and in My wrath, because you have borne the reproaches of nations.
new: Therefore prophesy concerning the land of Israel, and say to the mountains and to the hills and to the ravines and to the valleys, "Thus says the Lord: Look, I have spoken in My jealousy and in My wrath, because you have borne the reproaches of nations.
reason: τάδε λέγει → "Thus says …" (OT-wide)

old: This is what the Lord, the Lord says: "Because they said to you, 'You are one who devours people, and you have become bereaved by your nation,'
new: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: "Because they said to you, 'You are one who devours people, and you have become bereaved by your nation,'
reason: τάδε λέγει is "Thus says" throughout the OT prophets (218 occurrences); these were missed by the formula pass.

old: Therefore say to the house of Israel, 'This is what the Lord says: It is not for you that I am acting, house of Israel, but rather for the sake of My holy name, which you profaned among the nations where you went.
new: Therefore say to the house of Israel, 'Thus says the Lord: It is not for you that I am acting, house of Israel, but rather for the sake of My holy name, which you profaned among the nations where you went.
reason: τάδε λέγει → "Thus says …" (OT-wide)

old: This is what Adonai the Lord says: "On the day when I cleanse you from all your lawless deeds, I will also settle the cities, and desolate places will be built;
new: Thus says Adonai the Lord: "On the day when I cleanse you from all your lawless deeds, I will also settle the cities, and desolate places will be built;
reason: τάδε λέγει → "Thus says …" (OT-wide)

old: This is what Adonai the Lord says: "Yet for this I will be sought by the house of Israel, to do it for them: I will multiply them with people like sheep,
new: Thus says Adonai the Lord: "Yet for this I will be sought by the house of Israel, to do it for them: I will multiply them with people like sheep,
reason: τάδε λέγει → "Thus says …" (OT-wide)

old: This is what the Lord says to these bones: Look, I am bringing a spirit of life into you,
new: Thus says the Lord to these bones: Look, I am bringing a spirit of life into you,
reason: τάδε λέγει → "Thus says …" (OT-wide)

old: And He said to me, "Prophesy to the spirit; prophesy, son of man, and say to the spirit, 'This is what the Lord says: Come from the four winds and breathe into these dead ones, and let them live.'"
new: And He said to me, "Prophesy to the spirit; prophesy, son of man, and say to the spirit, 'Thus says the Lord: Come from the four winds and breathe into these dead ones, and let them live.'"
reason: τάδε λέγει → "Thus says …" (OT-wide)

old: Therefore prophesy and say, 'This is what the Lord says: Look, I am opening your tombs, and I will bring you up out of your tombs, and I will bring you into the land of Israel,
new: Therefore prophesy and say, 'Thus says the Lord: Look, I am opening your tombs, and I will bring you up out of your tombs, and I will bring you into the land of Israel,
reason: τάδε λέγει → "Thus says …" (OT-wide)

old: then you will say to them, 'This is what the Lord says: Look, I will take the tribe of Joseph, which is by the hand of Ephraim, and the tribes of Israel that are joined to him, and I will place them upon the tribe of Judah, and they will become one rod in the hand of Judah.'
new: then you will say to them, 'Thus says the Lord: Look, I will take the tribe of Joseph, which is by the hand of Ephraim, and the tribes of Israel that are joined to him, and I will place them upon the tribe of Judah, and they will become one rod in the hand of Judah.'
reason: τάδε λέγει → "Thus says …" (OT-wide)

old: And he brought me into the porch of the house. And he measured the jamb of the porch, five cubits in width on this side and five cubits on that side, and the breadth of the doorway was fourteen cubits, and the side walls of the door of the porch were three cubits on this side and three cubits on that side.
new: And he brought me into the porch of the house. And he measured the jamb of the porch, five cubits in width on this side and five cubits on that side, and the breadth of the doorway was fourteen cubits, and the shoulders of the door of the porch were three cubits on this side and three cubits on that side.
reason: ἐπωμίδες is rendered "shoulders" in 41:2-3 for the same architectural element; "side walls" breaks the pattern.

old: And he brought me into the temple, in which he measured the vestibule, six cubits in width on one side,
new: And he brought me into the temple, in which he measured the porch, six cubits in width on one side,
reason: αἰλάμ is rendered "porch" throughout ch. 40 (see note at 40:7), while "vestibule" is reserved for αἰλαμμών; using "vestibule" here conflates the two Greek terms.

old: Greek uses the Hebrew architectural loanword ailam ("vestibule" or "porch") here and in vv. 2, 15, and 25-26, where the Hebrew of v. 1 refers to pilasters or jambs.
new: Greek uses the Hebrew architectural loanword ailam ("porch") here and in vv. 2, 15, and 25-26, where the Hebrew of v. 1 refers to pilasters or jambs.
reason: Note aligned with the consistent rendering of αἰλάμ as "porch" (αἰλαμμών = "vestibule").

old: and six cubits the breadth of the vestibule on the other side, and the breadth of the gateway was ten cubits, and the shoulders of the gateway were five cubits on one side and five cubits on the other side. And he measured its length, forty cubits, and the breadth, twenty cubits.
new: and six cubits the breadth of the porch on the other side, and the breadth of the gateway was ten cubits, and the shoulders of the gateway were five cubits on one side and five cubits on the other side. And he measured its length, forty cubits, and the breadth, twenty cubits.
reason: τοῦ αἰλάμ: same term rendered "porch" in ch. 40; "vestibule" is the edition's word for αἰλαμμών.

old: And he measured the length of the partition in front of the remaining space of the parts behind that house, and the remaining spaces on one side and on the other, a hundred cubits in length. And the temple and the corners and the outer vestibule were paneled.
new: And he measured the length of the partition in front of the remaining space of the parts behind that house, and the remaining spaces on one side and on the other, a hundred cubits in length. And the temple and the corners and the outer porch were paneled.
reason: τὸ αἰλὰμ τὸ ἐξώτερον: αἰλάμ is "porch" in this edition (ch. 40), not "vestibule" (= αἰλαμμών).

old: And there was carving on them, and on the doors of the temple were cherubim and palm trees according to the carving of the sanctuary, and sturdy timbers in front of the vestibule on the outside,
new: And there was carving on them, and on the doors of the temple were cherubim and palm trees according to the carving of the sanctuary, and sturdy timbers in front of the porch on the outside,
reason: τοῦ αἰλάμ is the same structure called "the porch of the house" in 40:48-49.

old: and hidden windows. And he measured on one side and on the other, to the roofings of the vestibule, and the side rooms of the house were yoked together.
new: and hidden windows. And he measured on one side and on the other, to the roofings of the porch, and the side rooms of the house were yoked together.
reason: τοῦ αἰλάμ rendered "porch" as elsewhere in the temple vision; "vestibule" belongs to αἰλαμμών.

old: And you shall give to the priests, the Levites, who are from the offspring of Zadok, who draw near to Me, says the Lord God, to minister to Me, a young bull from the herd for a sin offering.
new: And you shall give to the priests, the Levites, who are from the seed of Zadok, who draw near to Me, says the Lord God, to minister to Me, a young bull from the herd for a sin offering.
reason: ἐκ τοῦ σπέρματος: the edition's OT convention renders σπέρμα (descendants) as "seed", not "offspring".

old: For the ruler, he shall sit in it to eat bread before the Lord; he shall enter by the way of the ailam of the gate, and by its way he shall go out."
new: For the ruler, he shall sit in it to eat bread before the Lord; he shall enter by the way of the porch of the gate, and by its way he shall go out."
reason: αἰλάμ is translated "porch" throughout the temple vision (e.g. 40:6-16, 40:48-49); leaving it untranslated here is inconsistent.

old: "Ailam" (αἰλάμ) is a Greek transliteration of the Hebrew architectural term for the porch or vestibule of the gate.
new: "Porch" renders αἰλάμ (ailam), a Greek transliteration of the Hebrew architectural term for the porch of the gate.
reason: Note adjusted to match the verse now translating αἰλάμ as "porch".

old: And you shall say to the rebellious house, to the house of Israel, 'Thus says the Lord God: Let it be enough for you from all your lawless deeds, house of Israel,
new: And you shall say to the provoking house, to the house of Israel, 'Thus says the Lord God: Let it be enough for you from all your lawless deeds, house of Israel,
reason: οἶκος ὁ παραπικραίνων → "provoking house" (as Ezek 2-3, 12)

old: And they shall not take for themselves as a wife a widow or a divorced woman, but only a virgin from the offspring of Israel; yet a widow, if she is from a priest, they may take.
new: And they shall not take for themselves as a wife a widow or a divorced woman, but only a virgin from the seed of Israel; yet a widow, if she is from a priest, they may take.
reason: ἐκ τοῦ σπέρματος Ἰσραήλ: OT convention renders σπέρμα as "seed", not "offspring".

old: And the ruler shall enter by the way of the vestibule of the inner gate and stand at the doorway of the gate, and the priests shall prepare his burnt offerings and his deliverance offerings.
new: And the ruler shall enter by the way of the porch of the inner gate and stand at the doorway of the gate, and the priests shall prepare his burnt offerings and his deliverance offerings.
reason: τοῦ αἰλάμ is rendered "porch" elsewhere in the vision; "vestibule" is the edition's word for the different term αἰλαμμών.

old: The Greek transliterates Hebrew ulam ("vestibule") as ailam (also v. 8) and specifies "the inner gate" where the Hebrew MT reads "from outside."
new: The Greek transliterates Hebrew ulam ("porch") as ailam (also v. 8) and specifies "the inner gate" where the Hebrew MT reads "from outside."
reason: Note aligned with the verse's rendering "porch" for αἰλάμ.

old: And when the ruler enters, he shall enter by the way of the vestibule of the gate, and by the way of the gate he shall go out.
new: And when the ruler enters, he shall enter by the way of the porch of the gate, and by the way of the gate he shall go out.
reason: τοῦ αἰλάμ: same term and sense as 44:3 and ch. 40, rendered "porch".

old: To these shall belong the firstfruit of the holy places, to the priests: toward the north twenty-five thousand, and toward the sea ten thousand, and toward the south twenty-five thousand; and the mountain of the holy places shall be in the midst of it;
new: Of these shall be the firstfruit of the holy places for the priests: toward the north twenty-five thousand, and toward the sea ten thousand, and toward the south twenty-five thousand; and the mountain of the holy places shall be in the midst of it;
reason: τούτων is genitive ("of these"), not a dative recipient; the recipients are τοῖς ἱερεῦσιν ("for the priests").

old: And the remainder shall belong to the leader, on this side and on that side, from the firstfruits of the holy place and to the possession of the city, along twenty-five thousand in length as far as the borders toward the east, and toward the sea along twenty-five thousand as far as the borders toward the sea, adjacent to the portions of the leader; and the firstfruit of the holy places and the sanctuary of the house shall be in the midst of it.
new: And the remainder shall belong to the ruler, on this side and on that side, from the firstfruits of the holy place and to the possession of the city, along twenty-five thousand in length as far as the borders toward the east, and toward the sea along twenty-five thousand as far as the borders toward the sea, adjacent to the portions of the ruler; and the firstfruit of the holy places and the sanctuary of the house shall be in the midst of it.
reason: ὁ ἀφηγούμενος is rendered "ruler" throughout chs. 45-46 (45:8-22; 46:2-18).

old: And from the Levites, from the possession of the city, it shall be in the midst of the leaders, between the borders of Judah and the borders of Benjamin; it shall belong to the leaders.
new: And from the Levites, from the possession of the city, it shall be in the midst of the rulers, between the borders of Judah and the borders of Benjamin; it shall belong to the rulers.
reason: τῶν ἀφηγουμένων: same term rendered "ruler(s)" in 45:8-46:18.

old: Preserves trailing comma continuing into v. 4.
new: φορθομμείν transliterates the Hebrew partemim ("nobles," a Persian loanword); it is rendered by its meaning.
reason: The old note was an editorial remark about punctuation, not about the Greek; replaced with a factual note on the transliteration φορθομμείν that the English renders by meaning.

old: And the chief eunuch gave names to them: to Daniel, Belteshazzar; and to Hananiah, Shadrach; and to Mishael, Meshach; and to Azariah, Abednego.
new: And the chief eunuch gave names to them: to Daniel, Baltasar; and to Hananiah, Shadrach; and to Mishael, Meshach; and to Azariah, Abednego.
reason: Βαλτασάρ is rendered "Baltasar" in 4:8-9, 4:18-19 and 5:12 (and for the king in ch. 5); the Greek has one form for both names, so the Greek form already used is kept throughout instead of the Hebrew-based Belteshazzar.

old: And the king answered and said to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, "Are you able to report to me the dream that I saw and its interpretation?"
new: And the king answered and said to Daniel, whose name was Baltasar, "Are you able to report to me the dream that I saw and its interpretation?"
reason: Same Greek Βαλτασάρ as 4:8-9, 4:18-19, 5:12, where the edition uses the Greek form "Baltasar"; unified to the Greek form.

old: The Greek spells the name Βαλτασάρ (Baltasar). The standard English form Belteshazzar, Daniel's Babylonian name, is used.
new: Βαλτασάρ (Baltasar) is the Greek form of Daniel's Babylonian name (Hebrew/Aramaic Belteshazzar); this Greek text uses the same form for King Belshazzar (5:1; 7:1; 8:1).
reason: Note updated to match the unified Greek-form rendering "Baltasar" and to state the Greek fact neutrally.

old: because the king's word was urgent, and the furnace was heated exceedingly.
new: because the king's word prevailed, and the furnace was heated exceedingly.
reason: ὑπερίσχυεν means "prevailed, was overpowering"; "was urgent" follows the Aramaic (maḥṣephah) rather than the Greek.

old: Verses 24–47 (continuing further in the chapter) form part of the Greek-only addition containing the Prayer of Azariah and the expanded narrative of the furnace.
new: Verses 24–90 are the Greek-only addition (the Prayer of Azariah, the expanded narrative of the furnace, and the Song of the Three); verse 91 corresponds to Aramaic 3:24.
reason: The old note gave the extent of the addition as vv. 24–47; in this numbering the addition runs through v. 90 and v. 91 resumes the Aramaic text.

old: and the flame spread out above the furnace for forty-nine cubits,
new: And the flame spread out above the furnace for forty-nine cubits,
reason: 3:46 ends with a full stop, so the new sentence must be capitalized.

old: How great and mighty they are! His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom; His authority is from generation to generation.
new: How great and mighty they are! His kingdom is an eternal kingdom; His authority is from generation to generation.
reason: βασιλεία αἰώνιος is "eternal kingdom" in 7:27; αἰώνιος → "eternal" is the edition's rendering.

old: By the decree of a watcher is the word, and a saying of holy ones is the demand, so that the living may know that the Most High is Lord of the kingdom of humans, and to whomever He sees fit He will give it, and He will set up over it the most despised of humans."
new: By the decree of a watcher is the word, and a saying of holy ones is the demand, so that the living may know that the Most High is Lord of the kingdom of humans, and to whomever He sees fit He will give it, and He will set up over it one despised by humans."
reason: ἐξουδένημα ἀνθρώπων is "an object of contempt among humans"; the superlative "most despised" has no Greek basis (it reflects the Aramaic "lowliest of men").

old: And after the end of the days, I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted up my eyes to heaven, and my understanding returned to me, and I blessed the Most High, and I praised and glorified Him who lives forever, because His authority is an everlasting authority and His kingdom is from generation to generation.
new: And after the end of the days, I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted up my eyes to heaven, and my understanding returned to me, and I blessed the Most High, and I praised and glorified Him who lives forever, because His authority is an eternal authority and His kingdom is from generation to generation.
reason: ἐξουσία αἰώνιος is "eternal authority" in 7:14; αἰώνιος → "eternal" is the edition's rendering.

old: And all those who dwell on the earth were accounted as nothing; and He acts according to His will in the power of heaven and in the habitation of the earth, and there is no one who can resist His hand and say to Him, "What have You done?"
new: And all those who dwell on the earth were accounted as nothing; and He acts according to His will in the host of heaven and in the habitation of the earth, and there is no one who can resist His hand and say to Him, "What have You done?"
reason: ἡ δύναμις τοῦ οὐρανοῦ is "the host of heaven" in 8:10, and the sense (heavenly host parallel to the earth's inhabitants) is the same here.

old: At that very time my understanding returned to me, and I came into the honor of my kingdom; and my appearance returned to me, and my rulers and my nobles sought me out, and I was firmly established over my kingdom, and surpassing greatness was added to me.
new: At that very time my understanding returned to me, and I came into the honor of my kingdom; and my appearance returned to me, and my potentates and my nobles sought me out, and I was firmly established over my kingdom, and surpassing greatness was added to me.
reason: τύραννοι is rendered "potentates" in 3:2-3; "rulers" is used for ἄρχοντες.

old: Now therefore, I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and exalt and glorify the King of heaven, because all His works are true and His paths are justice, and all those who walk in pride He is able to humble.
new: Now therefore, I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and highly exalt and glorify the King of heaven, because all His works are true and His paths are justice, and all those who walk in pride He is able to humble.
reason: ὑπερυψῶ is the compound rendered "highly exalt" throughout 3:52-90; plain "exalt" drops the ὑπερ- intensive.

old: And Daniel said before the king, "Let your gifts be yours, and give the reward of your house to another; yet I will read the writing and make known its interpretation to you. And this is the writing that has been inscribed: 'Mane, Thekel, Phares.'
new: And Daniel said before the king, "Let your gifts be yours, and give the reward of your house to another; yet I will read the writing and make known its interpretation to you.
reason: The Greek of 5:17 ends at γνωρίσω σοι; the sentence about the inscription is 5:25 (now present as its own verse), so it is duplicated here.

old: Greek reads three inscribed words ("Mane, Thekel, Phares") rather than the Aramaic MT's four ("Mene, Mene, Tekel, Upharsin"); verses 5:14-15, 5:18-22, and 5:24-25 of the MT are absent from this Greek text.
reason: The note belongs to 5:25 and is now false: 5:14-15, 5:18-22 and 5:24-25 are present in this Greek text as additional verses.

old: And when his heart was lifted up and his spirit grew hardened to act arrogantly, he was brought down from the throne of the kingdom, and the honor was taken away from him,
new: And when his heart was lifted up and his spirit was strengthened to act arrogantly, he was brought down from the throne of the kingdom, and the honor was taken away from him,
reason: ἐκραταιώθη is "was strengthened"; "grew hardened" follows the Aramaic teqiphat.

old: and he was driven away from human beings, and his heart was given to be with the wild beasts, and his dwelling was with wild donkeys, and they fed him grass like an ox, and his body was drenched with the dew of heaven, until he knew that the Most High God rules over the kingdom of human beings, and to whomever He chooses, He will give it.
new: and he was driven away from human beings, and his heart was given to be with the wild beasts, and his dwelling was with wild donkeys, and they fed him grass like an ox, and his body was drenched with the dew of heaven, until he knew that the Most High God rules over the kingdom of human beings, and to whomever He sees fit, He will give it.
reason: ᾧ ἂν δόξῃ δώσει αὐτήν is rendered "to whomever He sees fit He will give it" in 4:17, 4:25 and 4:32.

old: And you therefore, his son Baltasar, have not humbled your heart before God; did you not know all these things?
new: And you therefore, his son Baltasar, have not humbled your heart before God; you did not know all these things.
reason: The critical text punctuates οὐ πάντα ταῦτα ἔγνως with a raised dot (it marks questions with ;), so it is a statement, not a question.

old: The Greek reads the rhetorical question 'did you not know all these things?' (ou panta tauta egnos) where the Aramaic reads 'even though you knew all this.'
new: This Greek text punctuates οὐ πάντα ταῦτα ἔγνως as a statement, "you did not know all these things"; the Aramaic reads "even though you knew all this."
reason: The old note called the clause a question, which is false for this text's punctuation.

old: This verse has no separate place in the Saints.Bible numbering, so it is shown with the other additional verses after 5:23.
new: This verse has no separate place in the Saints.Bible numbering, so it is shown with the other additional verses after 5:23. The Greek has three inscribed words (Mane, Thekel, Phares), where the Aramaic has four (Mene, Mene, Tekel, Upharsin).
reason: Moves the accurate textual fact from the removed 5:17 note to the verse it concerns.

old: All the commanders and satraps, high officials and district governors over your kingdom have consulted together to establish a royal statute and to enforce an injunction, that whoever asks a petition from any god or man for thirty days except from you, O king, will be thrown into the den of lions.
new: All the commanders and satraps, chief magistrates and district governors over your kingdom have consulted together to establish a royal statute and to enforce an injunction, that whoever asks a petition from any god or man for thirty days except from you, O king, will be thrown into the den of lions.
reason: ὕπατοι is rendered "chief magistrates" in 3:2-3.

old: The Greek text moves directly from the king's distress and effort to rescue Daniel in 6:15 to his command in 6:17, omitting the phrase "until sunset" and verse 16 (the conspirators' second appeal in the Aramaic tradition).
new: This Greek text lacks the Aramaic phrase "until the going down of the sun."
reason: The old note claimed the Greek omits verse 16, but 6:16 is present in this Greek text (shown as an additional verse).

old: In the third year of Belshazzar king of the Chaldeans, Daniel saw a dream and the visions of his head upon his bed, and he wrote down his dream.
new: In the third year of Baltasar king of the Chaldeans, Daniel saw a dream and the visions of his head upon his bed, and he wrote down his dream.
reason: Βαλτασάρ (the king) is rendered "Baltasar" throughout ch. 5; the Greek form is kept consistently.

old: The Greek text dates this vision to the "third" year of Belshazzar "king of the Chaldeans," whereas the Aramaic tradition reads the "first" year of Belshazzar "king of Babylon" and includes "the sum of the matters" before he wrote the dream.
new: The Greek text dates this vision to the "third" year of Baltasar "king of the Chaldeans," whereas the Aramaic reads the "first" year of Belshazzar "king of Babylon" and adds a reference to "the sum of the matters."
reason: Note updated for the Greek-form name; the Aramaic "sum of the matters" follows, not precedes, the writing of the dream, so the wording is made neutral.

old: And to Him was given dominion and honor and kingdom, and all the peoples, tribes, and languages serve Him; His authority is an eternal authority that will not pass away, and His kingdom will not be destroyed.
new: And to him was given dominion and honor and kingdom, and all the peoples, tribes, and languages serve him; his authority is an eternal authority that will not pass away, and his kingdom will not be destroyed.
reason: The pronouns refer to "one like a son of man" (7:13, kept lowercase by the edition), whose identity is disputed; capitalization silently decides the referent, so αὐτῷ/αὐτοῦ are left lowercase.

old: In the third year of the reign of Belshazzar the king, a vision appeared to me—I, Daniel—after the one that appeared to me at the beginning.
new: In the third year of the reign of Baltasar the king, a vision appeared to me—I, Daniel—after the one that appeared to me at the beginning.
reason: Βαλτασάρ (the king) is rendered "Baltasar" throughout ch. 5; the Greek form is kept consistently.

old: At the beginning of your supplication a word went out, and I have come to tell you, because you are a man greatly desired; so consider the message and understand the vision.
new: At the beginning of your supplication a word went out, and I have come to tell you, because you are a man of delight; so consider the message and understand the vision.
reason: ἀνὴρ ἐπιθυμιῶν is "man of delight" in 10:11 and 10:19; "greatly" has no Greek basis.

old: The Greek contains seven infinitive purpose clauses (adding "and to blot out the iniquities") rather than six as in Hebrew, and reads singular "prophet" (προφήτην) rather than "prophecy."
new: The Greek contains seven infinitive purpose clauses (adding "and to blot out the iniquities") rather than six as in Hebrew.
reason: The removed clause contrasted Greek "prophet" with "prophecy," but the Hebrew also reads "prophet" (nabi); the contrast is with English translations, not the Hebrew.

old: In the third year of Cyrus king of the Persians, a word was revealed to Daniel, whose name was called Belteshazzar; and the word is true, and great power and understanding were given to him in the vision.
new: In the third year of Cyrus king of the Persians, a word was revealed to Daniel, whose name was called Baltasar; and the word is true, and great power and understanding were given to him in the vision.
reason: Βαλτασάρ is rendered "Baltasar" in 4:8-9, 4:18-19, 5:12; the Greek form is kept consistently (the existing note already explains the Greek form).

old: And I lifted up my eyes and looked, and look, one man clothed in baddin, and his waist was girded with gold of Uphaz,
new: And I lifted up my eyes and looked, and look, one man clothed in linen, and his waist was girded with gold of Uphaz,
reason: The same βαδδείν is rendered "linen" in 12:6 and 12:7.

old: "baddin" is an untranslated Greek transliteration of Hebrew baddim, meaning linen garments.

reason: Trims the survey of interpretive positions on the coming of the Son of Man, which is commentary rather than explanation of the Greek.

old: For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John;
new: For all the prophets and the Law prophesied until John;
reason: ὁ νόμος (the Mosaic Law) is capitalized "the Law" elsewhere in the edition (5:17-18, 7:12, 12:5).

old: "Works" (ἔργων) forms an intentional link back to "the works of the Christ" in 11:2; some manuscripts, harmonizing with Luke 7:35, read "children" (τέκνων).
new: "Works" (ἔργων) is the same word as in "the works of the Christ" (11:2); some manuscripts, harmonizing with Luke 7:35, read "children" (τέκνων).
reason: "Forms an intentional link" asserts authorial intent; restated as a factual observation about the shared word.

old: All things were delivered to Me by My Father, and no one fully knows the Son except the Father, nor does anyone fully know the Father except the Son and the one to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him.
new: All things were delivered to Me by My Father, and no one fully knows the Son except the Father, nor does anyone fully know the Father except the Son and anyone to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him.
reason: ᾧ ἐὰν βούληται is indefinite ("to whomever"); "the one to whom" wrongly implies a specific person.

old: Take up My yoke upon you and learn from Me, because I am meek and humble of heart, and you will find rest for your souls;
new: Take up My yoke upon you and learn from Me, because I am gentle and humble of heart, and you will find rest for your souls;
reason: πραΰς is rendered "gentle" in 5:5 (οἱ πραεῖς) and its cognate "gentleness" throughout the edition.

old: The Greek adjective meizon ("something greater") is neuter rather than masculine, pointing broadly to the greater reality of Jesus's messianic ministry and kingdom; the same neuter construction recurs with pleion in 12:41-42.
new: The Greek adjective meizon ("something greater") is neuter rather than masculine; the same neuter construction recurs with pleion in 12:41-42.
reason: Removes the interpretive gloss "pointing broadly to the greater reality of Jesus's messianic ministry and kingdom"; keeps the grammatical fact.

old: But if you had known what it means, 'I want mercy and not sacrifice,' you would not have condemned the guiltless.
new: But if you had known what it means, 'I desire mercy and not sacrifice,' you would not have condemned the guiltless.
reason: The identical quotation Ἔλεος θέλω καὶ οὐ θυσίαν is rendered "I desire mercy and not sacrifice" in 9:13.

old: Jesus, knowing this, withdrew from there. Many followed Him, and He healed them all,
new: But Jesus, knowing this, withdrew from there. Many followed Him, and He healed them all,
reason: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς: the adversative δέ sets Jesus' response against the Pharisees' plot in v. 14 and was not represented.

old: Matthew's quotation of Isaiah 42:3 renders the closing phrase as "to victory" (eis nikos), differing from the standard Hebrew ("in truth") and Septuagint wording to highlight the triumphant outcome of the Servant's justice.
new: Matthew's quotation of Isaiah 42:3 has "to victory" (eis nikos) in the closing phrase, where the Hebrew and the Septuagint have "in/to truth."
reason: Removes the interpretive claim about Matthew's purpose ("to highlight the triumphant outcome..."); keeps the factual textual comparison.

old: and he said to his servants, "This is John the Baptist; he himself has been raised from the dead, and for this reason the miraculous powers are working in him."
new: and he said to his servants, "This is John the Baptist; he himself has been raised from the dead, and for this reason the powers are working in him."
reason: αἱ δυνάμεις is simply "the powers"; "miraculous" is an explanatory addition (the edition has "these powers" in Mark 6:14).

old: The phrase 'it is I' literally translates Greek 'ego eimi' ('I am'), which serves both as a normal self-identification and as an echo of God's self-revelation in the Greek Old Testament (e.g., Exodus 3:14; Isaiah 43:10).
new: Greek egō eimi, literally "I am," is used here as an ordinary self-identification, "it is I."
reason: Removes the theological assertion that the phrase echoes God's self-revelation; keeps the lexical explanation.

old: and saying, "Lord, have mercy on my son, because he has seizures and suffers badly; for often he falls into the fire and often into the water.
new: and saying, "Lord, have mercy on my son, because he has seizures and is ill; for often he falls into the fire and often into the water.
reason: This Greek reads κακῶς ἔχει ("is ill", as κακῶς ἔχοντας is rendered in 14:35), not κακῶς πάσχει ("suffers badly") of other editions.

old: And He told them, "Because of your little faith. For truly I tell you, if you have faith like a mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, 'Move from here to over there,' and it will move, and nothing will be impossible for you."
new: And He told them, "Because of your little faith. For truly I say to you, if you have faith like a mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, 'Move from here to over there,' and it will move, and nothing will be impossible for you."
reason: NT-wide consistency pass (ἀμὴν λέγω "Truly I say to you"; μὴ γένοιτο; ἑορτή "feast"; μύρον "perfume"; λῃστής "robber"; οἱ δώδεκα; γέγραπται; ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς in Matthew).

old: Greek oligopistian means "little faith" rather than "unbelief." Verse 21 ("But this kind does not go out except by prayer and fasting") is absent from the earliest manuscripts and is omitted in this critical text.

old: And if your hand or your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away from you; it is better for you to enter into life maimed or crippled, than, having two hands or two feet, to be thrown into the eternal fire.

old: Verse 11 ("For the Son of Man came to save the lost") is absent from the earliest manuscripts and is omitted in this critical text.
new: Verse 11 ("For the Son of Man came to save the lost") is absent from the earliest manuscripts; the Saints Greek Critical Text prints it within double brackets ⟦ ⟧ (shown as an additional verse).

old: And if it happens that he finds it, truly I tell you that he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine that have not strayed.
new: And if it happens that he finds it, truly I say to you that he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine that have not strayed.
reason: NT-wide consistency pass (ἀμὴν λέγω "Truly I say to you"; μὴ γένοιτο; ἑορτή "feast"; μύρον "perfume"; λῃστής "robber"; οἱ δώδεκα; γέγραπται; ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς in Matthew).

old: Truly I tell you, whatever you bind on earth will have been bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will have been loosed in heaven.
new: Truly I say to you, whatever you bind on earth will have been bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will have been loosed in heaven.
reason: NT-wide consistency pass (ἀμὴν λέγω "Truly I say to you"; μὴ γένοιτο; ἑορτή "feast"; μύρον "perfume"; λῃστής "robber"; οἱ δώδεκα; γέγραπται; ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς in Matthew).

old: Again, truly I tell you that if two of you agree on earth concerning anything that they may ask, it will be done for them by My Father who is in heaven.
new: Again, truly I say to you that if two of you agree on earth concerning anything that they may ask, it will be done for them by My Father who is in heaven.

old: Greek hebdomēkontakis hepta literally reads "seventy times seven," though it can also be rendered "seventy-seven times" (echoing Gen 4:24 LXX); either way it signifies limitless forgiveness.
new: Greek hebdomēkontakis hepta literally reads "seventy times seven," though it can also be rendered "seventy-seven times" (echoing Gen 4:24 LXX).

old: For this reason the kingdom of heaven may be compared to a king who wished to settle accounts with his servants.
new: For this reason the kingdom of heaven may be compared to a king who wished to settle accounts with his slaves.
reason: τῶν δούλων αὐτοῦ: δοῦλος is "slave" in this edition (e.g. 13:27-28; 20:27; 21:34).

old: So the servant fell down and bowed before him, saying, 'Master, be patient with me, and I will repay you everything.'
new: So the slave fell down and bowed before him, saying, 'Master, be patient with me, and I will repay you everything.'
reason: ὁ δοῦλος: δοῦλος is "slave" in this edition.

old: And moved with compassion, the master of that servant released him and forgave him the loan.
new: And moved with compassion, the master of that slave released him and forgave him the loan.
reason: τοῦ δούλου ἐκείνου: δοῦλος is "slave" in this edition.

old: But going out, that servant found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred denarii; and seizing him, he began to choke him, saying, 'Pay back what you owe.'
new: But going out, that slave found one of his fellow slaves who owed him a hundred denarii; and seizing him, he began to choke him, saying, 'Pay back what you owe.'
reason: ὁ δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος ... τῶν συνδούλων αὐτοῦ: δοῦλος is "slave", so σύνδουλος is "fellow slave".

old: So his fellow servant fell down and pleaded with him, saying, 'Be patient with me, and I will repay you.'
new: So his fellow slave fell down and pleaded with him, saying, 'Be patient with me, and I will repay you.'
reason: ὁ σύνδουλος αὐτοῦ: "fellow slave", consistent with δοῦλος → "slave".

old: So when his fellow servants saw what had happened, they were greatly grieved, and came and reported clearly to their master all that had happened.
new: So when his fellow slaves saw what had happened, they were greatly grieved, and came and reported clearly to their master all that had happened.
reason: οἱ σύνδουλοι αὐτοῦ: "fellow slaves", consistent with δοῦλος → "slave".

old: Then his master summoned him and said to him, 'You wicked servant, I forgave you all that debt because you pleaded with me;
new: Then his master summoned him and said to him, 'You wicked slave, I forgave you all that debt because you pleaded with me;
reason: Δοῦλε πονηρέ: δοῦλος is "slave" in this edition.

old: should you not also have had mercy on your fellow servant, just as I also had mercy on you?'
new: should you not also have had mercy on your fellow slave, just as I also had mercy on you?'
reason: τὸν σύνδουλόν σου: "fellow slave", consistent with δοῦλος → "slave".

old: Greek palingenesia ("rebirth" or "regeneration") refers to the future renewal of creation at the coming of the Messianic reign.
new: Greek palingenesia means "rebirth" or "regeneration"; here it denotes the renewal of the world in the age to come.
reason: Removes the confessional framing ("at the coming of the Messianic reign"); keeps the lexical sense.

old: Greek lytron denotes a ransom price paid for release, and the preposition anti ("in place of" or "for") expresses substitution.
new: Greek lytron denotes a ransom price paid for release; the preposition anti means "in place of" or "in exchange for."
reason: Removes the doctrinal assertion that the preposition "expresses substitution"; keeps the lexical information.

old: And Jesus answered and said to them, "Truly I tell you, if you have faith and do not doubt, you will not only do what was done to the fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain, 'Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,' it will happen.
new: And Jesus answered and said to them, "Truly I say to you, if you have faith and do not doubt, you will not only do what was done to the fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain, 'Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,' it will happen.
reason: NT-wide consistency pass (ἀμὴν λέγω "Truly I say to you"; μὴ γένοιτο; ἑορτή "feast"; μύρον "perfume"; λῃστής "robber"; οἱ δώδεκα; γέγραπται; ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς in Matthew).

old: Which of the two did the will of the father?" They said, "The first." Jesus said to them, "Truly I tell you that the tax collectors and the prostitutes are going ahead of you into the kingdom of God.
new: Which of the two did the will of the father?" They said, "The first." Jesus said to them, "Truly I say to you that the tax collectors and the prostitutes are going ahead of you into the kingdom of God.
reason: NT-wide consistency pass (ἀμὴν λέγω "Truly I say to you"; μὴ γένοιτο; ἑορτή "feast"; μύρον "perfume"; λῃστής "robber"; οἱ δώδεκα; γέγραπται; ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς in Matthew).

old: Verse 14 (a woe regarding devouring widows' houses, parallel to Mark 12:40 and Luke 20:47) is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts and is not present in this critical text.
new: Verse 14 (a woe regarding devouring widows' houses, parallel to Mark 12:40 and Luke 20:47) is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts; the Saints Greek Critical Text prints it within double brackets ⟦ ⟧.
reason: The critical text does contain 23:14 (in ⟦ ⟧, supplied as an additional verse), so the claim that it is not present in this text is false.

old: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her—how often I wanted to gather your children together, just as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you were unwilling!
new: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her—how often did I want to gather your children together, just as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you were unwilling?
reason: This Greek punctuates ποσάκις ἠθέλησα ... καὶ οὐκ ἠθελήσατε; as a question, not an exclamation.

old: But He answered and said to them, "Do you not see all these things? Truly I tell you, by no means will a stone be left here upon a stone that will not be torn down."
new: But He answered and said to them, "Do you not see all these things? Truly I say to you, by no means will a stone be left here upon a stone that will not be torn down."
reason: NT-wide consistency pass (ἀμὴν λέγω "Truly I say to you"; μὴ γένοιτο; ἑορτή "feast"; μύρον "perfume"; λῃστής "robber"; οἱ δώδεκα; γέγραπται; ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς in Matthew).

old: For then there will be great affliction, such as has not occurred from the beginning of the world until now, nor will by any means occur again.
new: For then there will be great affliction, such as has not occurred from the beginning of the world until now, nor will by any means occur.
reason: οὐδʼ οὐ μὴ γένηται has no word for "again"; the emphatic negation is already rendered by "by any means".

old: Truly I tell you, this generation will by no means pass away until all these things take place.
new: Truly I say to you, this generation will by no means pass away until all these things take place.
reason: NT-wide consistency pass (ἀμὴν λέγω "Truly I say to you"; μὴ γένοιτο; ἑορτή "feast"; μύρον "perfume"; λῃστής "robber"; οἱ δώδεκα; γέγραπται; ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς in Matthew).

old: Some later manuscripts omit "nor the Son," likely out of theological concern, whereas the earliest and best-attested witnesses include the phrase.
new: Some later manuscripts omit "nor the Son," which the earliest witnesses and the Saints Greek Critical Text include.
reason: Removes speculation about scribal motive and evaluative wording; keeps the factual textual information.

old: Truly I tell you, he will put him in charge of all his possessions.
new: Truly I say to you, he will put him in charge of all his possessions.
reason: NT-wide consistency pass (ἀμὴν λέγω "Truly I say to you"; μὴ γένοιτο; ἑορτή "feast"; μύρον "perfume"; λῃστής "robber"; οἱ δώδεκα; γέγραπται; ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς in Matthew).

old: and will cut him in two and assign his portion with the hypocrites. In that place there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth."
new: and will cut him in two and assign his portion with the hypocrites. In that place there will be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth."
reason: ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων has the articles, rendered "the weeping and the gnashing of teeth" in 22:13 and 25:30.

old: And while they were going away to buy, the bridegroom came, and those who were ready entered with him into the wedding feast, and the door was shut.
new: And while they were going away to buy, the bridegroom came, and those who were ready entered with him into the wedding banquet, and the door was shut.
reason: εἰς τοὺς γάμους is rendered "to the wedding banquet" throughout 22:2-10; same term, same sense.

old: For it is just like a man going on a journey, who called his own servants and entrusted his possessions to them.
new: For it is just like a man going on a journey, who called his own slaves and entrusted his possessions to them.
reason: δούλους is "slaves" in this edition (as in 24:45-50 and 22:3-10).

old: Now after a long time the master of those servants came and settled accounts with them.
new: Now after a long time the master of those slaves came and settled accounts with them.

old: And throw the worthless servant out into the outer darkness; in that place there will be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.'

new: Now while they were eating, Jesus took bread, and having said a blessing, He broke it, and giving it to the disciples, He said, "Take, eat; this is My body."
reason: εὐλογήσας has no object; supplying "it" decides a disputed point (blessing the bread vs. blessing God) that the Greek leaves open.

old: Then Judas, who had betrayed Him, seeing that He had been condemned, was filled with remorse and returned the thirty silver coins to the chief priests and elders,
new: Then Judas, who had handed Him over, seeing that He had been condemned, was filled with remorse and returned the thirty silver coins to the chief priests and elders,

old: Now after the Sabbath, as it was dawning toward the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the grave.
new: Now after the Sabbath, as it was dawning toward the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb.

old: The beginning of the good news of Jesus Christ, Son of God.
new: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, Son of God.
reason: εὐαγγέλιον is rendered "gospel" in this edition, including elsewhere in Mark (8:35; 10:29; 13:10; 14:9; 16:15).

old: And after John was handed over, Jesus came into Galilee, proclaiming the good news of God
new: And after John was handed over, Jesus came into Galilee, proclaiming the gospel of God
reason: τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ θεοῦ: εὐαγγέλιον is "gospel" in this edition (cf. 2 Cor 11:7 "the gospel of God").

old: and saying, "The appointed time has been fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has drawn near; repent and believe in the good news."
new: and saying, "The appointed time has been fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has drawn near; repent and believe in the gospel."
reason: ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ: εὐαγγέλιον is "gospel" in this edition, including elsewhere in Mark.

old: And Simon and those with him tracked Him down,

old: And Jesus said to them, "Can the sons of the bridal chamber fast while the bridegroom is with them? For as long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.
new: And Jesus said to them, "Can the sons of the bridal chamber fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.
reason: ὅσον χρόνον ἔχουσιν... stands in asyndeton; there is no γάρ, so "For" is unwarranted.

old: how he entered the house of God in the time of Abiathar the high priest and ate the loaves of the Presence, which it is not lawful for anyone to eat except the priests, and gave some also to those who were with him?"
new: how he entered the house of God in the time of Abiathar the high priest and ate the loaves of presentation, which it is not lawful for anyone to eat except the priests, and gave some also to those who were with him?"
reason: τοὺς ἄρτους τῆς προθέσεως is "loaves of presentation" (as in this edition's Matt 12:4; Luke 6:4); "of the Presence" follows the Hebrew lechem panim.

old: And when He was alone, those around Him, together with the Twelve, were asking Him about the parables.

reason: NT-wide consistency pass (ἀμὴν λέγω "Truly I say to you"; μὴ γένοιτο; ἑορτή "feast"; μύρον "perfume"; λῃστής "robber"; οἱ δώδεκα; γέγραπται; ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς in Matthew).

old: and they have no root in themselves, but are only temporary; then, when affliction or persecution arises because of the word, immediately they stumble.

reason: ἀλλὰ πρόσκαιροί εἰσιν is simply "but are temporary"; "only" has no Greek basis.

old: And King Herod heard of it, for His name had become well known; and people were saying, "John the Baptizer has been raised from the dead, and because of this these powers are at work in Him."
new: And King Herod heard of it, for His name had become well known; and people were saying, "John the Baptizer has been raised from the dead, and because of this these powers are at work in him."
reason: ἐν αὐτῷ refers to John, the subject of ἐγήγερται, so the pronoun must not be capitalized as if it referred to Jesus.

old: Verse 16 ('If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear') is absent from the earliest and best manuscripts and is omitted in this critical text.

reason: The Saints Greek Critical Text does not omit 7:16; it prints ⟦Εἴ τις ἔχει ὦτα ἀκούειν ἀκουέτω.⟧ in double brackets, so the note's claim is false.

old: And He began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected by the elders and the chief priests and the scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.
new: And He began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected by the elders and the chief priests and the scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise.
reason: ἀναστῆναι is simply "rise"; "again" has no Greek basis (cf. this edition's Mark 9:31 "He will rise").

old: And He was saying to them, "Truly I tell you that there are some of those standing here who will by no means taste death until they see the kingdom of God having come in power."
new: And He was saying to them, "Truly I say to you that there are some of those standing here who will by no means taste death until they see the kingdom of God having come in power."
reason: NT-wide consistency pass (ἀμὴν λέγω "Truly I say to you"; μὴ γένοιτο; ἑορτή "feast"; μύρον "perfume"; λῃστής "robber"; οἱ δώδεκα; γέγραπται; ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς in Matthew).

old: And Peter responded and said to Jesus, "Rabbi, it is good for us to be here; and let us make three shelters, one for You, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah."
new: And Peter responded and said to Jesus, "Rabbi, it is good for us to be here; and let us make three tents, one for You, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah."
reason: τρεῖς σκηνάς is rendered "three tents" in this edition's parallels (Matt 17:4; Luke 9:33); the same Greek in the same sense should not become "shelters" here.

old: The earliest manuscripts end the verse with 'by prayer'; later manuscripts add 'and fasting'.
new: Several early manuscripts (including Codex Vaticanus) end the verse with 'by prayer'; most others add 'and fasting'.
reason: The 'and fasting' reading is also attested early (P45 apparently has it), so 'the earliest manuscripts' omitting it overstates the evidence.

old: for He was teaching His disciples and saying to them, "The Son of Man is being delivered into the hands of men, and they will kill Him; and when He has been killed, after three days He will rise."
new: for He was teaching His disciples and saying to them, "The Son of Man is being handed over into the hands of men, and they will kill Him; and when He has been killed, after three days He will rise."
reason: παραδίδοται is rendered 'hand over' throughout this section (10:33; 14:10-11, 21, 41); 'delivered' is the lone outlier.

old: For whoever gives you a cup of water to drink on account of the name, because you belong to Christ, truly I tell you that he will by no means lose his reward.
new: For whoever gives you a cup of water to drink on account of the name, because you belong to Christ, truly I say to you that he will by no means lose his reward.
reason: The formula ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν is rendered 'Truly I say to you' everywhere else in this section (10:15, 29; 11:23; 12:43; 13:30; 14:9, 18, 25).

old: And if your eye causes you to stumble, tear it out; it is better for you to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye than, having two eyes, to be thrown into Gehenna,
new: And if your eye causes you to stumble, throw it out; it is better for you to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye than, having two eyes, to be thrown into Gehenna,
reason: ἔκβαλε is 'throw/cast out'; 'tear out' imports Matthew's ἔξελε (Matt 5:29; 18:9).

old: This concise saying links fiery testing with the Old Testament practice of seasoning sacrifices with salt (Leviticus 2:13); later manuscripts expand it with 'and every sacrifice will be salted with salt'.
new: Later manuscripts add 'and every sacrifice will be salted with salt' (compare Leviticus 2:13).
reason: Removes the interpretive claim that the saying 'links fiery testing' with sacrificial salting; keeps the factual textual information.

old: And Jesus said to him, "Why do you call Me good? No one is good except One, God alone.
new: And Jesus said to him, "Why do you call Me good? No one is good except One, God.
reason: εἷς ὁ θεός is 'One, God'; 'alone' renders εἷς a second time.

old: Now they were on the road going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was walking ahead of them; and they were amazed, while those who followed were afraid. And taking the Twelve aside again, He began to tell them the things that were about to happen to Him,
new: Now they were on the road going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was walking ahead of them; and they were amazed, while those who followed were afraid. And taking the twelve aside again, He began to tell them the things that were about to happen to Him,
reason: NT-wide consistency pass (ἀμὴν λέγω "Truly I say to you"; μὴ γένοιτο; ἑορτή "feast"; μύρον "perfume"; λῃστής "robber"; οἱ δώδεκα; γέγραπται; ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς in Matthew).

old: and they will mock Him and spit on Him and flog Him and kill Him, and after three days He will rise again."
new: and they will mock Him and spit on Him and flog Him and kill Him, and after three days He will rise."
reason: ἀναστήσεται has no 'again'; the parallel 9:31 has the same verb rendered 'He will rise.'

old: The Greek preposition anti ('in place of') conveys substitutionary exchange within the ransom (lytron) metaphor of paying a price to release captives or slaves.
new: The preposition anti basically means 'in place of' or 'in exchange for'; lytron denotes a price paid to release captives or slaves.
reason: Replaces the doctrinal claim that anti 'conveys substitutionary exchange' with a neutral lexical statement.

old: The Greek verb sozo ('saved') carries a dual nuance of physical restoration ('made well / healed') and spiritual salvation, connecting Bartimaeus's sight with his following Jesus on the road.
new: The verb sozo ('save') is also used of physical healing ('make well').
reason: Removes the interpretive claim that the verb connects his sight with 'spiritual salvation' and his following Jesus; keeps the lexical point.

old: And He entered Jerusalem, into the temple; and after looking around at everything, since the hour was already late, He went out to Bethany with the Twelve.
new: And He entered Jerusalem, into the temple; and after looking around at everything, since the hour was already late, He went out to Bethany with the twelve.
reason: NT-wide consistency pass (ἀμὴν λέγω "Truly I say to you"; μὴ γένοιτο; ἑορτή "feast"; μύρον "perfume"; λῃστής "robber"; οἱ δώδεκα; γέγραπται; ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς in Matthew).

old: The Greek aorist "have received" (elabete) vividly expresses the certainty of the answer to prayer as already secured.
new: The verb elabete is aorist, literally 'you received.'
reason: Replaces the interpretive comment ('vividly expresses the certainty... already secured') with the plain grammatical fact.

old: The verse numbered 11:26 in later manuscripts (a parallel to Matthew 6:15) is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts and from this source text.
new: The verse numbered 11:26 in later manuscripts (a parallel to Matthew 6:15) is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts; this text prints it in double brackets.
reason: The note falsely said 11:26 is absent 'from this source text'; the Saints Greek Critical Text prints it within ⟦ ⟧.

old: He still had one more, a beloved son; he sent him last of all to them, saying, 'They will respect my son.'
new: He still had one more, a beloved son; he sent him last to them, saying, 'They will respect my son.'
reason: ἔσχατον alone is 'last'; 'of all' has no Greek basis here (contrast ἔσχατον πάντων in 12:22).

old: and to love Him with the whole heart, and with the whole understanding, and with the whole strength, and to love one's neighbor as oneself, is far more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices."
new: and to love Him with the whole heart, and with the whole understanding, and with the whole strength, and to love one's neighbor as oneself, is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices."
reason: περισσότερόν ἐστιν is 'is more than'; 'far' is an unwarranted intensifier.

old: For they were saying, "Not during the festival, or else there will be an uproar of the people."
new: For they were saying, "Not during the feast, or else there will be an uproar of the people."
reason: NT-wide consistency pass (ἀμὴν λέγω "Truly I say to you"; μὴ γένοιτο; ἑορτή "feast"; μύρον "perfume"; λῃστής "robber"; οἱ δώδεκα; γέγραπται; ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς in Matthew).

old: And while they were eating, He took bread, and after blessing it, He broke it and gave it to them, and said, "Take; this is My body."
new: And while they were eating, He took bread, and after blessing, He broke it and gave it to them, and said, "Take; this is My body."
reason: εὐλογήσας has no object; supplying 'it' decides that the bread (rather than God) was blessed.

old: And Jesus said to him, "Truly I say to you that today, on this very night, before a rooster crows twice, you yourself will deny Me three times."
new: And Jesus said to him, "Truly I say to you that today, this night, before a rooster crows twice, you yourself will deny Me three times."
reason: ταύτῃ τῇ νυκτί is 'this night'; 'very' is an added intensifier.

old: And answering, Jesus said to them, "Have you come out as against a bandit with swords and clubs to arrest Me?
new: And answering, Jesus said to them, "Have you come out as against a robber with swords and clubs to arrest Me?
reason: λῃστής is rendered 'robber' in this edition (11:17; 15:27).

old: Now at the festival he used to release to them one prisoner, whomever they requested.
new: Now at the feast he used to release to them one prisoner, whomever they requested.
reason: NT-wide consistency pass (ἀμὴν λέγω "Truly I say to you"; μὴ γένοιτο; ἑορτή "feast"; μύρον "perfume"; λῃστής "robber"; οἱ δώδεκα; γέγραπται; ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς in Matthew).

old: The earliest and best Greek manuscripts omit verse 28 ("And the Scripture was fulfilled that says, 'He was numbered with the transgressors'"), which entered later manuscripts from Luke 22:37.
new: The earliest Greek manuscripts lack verse 28 (printed in double brackets in this text), which probably entered later manuscripts from Luke 22:37.
reason: The note implied v. 28 is omitted and quoted it in wording different from the edition's 15:28; this Greek text prints it within ⟦ ⟧.

old: The Greek phrase "huios theou" lacks the definite article before the verb and can be translated either "the Son of God" (aligning with Mark 1:1) or "a son of God" (reflecting a Roman centurion's vantage point).
new: The predicate huios theou has no article and stands before the verb, so it can be translated either 'the Son of God' or 'a son of God.'
reason: Corrects the garbled grammatical description ('lacks the definite article before the verb') and removes interpretive asides about Mark 1:1 and the centurion's vantage point.

old: Greek κεχαριτωμένη is a perfect passive participle meaning "one who has been shown favor" or "graced," emphasizing God's initiative in bestowing grace.
new: Greek κεχαριτωμένη is a perfect passive participle meaning "one who has been shown favor" or "graced."
reason: The closing clause is theological commentary rather than an explanation of the Greek participle; trimmed to the lexical/grammatical content.

old: And Mary said, "Here is the servant of the Lord; may it happen to me according to your word." And the angel departed from her.
new: And Mary said, "Here is the slave of the Lord; may it happen to me according to your word." And the angel departed from her.
reason: δούλη is the feminine of δοῦλος, which this edition renders "slave" (cf. Luke 7:2-10); "servant" is reserved for διάκονος/παῖς/οἰκέτης/θεράπων.

old: because He has looked upon the humble condition of His servant; for look, from now on all generations will call me blessed.
new: because He has looked upon the humble condition of His slave; for look, from now on all generations will call me blessed.
reason: δούλης (feminine of δοῦλος) takes the edition's established rendering "slave", as in 1:38.

old: Greek ἀνατολή denotes "dawn" or "sunrise" and also renders the messianic title "Branch" in the Septuagint (Zech 3:8; 6:12); the future tense ἐπισκέψεται ("will visit") is translated here rather than the aorist variant ἐπεσκέψατο ("has visited").
new: Greek ἀνατολή denotes "dawn" or "sunrise" and also renders "Branch" in the Septuagint (Zech 3:8; 6:12); the future tense ἐπισκέψεται ("will visit") is translated here rather than the aorist variant ἐπεσκέψατο ("has visited").
reason: Labeling the term a "messianic title" is an interpretive claim; the lexical point (LXX ἀνατολή renders "Branch" in Zech 3:8; 6:12) stands without it.

old: "Now You are releasing Your servant, Master, according to Your word, in peace;
new: "Now You are releasing Your slave, Master, according to Your word, in peace;
reason: τὸν δοῦλόν σου, paired with δέσποτα, takes the edition's established rendering "slave" (cf. Luke 7:2-10).

old: And when the devil had completed every temptation, he departed from Him until an appointed time.
new: And when the devil had completed every temptation, he departed from Him until an opportune time.
reason: ἄχρι καιροῦ is anarthrous "until a (suitable) time"; "appointed" adds an idea of a fixed, predetermined time not in the Greek.

old: And He said to them, "Surely you will say this proverb to Me: 'Physician, heal yourself! Whatever we heard took place in Capernaum, do here also in Your hometown.'"
new: And He said to them, "Surely you will say this proverb to Me: 'Physician, heal Yourself! Whatever we heard took place in Capernaum, do here also in Your hometown.'"
reason: σεαυτόν refers to Jesus, as does σου ("Your hometown") in the same quotation; house style capitalizes pronouns for Jesus.

old: Now as He approached the gate of the city, look, a dead man was being carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow; and a sizable crowd from the city was with her.
new: Now as He approached the gate of the city, look, a dead man was being carried out, the only-begotten son of his mother, and she was a widow; and a sizable crowd from the city was with her.
reason: μονογενὴς υἱός: the edition's established rendering of μονογενής is "only-begotten"; keeping it uniform avoids reserving the term for one referent.

old: (When all the people and the tax collectors heard this, they vindicated God, having been baptized with the baptism of John;
new: (When all the people and the tax collectors heard this, they justified God, having been baptized with the baptism of John;
reason: ἐδικαίωσαν τὸν θεόν: δικαιόω has the established rendering "justify", and English "justify" (show/declare to be right) fits here; the note explains the sense.

old: Verses 29–30 are punctuated as a parenthetical comment by the narrator, though some interpreters view them as a continuation of Jesus' speech. "Vindicated God" (ἐδικαίωσαν τὸν θεόν) means they acknowledged God to be righteous.
new: Verses 29–30 are punctuated as a parenthetical comment by the narrator, though some interpreters view them as a continuation of Jesus' speech. "Justified God" (ἐδικαίωσαν τὸν θεόν) means they acknowledged God to be righteous.
reason: Note updated to match the verse rendering of ἐδικαίωσαν as "justified".

old: Yet wisdom is vindicated by all her children."
new: Yet wisdom is justified by all her children."
reason: ἐδικαιώθη (δικαιόω) takes the established rendering "justify", which also keeps the verbal link with 7:29.

old: "Is vindicated" uses a gnomic aorist (ἐδικαιώθη), echoing "vindicated" in 7:29; the preposition ἀπό ("by") marks the children of wisdom as those through whom wisdom's rightness is demonstrated.
new: "Is justified" uses a gnomic aorist (ἐδικαιώθη), echoing "justified" in 7:29; the preposition ἀπό ("by") marks the children of wisdom as those through whom wisdom's rightness is demonstrated.
reason: Note updated to match the verse rendering of ἐδικαιώθη as "justified".

old: Luke's "about eight days" reflects inclusive reckoning of the interval that Matthew 17:1 and Mark 9:2 express as "six days."
new: Greek hosei hemerai okto ("about eight days") stands as a parenthetical nominative; Matthew 17:1 and Mark 9:2 read "after six days."
reason: The note harmonizes Luke with Matthew/Mark ("inclusive reckoning") instead of describing the Greek; replaced with a neutral statement of the construction and the parallels.

old: The Greek word exodos literally means "departure" or "exodus," echoing Israel's Exodus while referring to Jesus' impending death, resurrection, and ascension.
new: The Greek word exodos literally means "a going out," that is, "departure" (the source of English "exodus").
reason: The claims that exodos "echoes Israel's Exodus" and refers to death, resurrection and ascension are interpretive; reduced to the lexical meaning.

old: The Greek term analempsis ("taking up" or "ascension") opens Luke's travel narrative to Jerusalem and looks ahead to Jesus' passion, resurrection, and ascension.
new: The Greek term analempsis means "a taking up."
reason: The note's claims about the travel narrative and "passion, resurrection, and ascension" are interpretive commentary; reduced to the lexical meaning.

old: The reading "few things are needed, or one" (combining a literal reference to a simple meal with the single spiritual necessity) is strongly attested in early Alexandrian witnesses, while other manuscripts shorten it to "one thing is needed" or "few things are needed."
new: The critical text reads "few things are needed, or one," with early Alexandrian witnesses (e.g., Sinaiticus, Vaticanus); other manuscripts read "one thing is needed" or "few things are needed."
reason: Removed the interpretive parenthesis (simple meal vs. spiritual necessity) and the evaluative "shorten"; the "one thing" reading is not a shortening but a rival reading.

old: But I will show you whom to fear: fear the One who, after killing, has authority to throw into hell; yes, I say to you, fear Him.
new: But I will show you whom to fear: fear the One who, after killing, has authority to throw into Gehenna; yes, I say to you, fear Him.
reason: γέεννα is rendered "Gehenna" throughout this edition (Matt 5:29-30; 10:28; Mark 9:43-47); "hell" breaks the established rendering.

old: for all the nations of the world eagerly seek these things, and your Father knows that you need these things.
new: for all the nations of the world eagerly seek these things, but your Father knows that you need these things.
reason: ὑμῶν δὲ ὁ πατήρ is contrastive (the nations seek, but your Father knows); "and" loses the adversative δέ.

old: Blessed are those servants whom the master will find staying awake when he comes. Truly I say to you that he will fasten his belt, have them recline at table, and come forward and serve them.
new: Blessed are those slaves whom the master will find staying awake when he comes. Truly I say to you that he will fasten his belt, have them recline at table, and come forward and serve them.
reason: οἱ δοῦλοι: the edition's established rendering of δοῦλος is "slave."

old: Blessed is that servant whom his master will find doing so when he comes.
new: Blessed is that slave whom his master will find doing so when he comes.
reason: ὁ δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος: δοῦλος → "slave" per the edition's established rendering.

old: But if that servant says in his heart, 'My master is delayed in coming,' and begins to beat the male servants and the female servants, and to eat and drink and get drunk,
new: But if that slave says in his heart, 'My master is delayed in coming,' and begins to beat the male servants and the female servants, and to eat and drink and get drunk,
reason: ὁ δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος: δοῦλος → "slave" (παῖδας/παιδίσκας remain "servants").

old: the master of that servant will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not know, and will cut him in two and assign his portion with the unfaithful.
new: the master of that slave will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not know, and will cut him in two and assign his portion with the unfaithful.
reason: τοῦ δούλου ἐκείνου: δοῦλος → "slave" per the edition's established rendering.

old: And that servant who knew his master's will and did not get ready or act according to his will will be beaten with many blows;
new: And that slave who knew his master's will and did not get ready or act according to his will will be beaten with many blows;
reason: ἐκεῖνος δὲ ὁ δοῦλος: δοῦλος → "slave" per the edition's established rendering.

old: But the synagogue leader, indignant because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, responded and was saying to the crowd, "There are six days in which it is necessary to work; so come on those days and be healed, and not on the Sabbath day."
new: But the synagogue ruler, indignant because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, responded and was saying to the crowd, "There are six days in which it is necessary to work; so come on those days and be healed, and not on the Sabbath day."
reason: ἀρχισυνάγωγος is "synagogue ruler" in Luke 8:49 and Mark 5:35-38; keep the same term within Luke.

old: Greek teleioumai can mean "I reach completion" (finishing His appointed course) or "I am brought to perfection" through suffering.
new: Greek teleioumai can mean "I reach completion" (middle) or "I am brought to completion, perfected" (passive).
reason: "Finishing His appointed course" and "through suffering" are theological glosses not in the Greek; reduced to the lexical options.

old: and at the hour of the banquet he sent his slave to say to those who had been invited, 'Come, because everything is ready now.'
new: and at the hour of the banquet he sent his slave to say to those who had been invited, 'Come, because it is ready now.'
reason: This Greek reads ὅτι ἤδη ἕτοιμά ἐστιν without πάντα; "everything" follows the TR reading (ἕτοιμά ἐστι πάντα).

old: "You" is plural (hymin), shifting from the single slave addressed in v. 23 so that the host's final declaration also speaks directly to Jesus' listeners.
new: "You" is plural (hymin), although a single slave is addressed in v. 23.
reason: The purpose clause ("so that the host's final declaration also speaks directly to Jesus' listeners") is an interpretive claim; kept only the grammatical observation.

old: In Semitic idiom, "hate" (miseo) is used hyperbolically for loving less or subordinating all other allegiances to devotion to Jesus (cf. Matthew 10:37).
new: In Semitic idiom, "hate" (miseo) can be used hyperbolically for loving less (cf. Matthew 10:37).
reason: Removed the devotional gloss "subordinating all other allegiances to devotion to Jesus"; kept the lexical point.

old: Greek ho kyrios ("the master" or "the Lord") refers here to the rich master of the parable rather than Jesus, as confirmed by the shift to Jesus's own voice in verse 9 ("And I tell you").
new: Greek ho kyrios can mean "the master" or "the Lord"; it is taken here as the master of the parable (cf. "my master," vv. 3, 5).
reason: The referent of ὁ κύριος is debated; the note overstated it as "confirmed." Rewritten to state the choice neutrally.

old: So you also, when you have done all the things commanded you, say, 'We are unworthy slaves; we have done what we were obligated to do.'"
new: So you also, when you have done all the things commanded you, say, 'We are worthless slaves; we have done what we were obligated to do.'"
reason: ἀχρεῖοι means "useless, unprofitable," not morally "unworthy"; the edition renders ἀχρεῖον δοῦλον "worthless" in Matt 25:30.

old: "Unworthy" translates Greek achreioi, which literally means "useless" or "unprofitable," referring here to slaves who have earned no special merit beyond their required duty.
new: "Worthless" translates Greek achreioi, literally "useless" or "unprofitable."
reason: Note updated to match the verse; removed the interpretive clause about slaves having "earned no special merit."

old: In the very same way it will be on the day the Son of Man is revealed.
new: In the same way it will be on the day the Son of Man is revealed.
reason: κατὰ ταῦτα is simply "in the same way" (lit. "according to these things"); "very" is an added intensifier.

old: Whoever seeks to preserve his life will lose it, and whoever loses it will keep it alive.
new: Whoever seeks to preserve his life will lose it, but whoever loses it will keep it alive.
reason: ὃς δʼ ἂν ἀπολέσῃ: δέ is adversative here, contrasting the two outcomes; "and" loses the contrast.

old: Verse 36 ("Two men will be in the field; one will be taken and the other will be left") is absent from the earliest and best Greek manuscripts and is omitted in the critical text.
new: Verse 36 is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts; the critical text prints it within double brackets ⟦ ⟧.
reason: The Saints Greek Critical Text does include 17:36 in ⟦ ⟧, so "omitted in the critical text" is false; also "Two men" adds a gender the Greek Δύο lacks.

old: I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than that one; because everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted."
new: I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than that one; because everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but the one who humbles himself will be exalted."
reason: ὁ δὲ ταπεινῶν: δέ is adversative in this antithesis; "but" represents it.

old: Truly I tell you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will by no means enter into it."
new: Truly I say to you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will by no means enter into it."
reason: NT-wide consistency pass (ἀμὴν λέγω "Truly I say to you"; μὴ γένοιτο; ἑορτή "feast"; μύρον "perfume"; λῃστής "robber"; οἱ δώδεκα; γέγραπται; ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς in Matthew).

old: And He said to them, "Truly I tell you that there is no one who has left house or wife or brothers or parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God,
new: And He said to them, "Truly I say to you that there is no one who has left house or wife or brothers or parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God,
reason: NT-wide consistency pass (ἀμὴν λέγω "Truly I say to you"; μὴ γένοιτο; ἑορτή "feast"; μύρον "perfume"; λῃστής "robber"; οἱ δώδεκα; γέγραπται; ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς in Matthew).

old: who will not certainly receive many times as much in this time, and in the coming age eternal life."
new: who will not receive many times as much in this time, and in the coming age eternal life."
reason: οὐχὶ μὴ ἀπολάβῃ negates the verb emphatically; "will not certainly receive" reads in English as "is not sure to receive", reversing the promise.

old: He will come and destroy these farmers, and will give the vineyard to others." And when they heard this, they said, "May it never be!"
new: He will come and destroy these farmers, and will give the vineyard to others." And when they heard this, they said, "May it never happen!"
reason: NT-wide consistency pass (ἀμὴν λέγω "Truly I say to you"; μὴ γένοιτο; ἑορτή "feast"; μύρον "perfume"; λῃστής "robber"; οἱ δώδεκα; γέγραπται; ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς in Matthew).

old: Truly I tell you that this generation will by no means pass away until all things take place.
new: Truly I say to you that this generation will by no means pass away until all things take place.
reason: NT-wide consistency pass (ἀμὴν λέγω "Truly I say to you"; μὴ γένοιτο; ἑορτή "feast"; μύρον "perfume"; λῃστής "robber"; οἱ δώδεκα; γέγραπται; ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς in Matthew).

old: ⟦Now he was obligated to release one to them at each festival.⟧
new: ⟦Now he was obligated to release one to them at each feast.⟧
reason: NT-wide consistency pass (ἀμὴν λέγω "Truly I say to you"; μὴ γένοιτο; ἑορτή "feast"; μύρον "perfume"; λῃστής "robber"; οἱ δώδεκα; γέγραπται; ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς in Matthew).

old: Verse 17 (mentioning an obligation to release one prisoner at the festival) is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts and from the Saints Greek Critical Text, which moves directly from 23:16 to 23:18.
new: Verse 17 (mentioning an obligation to release one prisoner at the festival) is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts; the Saints Greek Critical Text prints it within double brackets ⟦ ⟧.
reason: The Saints Greek Critical Text includes 23:17 in ⟦ ⟧ (Ἀνάγκην δὲ εἶχεν...), so the claim that it is absent from that text is false.

old: In the beginning the Word existed, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
new: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

old: Truly, truly, I tell you, a slave is not greater than his master, nor is a messenger greater than the one who sent him.

old: Greek ego eimi literally reads "I am," echoing the divine self-declaration in the Greek Old Testament (e.g., Isa 43:10), though it can also be understood as "I am He."
new: Greek ego eimi literally reads "I am," though it can also be understood as "I am He."

old: Truly, truly, I tell you, the one who believes in Me, he also will do the works that I do; and he will do greater things than these, because I am going to the Father.
