old: Greek parakletos designates one called alongside to assist, intercede, or plead a case, rendered "Advocate" (also commonly translated "Helper" or "Counselor").
new: Greek parakletos designates one called alongside to assist, intercede, or plead a case, rendered "Advocate" (it can also be rendered "Helper" or "Counselor").
reason: Notes should describe the word's range, not what other translations commonly do.

old: Greek uses neuter pronouns here to agree grammatically with neuter pneuma ("Spirit"), rendered with masculine personal pronouns reflecting the Spirit's personhood (cf. masculine ekeinos in 14:26).
new: Greek uses neuter pronouns here to agree grammatically with neuter pneuma ("Spirit"); they are rendered with personal pronouns, as with masculine ekeinos in 14:26.
reason: "Reflecting the Spirit's personhood" is a doctrinal assertion; the grammatical facts (neuter ὅ/αὐτό, masculine ἐκεῖνος in 14:26) are kept.

old: but so that the world may know that I love the Father, just as the Father commanded Me, so I do. Get up, let us go from here."

old: Greek airei is most commonly rendered "takes away," though some interpreters suggest "lifts up." The verb kathairei ("prunes" or "cleanses") creates a wordplay with katharoi ("clean") in verse 3.
new: Greek airei can mean "takes away" or "lifts up." The verb kathairei ("prunes" or "cleanses") creates a wordplay with katharoi ("clean") in verse 3.

old: Greek parakletos ("Advocate") denotes one called alongside to assist, intercede, or counsel, and is also translated "Helper" or "Counselor."
new: Greek parakletos ("Advocate") denotes one called alongside to assist, intercede, or counsel, and can also be rendered "Helper" or "Counselor."

old: The Greek text reads the future tense akousei ("will hear"), highlighting the Spirit's ongoing reception and declaration of what He receives.
new: The Greek text reads the future tense akousei ("will hear").
reason: The second clause is interpretive comment, not an explanation of the Greek.

old: The Greek uses a neuter singular collective ("all that You have given Him," similarly in 17:24) resumed by a plural pronoun ("them"), presenting believers both as a unified gift and as individual recipients of eternal life.
new: The Greek uses a neuter singular collective ("all that You have given Him," similarly in 17:24) resumed by a plural pronoun ("them").

old: Jesus' reply "I am" (repeated in 18:6, 8) functions both as ordinary self-identification ("I am he") and as a resonant echo of the divine self-declaration in John, directly contrasting with Peter's "I am not" in 18:17 and 18:25.
new: Greek ego eimi, literally "I am" (repeated in 18:6, 8), can be understood as self-identification ("I am he"); compare Peter's "I am not" (ouk eimi) in 18:17 and 18:25.

old: The Greek verb is a simple past ("sent") rather than an explicit pluperfect, reflecting the narrative sequence in which Annas—who retained the courtesy title "high priest" after leaving office—interrogated Jesus before sending Him on to Caiaphas.
new: The Greek verb apesteilen is a simple aorist ("sent"), not a pluperfect ("had sent").
reason: The historical reconstruction about Annas's title is not a statement about the Greek; the grammatical point is kept.

old: The Greek wording "You say that I am a king" can also be construed as "You say so, because I am a king"; in either reading, Jesus affirms His kingship while reframing it around bearing witness to the truth rather than political revolt.
new: The Greek wording "You say that I am a king" can also be construed as "You say so, because I am a king."

old: Then they cried out again, saying, "Not this man, but Barabbas!" Now Barabbas was a bandit.

reason: NT-wide consistency pass (ἀμὴν λέγω "Truly I say to you"; μὴ γένοιτο; ἑορτή "feast"; μύρον "perfume"; λῃστής "robber"; οἱ δώδεκα; γέγραπται; ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς in Matthew).

old: Therefore, when the chief priests and the officers saw Him, they shouted, saying, "Crucify! Crucify!" Pilate said to them, "Take Him yourselves and crucify Him, for I myself find no grounds for a charge in Him."
new: Therefore, when the chief priests and the attendants saw Him, they shouted, saying, "Crucify! Crucify!" Pilate said to them, "Take Him yourselves and crucify Him, for I myself find no grounds for a charge in Him."
reason: οἱ ὑπηρέται is rendered "attendants" throughout this passage (18:3, 12, 18, 22, 36).

old: Jesus said to her, "Woman, why are you weeping? Whom are you looking for?" Supposing that He was the gardener, she said to Him, "Sir, if you have carried Him away, tell me where you have placed Him, and I will take Him away."
new: Jesus said to her, "Woman, why are you weeping? Whom are you looking for?" Supposing that He was the gardener, she said to Him, "Sir, if You have carried Him away, tell me where You have placed Him, and I will take Him away."
reason: σύ/ἔθηκας address Jesus; house style capitalizes pronouns for Jesus even when the speaker does not recognize Him (cf. 18:22; 19:9-10).

old: But the other disciples came in the little boat, for they were not far from the land, only about two hundred cubits away, dragging the net of fish.
new: But the other disciples came in the little boat, for they were not far from the land, but about two hundred cubits away, dragging the net of fish.
reason: ἀλλὰ ὡς ἀπὸ πηχῶν διακοσίων is "but about two hundred cubits"; "only" has no Greek basis and ἀλλά was not represented.

old: Across verses 15-17, the Greek alternates between ἀγαπάω and φιλέω ("love"), βόσκω ("feed") and ποιμαίνω ("shepherd"), ἀρνία ("lambs"), πρόβατα ("sheep"), and προβάτια ("little sheep"), as well as οἶδα and γινώσκω ("know"), illustrating John's characteristic stylistic variation.
new: Across verses 15-17, the Greek alternates between ἀγαπάω and φιλέω ("love"), βόσκω ("feed") and ποιμαίνω ("shepherd"), ἀρνία ("lambs"), πρόβατα ("sheep"), and προβάτια ("little sheep"), as well as οἶδα and γινώσκω ("know").
reason: The closing clause settles a disputed interpretive question (stylistic vs. meaningful variation); the lexical facts are kept neutral.

old: and even upon My male servants and upon My female servants in those days I will pour out from My Spirit, and they will prophesy.
new: and even upon My male slaves and upon My female slaves in those days I will pour out from My Spirit, and they will prophesy.
reason: δούλους / δούλας are forms of δοῦλος, which this edition renders "slave" ("servant" is reserved for διάκονος/παῖς/οἰκέτης/θεράπων).

old: Greek pais can mean "child" or "servant"; here and in 3:26, 4:27, and 4:30 it echoes the Servant of the Lord in Isaiah (cf. Isa 52:13).
new: Greek pais can mean "child" or "servant"; so also in 3:26, 4:27, and 4:30.
reason: Keeps the lexical point on παῖς; drops the typological claim that it 'echoes the Servant of the Lord in Isaiah', which is interpretation, not an explanation of the Greek.

old: So having ordered them to leave the Council, they began conferring with one another,
new: So having ordered them to leave the Sanhedrin, they began conferring with one another,
reason: συνέδριον is rendered "Sanhedrin" everywhere else in this range (5:21, 5:27, 5:34, 5:41, 6:12, 6:15); "Council" here is the lone exception.

old: So the Twelve summoned the multitude of the disciples and said, "It is not fitting for us to leave the word of God in order to serve tables.
new: So the twelve summoned the multitude of the disciples and said, "It is not fitting for us to leave the word of God in order to serve tables.
reason: NT-wide consistency pass (ἀμὴν λέγω "Truly I say to you"; μὴ γένοιτο; ἑορτή "feast"; μύρον "perfume"; λῃστής "robber"; οἱ δώδεκα; γέγραπται; ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς in Matthew).

old: Therefore, brothers, select from among you seven men of good reputation, full of the Spirit and of wisdom, whom we will appoint over this duty;
new: But, brothers, select from among you seven men of good reputation, full of the Spirit and of wisdom, whom we will appoint over this duty;
reason: This Greek reads ἐπισκέψασθε δέ (adversative after the negative in 6:2), not the inferential οὖν of other editions; "Therefore" renders οὖν.

old: Early manuscripts (including P74, B, and C) read 'to you' (hymin), whereas later witnesses assimilate to 'to us' (hemin).
new: Early manuscripts (including P74 and B) read 'to you' (hymin), whereas later witnesses assimilate to 'to us' (hemin).
reason: Codex C (Ephraemi) is normally cited for ἡμῖν, not ὑμῖν; removing it leaves the note's claim accurate.

old: And you took up the tent of Moloch and the star of the god Rompha, the images that you made to bow down to them; and I will relocate you beyond Babylon.'
new: And you took up the tabernacle of Moloch and the star of the god Rompha, the images that you made to bow down to them; and I will relocate you beyond Babylon.'
reason: σκηνή is rendered "tabernacle" in this edition's NT; keeping the same word as 7:44 also keeps the Greek's deliberate contrast between the σκηνή of Moloch and the σκηνή of testimony.

old: Our fathers had the tent of testimony in the wilderness, just as the One who spoke to Moses directed him to make it according to the pattern that he had seen,
new: Our fathers had the tabernacle of testimony in the wilderness, just as the One who spoke to Moses directed him to make it according to the pattern that he had seen,
reason: ἡ σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου: σκηνή is rendered "tabernacle" in this edition's NT.

old: Now an angel of the Lord spoke to Philip, saying, "Rise and go toward the south to the road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza." This is a desert road.
new: Now an angel of the Lord spoke to Philip, saying, "Rise and go toward the south to the road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza." This is deserted.
reason: αὕτη ἐστὶν ἔρημος has no word for "road"; αὕτη may refer to the road or to Gaza (as the note says), so the added "road" settles a referent the Greek leaves open.

old: The earliest manuscripts read the singular "the church" (hē ekklēsia) with singular verbs, emphasizing the unity of the whole Christian community across Judea, Galilee, and Samaria rather than the later plural reading "churches."
new: The earliest manuscripts read the singular "the church" (hē ekklēsia) with singular verbs; later manuscripts read the plural "churches."
reason: Keeps the textual fact; drops the ecclesiological claim ('emphasizing the unity of the whole Christian community'), which is interpretation, not an explanation of the Greek.

old: The Greek text reads simply "men" without a numeral; later manuscripts supply "three" (or "two") by harmonizing with v. 7.
new: The Greek text reads simply "men" without a numeral; other manuscripts read "three" or "two."
reason: Witnesses reading "three" include early manuscripts, so "later" is inaccurate, and "by harmonizing" is speculation about scribal motive.

old: The Greek phrase translated "without hesitating at all" (meden diakrinomenos) can also mean "making no distinction," carrying a fitting double resonance in the context of Gentile inclusion (cf. 11:12).
new: The Greek phrase μηδὲν διακρινόμενος (middle voice) means "without hesitating at all"; compare the active μηδὲν διακρίναντα, "making no distinction," in 11:12.
reason: "A fitting double resonance in the context of Gentile inclusion" is interpretive comment; restated as a neutral note on voice and lexis.

old: "I was in the city of Joppa praying, and in a trance I saw a vision: a certain vessel descending, like a large sheet being lowered from heaven by four corners, and it came all the way to me.
new: "I was in the city of Joppa praying, and in a trance I saw a vision: a certain object descending, like a large sheet being lowered from heaven by four corners, and it came all the way to me.
reason: σκεῦός τι is the same phrase rendered "a certain object" in 10:11 and 10:16.

old: I also heard a voice saying to me, 'Rise, Peter, slaughter and eat.'
new: I also heard a voice saying to me, 'Get up, Peter; slaughter and eat.'
reason: Ἀναστάς, Πέτρε, θῦσον καὶ φάγε is identical to 10:13, rendered there "Get up, Peter; slaughter and eat."

old: But a voice answered a second time from heaven, 'What God has made clean, you must not call common.'
new: But a voice answered a second time from heaven, 'What God has cleansed, you must not regard as common.'
reason: Ἃ ὁ θεὸς ἐκαθάρισεν σὺ μὴ κοίνου is identical to 10:15, rendered there "What God has cleansed, you must not regard as common."

old: The Greek text reads Ἑλληνιστάς ("Hellenists"), while some manuscripts read Ἕλληνας ("Greeks"); contrasted with "Jews" in v. 19, the term here refers to Greek-speaking Gentiles.
new: The Greek text reads Ἑλληνιστάς ("Hellenists," i.e., Greek-speakers), while some manuscripts read Ἕλληνας ("Greeks"); here the term stands in contrast to "Jews" in v. 19.
reason: The note stated a disputed referent as fact (Ἑλληνιστής denotes Greek-speaking Jews in 6:1 and 9:29); reworded to state the textual contrast without deciding it.

old: Greek οἰκουμένην ("inhabited world") in Luke-Acts typically refers to the Roman world; historical sources attest severe famines during the reign of Claudius (AD 41-54), especially in Judea around AD 46-48.
new: Greek οἰκουμένην ("inhabited world") in Luke-Acts typically refers to the Roman world.
reason: Historical corroboration from outside sources does not explain the Greek; the lexical part is kept.

old: And when Herod had searched for him and did not find him, he examined the guards and ordered them to be led away to execution. Then he went down from Judea to Caesarea and stayed there.
new: And when Herod had searched for him and did not find him, he examined the guards and ordered them to be led away. Then he went down from Judea to Caesarea and stayed there.
reason: ἐκέλευσεν ἀπαχθῆναι is "ordered them to be led away"; "to execution" is a supplied interpretation, which the existing note already explains.

old: For David, after serving the purpose of God in his own generation, fell asleep and was laid with his fathers and saw decay;
new: For David, after serving the purpose of God in his own generation, fell asleep and was added to his fathers and saw decay;

old: Watch out, then, so that what was spoken in the prophets may not come upon you:
new: Watch out, then, so that what was spoken in the prophets may not come about:

old: The perfect passive participle τεταγμένοι ("had been appointed") reflects Luke's standard usage for external appointment, though some interpreters understand it in a middle sense ("were disposed" or "aligned themselves").
new: The perfect participle τεταγμένοι is taken here as passive ("had been appointed"); some interpreters understand it in a middle sense ("were disposed" or "aligned themselves").
reason: The middle and passive forms are identical; the claim about Luke's "standard usage for external appointment" argues one side of a doctrinally disputed point, so the note now just states the choice.

old: And the disciples were continually being filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.
new: And the disciples were being filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.
reason: ἐπληροῦντο is a plain imperfect, "were being filled"; "continually" has no Greek word behind it.

old: But the Jews who disbelieved stirred up and embittered the minds of the Gentiles against the brothers.
new: But the Jews who disbelieved stirred up and embittered the souls of the Gentiles against the brothers.
reason: τὰς ψυχάς is rendered "souls" per the edition's ψυχή convention (cf. 14:22, 15:24 "souls").

old: On the contrary, we believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus we are saved, in the very same way as they also are."
new: On the contrary, we believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus we are saved, in the same way as they also are."
reason: καθʼ ὃν τρόπον is "in the same way as"; "very" is an intensifier with no Greek basis.

old: "Simeon" (Symeon) is the Semitic form of Peter's Hebrew name Simon, fitting James's Jerusalem setting.
new: "Simeon" (Symeon) is the Semitic form of Peter's name Simon.
reason: "Fitting James's Jerusalem setting" is interpretive comment, not an explanation of the Greek.

old: 'After these things I will return, and I will rebuild the fallen tent of David; I will rebuild its ruins, and I will restore it,
new: 'After these things I will return, and I will rebuild the fallen tabernacle of David; I will rebuild its ruins, and I will restore it,

old: so that the rest of mankind may seek the Lord, even all the Gentiles upon whom My name has been called, says the Lord, who makes these things
new: so that the rest of mankind may seek the Lord, and all the Gentiles upon whom My name has been called, says the Lord, who makes these things
reason: καὶ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη simply joins a second subject ("and all the Gentiles"); "even" makes the Gentiles the same group as "the rest of mankind," which the Greek does not say.

old: So when they were sent off, they went down to Antioch, and having gathered the assembly together, they delivered the letter.
new: So when they were sent off, they went down to Antioch, and having gathered the multitude together, they delivered the letter.
reason: τὸ πλῆθος is rendered "multitude" elsewhere (15:12; 14:1, 4); "assembly" blurs it with ἐκκλησία.

old: The earliest manuscripts omit verse 34 (present in later manuscripts: "But it seemed good to Silas to remain there"), so verse numbering proceeds directly to 15:35.
new: The earliest manuscripts lack verse 34 ("But it seemed good to Silas to remain there"); the Saints Greek Critical Text prints it within double brackets ⟦ ⟧ (shown as an additional verse).
reason: The critical text prints 15:34 in ⟦ ⟧; the note said numbering skips it.

old: The shift from third person ('they') to first person plural ('we') marks the first of the 'we' sections in Acts, indicating the narrator's direct presence from Troas to Philippi.
new: The shift from third person ('they') to first person plural ('we') marks the first of the 'we' sections in Acts.
reason: What the shift "indicates" about the narrator is a disputed critical inference, not a statement about the Greek.

old: "City officials" translates Greek politarchas (politarchs), a civic title confirmed by inscriptions specifically for the magistrates of Thessalonica.
new: "City officials" translates Greek politarchas (politarchs), the title of the city's magistrates.
reason: The inscriptional claim is outside comment, and "specifically for" Thessalonica is inaccurate, since the title is attested for other Macedonian cities too.

old: Greek deisidaimonesterous is an ambiguous comparative ranging from "very religious" to "rather superstitious," allowing Paul a diplomatic opening before critiquing Athenian idolatry.
new: Greek deisidaimonesterous is an ambiguous comparative ranging from "very religious" to "rather superstitious."
reason: The clause about Paul's diplomatic strategy is interpretive comment, not an explanation of the Greek.

old: for while passing through and closely observing your objects of worship, I also found an altar on which had been inscribed, 'To an Unknown God.' What therefore you worship in ignorance, this I proclaim to you.
new: for while passing through and closely observing your objects of worship, I also found an altar on which had been inscribed, 'To an unknown god.' What therefore you worship in ignorance, this I proclaim to you.
reason: Ἀγνώστῳ θεῷ is a pagan altar inscription; capital "God" quietly identifies it with the true God, which the neuter ὃ...τοῦτο that follows avoids doing (cf. 12:22 "a god").

old: And He made from one man every nation of mankind to live on the entire face of the earth, having determined their appointed times and the boundaries of their habitation,
new: And He made from one every nation of mankind to live on the entire face of the earth, having determined their appointed times and the boundaries of their habitation,
reason: ἐξ ἑνός has no noun; "man" is supplied and settles an ambiguity the Greek leaves open (the note explains the usual reading).

old: Literally "from one" (ex henos), understood as one man (Adam); some later manuscripts add "blood" (haimatos).
new: Greek ex henos, "from one," is usually understood as one man; some later manuscripts add "blood" (haimatos).
reason: Adjusted to match the verse, which now gives the literal "from one"; the identification is kept as the usual reading without asserting it.

old: Now Crispus, the synagogue leader, believed in the Lord together with his whole household; and many of the Corinthians, as they heard, were believing and being baptized.
new: Now Crispus, the synagogue ruler, believed in the Lord together with his whole household; and many of the Corinthians, as they heard, were believing and being baptized.
reason: ἀρχισυνάγωγος is "synagogue ruler" in most of the edition (Mark 5:22, 35, 36, 38; Luke 8:49; Acts 13:15).

old: Then they all took hold of Sosthenes, the synagogue leader, and began beating him in front of the tribunal; and Gallio was not concerned about any of these things.
new: Then they all took hold of Sosthenes, the synagogue ruler, and began beating him in front of the tribunal; and Gallio was not concerned about any of these things.
reason: ἀρχισυνάγωγος is "synagogue ruler" in most of the edition (Mark 5:22, 35, 36, 38; Luke 8:49; Acts 13:15).

old: These men went ahead and were waiting for us in Troas.
new: These men came and were waiting for us in Troas.
reason: This Greek reads προσελθόντες ('having come/approached'); 'went ahead' renders the other reading προελθόντες.

old: The critical Greek text reads proselthontes (lit. 'having come forward/arrived'), while other manuscripts read proelthontes ('having gone ahead'); in context it conveys that they traveled ahead to wait at Troas.
new: The critical Greek text reads proselthontes (lit. 'having come forward/arrived'), while other manuscripts read proelthontes ('having gone ahead').
reason: Removes the claim that the text 'conveys that they traveled ahead', which reads the variant proelthontes into this text.

old: The Greek phrasing blends two idioms ('consider my life of no account' and 'consider my life precious to myself') to emphasize Paul's complete devotion to his mission.
new: The Greek phrasing blends two idioms ('consider my life of no account' and 'consider my life precious to myself').
reason: 'To emphasize Paul's complete devotion to his mission' is devotional comment, not explanation of the Greek.

old: This saying of Jesus is not recorded in any of the four Gospels, preserving an independent oral tradition of His teaching.
new: This saying of Jesus is not recorded in any of the four Gospels.
reason: 'Preserving an independent oral tradition of His teaching' is a historical-critical claim beyond the Greek; keep the factual statement only.

old: Looking intently at the Council, Paul said, "Men, brothers, I have conducted my life before God in all good conscience until this day."
new: Looking intently at the Sanhedrin, Paul said, "Men, brothers, I have conducted my life before God in all good conscience until this day."
reason: τῷ συνεδρίῳ is the same body called 'the whole Sanhedrin' in 22:30 and 'Sanhedrin' throughout the Gospels and Acts 5-6.

old: Now knowing that one part was Sadducees and the other Pharisees, Paul cried out in the Council, "Men, brothers, I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees! Concerning the hope and resurrection of the dead I am on trial."
new: Now knowing that one part was Sadducees and the other Pharisees, Paul cried out in the Sanhedrin, "Men, brothers, I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees! Concerning the hope and resurrection of the dead I am on trial."
reason: ἐν τῷ συνεδρίῳ: edition renders συνέδριον (the Jewish high council) as 'Sanhedrin' (22:30; Gospels; Acts 5-6).

old: And as a great dissension developed, the tribune, fearing that Paul might be torn to pieces by them, commanded the troops to go down and seize him from their midst and bring him into the barracks.
new: And as a great dissension developed, the commander, fearing that Paul might be torn to pieces by them, commanded the troops to go down and seize him from their midst and bring him into the barracks.
reason: ὁ χιλίαρχος is 'the commander' in 21:31-22:29 (and John 18:12); same officer, same term.

old: Now therefore, you, along with the Council, notify the tribune so that he will bring him down to you, as though you were about to investigate the matters concerning him more closely; and as for us, before he comes near, we are ready to kill him."
new: Now therefore, you, along with the Sanhedrin, notify the commander so that he will bring him down to you, as though you were about to investigate the matters concerning him more closely; and as for us, before he comes near, we are ready to kill him."
reason: τῷ χιλιάρχῳ and τῷ συνεδρίῳ rendered as elsewhere in the edition ('commander', 'Sanhedrin'; cf. 21:31-22:30).

old: Then Paul called one of the centurions to him and said, "Lead this young man to the tribune, for he has something to report to him."
new: Then Paul called one of the centurions to him and said, "Lead this young man to the commander, for he has something to report to him."
reason: πρὸς τὸν χιλίαρχον: 'commander' as in 21:31-22:29.

old: So he took him and brought him to the tribune and said, "The prisoner Paul called me to him and asked me to bring this young man to you, since he has something to tell you."
new: So he took him and brought him to the commander and said, "The prisoner Paul called me to him and asked me to bring this young man to you, since he has something to tell you."
reason: πρὸς τὸν χιλίαρχον: 'commander' as in 21:31-22:29.

old: And the tribune took him by the hand and, withdrawing privately, began to inquire, "What is it that you have to report to me?"
new: And the commander took him by the hand and, withdrawing privately, began to inquire, "What is it that you have to report to me?"
reason: ὁ χιλίαρχος: 'commander' as in 21:31-22:29.

old: And he said, "The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul down to the Council tomorrow, as though you were going to inquire somewhat more closely concerning him.
new: And he said, "The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul down to the Sanhedrin tomorrow, as though you were going to inquire somewhat more closely concerning him.
reason: εἰς τὸ συνέδριον: 'Sanhedrin' as in 22:30 and elsewhere in the edition.

old: The critical text reads the singular participle mellon ("as though you were going to inquire"), attributing the pretext to the tribune, whereas some manuscripts read plural forms referring to the Council.
new: The critical text reads the singular participle mellon ("as though you were going to inquire"), attributing the pretext to the commander, whereas some manuscripts read plural forms referring to the Sanhedrin.
reason: Note terminology aligned with the verse renderings of χιλίαρχος and συνέδριον.

old: So the tribune dismissed the young man, charging him, "Tell no one that you have reported these things to me."
new: So the commander dismissed the young man, charging him, "Tell no one that you have reported these things to me."
reason: ὁ χιλίαρχος: 'commander' as in 21:31-22:29.

old: And wanting to ascertain the charge for which they were accusing him, I brought him down to their Council.
new: And wanting to ascertain the charge for which they were accusing him, I brought him down to their Sanhedrin.
reason: εἰς τὸ συνέδριον αὐτῶν: 'Sanhedrin' as in 22:30 and elsewhere in the edition.

old: who even attempted to profane the temple, so we seized him.
new: who even attempted to profane the temple, and we seized him.
reason: ὃν καὶ ἐκρατήσαμεν is a relative clause ('whom we also seized'), not a result clause; 'so' adds a causal link.

old: The earliest manuscripts omit the material traditionally numbered as verse 7 (along with portions of verses 6 and 8) describing Lysias intervening by force; in the shorter text, "from him" in 24:8 refers directly to Paul.
new: The earliest manuscripts lack the material traditionally numbered as verse 7 (with portions of verses 6 and 8) describing Lysias intervening by force; the Saints Greek Critical Text prints verse 7 within double brackets ⟦ ⟧ (shown as an additional verse). In the shorter text, "from him" in 24:8 refers directly to Paul.
reason: Note did not reflect that the critical text prints 24:7 in ⟦ ⟧.

old: ⟦But Lysias the tribune came by and with great force took him away out of our hands,⟧
new: ⟦But Lysias the commander came by and with great force took him away out of our hands,⟧
reason: Λυσίας ὁ χιλιαρχος: 'commander' as in 21:31-22:29.

old: Or let these men themselves say what wrongdoing they found when I stood before the Council,
new: Or let these men themselves say what wrongdoing they found when I stood before the Sanhedrin,
reason: ἐπὶ τοῦ συνεδρίου: 'Sanhedrin' as in 22:30 and elsewhere in the edition.

old: Then Felix, having quite accurate knowledge of the matters concerning the Way, put them off, saying, "When Lysias the tribune comes down, I will decide your case."
new: Then Felix, having quite accurate knowledge of the matters concerning the Way, put them off, saying, "When Lysias the commander comes down, I will decide your case."
reason: Λυσίας ὁ χιλίαρχος: 'commander' as in 21:31-22:29.

old: Now when several days had passed, King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea to greet Festus.
new: Now when several days had passed, King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea and greeted Festus.
reason: This text has the aorist ἀσπασάμενοι; 'to greet' renders the future participle ἀσπασόμενοι of later manuscripts.

old: So on the next day, when Agrippa and Bernice came with great pomp and entered the audience hall along with the military tribunes and the prominent men of the city, at the command of Festus Paul was brought in.
new: So on the next day, when Agrippa and Bernice came with great pomp and entered the audience hall along with the military commanders and the prominent men of the city, at the command of Festus Paul was brought in.
reason: χιλιάρχοις: the edition renders χιλίαρχος 'commander' (21:31-22:29; Mark 6:21 'military commanders').

old: Greek ei (literally "whether") introduces debated propositions confirmed by Scripture, and pathetos literally means "subject to suffering" or "destined to suffer."
new: Greek ei (literally "whether") introduces the propositions at issue, and pathetos literally means "subject to suffering" or "destined to suffer."
reason: 'Confirmed by Scripture' is an assertion, not an explanation of the Greek conjunction.

old: And Agrippa said to Paul, "In a short time you are trying to persuade me to become a Christian."
new: And Agrippa said to Paul, "In a short time you are trying to persuade me to act as a Christian."
reason: This text reads ποιῆσαι ('to make/do'), not γενέσθαι ('to become'), as the existing note itself states; 'become' follows the later reading.

old: For this very night an angel of the God to whom I belong and whom I also serve stood beside me,
new: For this night an angel of the God to whom I belong and whom I also serve stood beside me,
reason: ταύτῃ τῇ νυκτί is simply 'this night'; 'very' has no Greek basis (contrast αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ in 22:13).

old: Verse 29 ("And when he had said these things, the Jews departed, having a great dispute among themselves") is absent from the earliest and best manuscripts and is omitted in the critical text.
new: Verse 29 ("And when he had said these things, the Jews departed, having a great dispute among themselves") is absent from the earliest manuscripts; the Saints Greek Critical Text prints it in double brackets ⟦ ⟧.
reason: The note says the verse 'is omitted in the critical text', but the Saints Greek Critical Text includes 28:29 within ⟦ ⟧; 'and best' is an evaluative claim.

old: Greek horisthentos can mean 'designated,' 'appointed,' or 'declared.' The phrase 'Spirit of holiness' reflects a Semitic idiom, and 'by the resurrection of the dead' literally translates ex anastaseos nekron.
new: Greek horisthentos can mean 'designated,' 'appointed,' or 'declared.' The phrase 'Spirit of holiness' reflects a Semitic idiom and may refer to the Holy Spirit or to Christ's own spirit; 'by the resurrection of the dead' literally translates ex anastaseos nekron.
reason: Capitalized 'Spirit' silently decides the disputed referent of πνεῦμα ἁγιωσύνης; the note should state that the Greek allows either reading.

old: always in my prayers, requesting that somehow now at last I may succeed in the will of God to come to you.
new: always in my prayers, asking if somehow now at last I may succeed in the will of God to come to you.
reason: εἴ πως is 'if somehow' (so rendered at 11:14); 'requesting that' drops the conditional εἰ and turns a tentative hope into a direct petition.

old: May that never happen! Rather, let God prove true, and every person a liar, just as it is written: "So that You may be justified in Your words and will prevail when You are judged."
new: May it never happen! Rather, let God prove true, and every person a liar, just as it is written: "So that You may be justified in Your words and will prevail when You are judged."
reason: μὴ γένοιτο is rendered 'May it never happen!' in 6:2, 6:15, 7:7, 7:13, 11:1, 11:11; align this formula.

old: May that never happen! For otherwise, how will God judge the world?
new: May it never happen! For otherwise, how will God judge the world?
reason: μὴ γένοιτο is rendered 'May it never happen!' elsewhere in Romans (6:2, 6:15, 7:7, 7:13, 11:1, 11:11).

old: But now, apart from the law, a righteousness of God has been revealed, attested by the Law and the Prophets,
new: But now, apart from the law, a righteousness of God has been manifested, attested by the Law and the Prophets,
reason: πεφανέρωται is φανερόω, rendered 'manifested' in 16:26; 'revealed' is this edition's word for ἀποκαλύπτω (1:17-18, 8:18), so it merges two different verbs.

old: Do we then nullify the law through faith? May that never happen! On the contrary, we establish the law.
new: Do we then nullify the law through faith? May it never happen! On the contrary, we establish the law.
reason: μὴ γένοιτο is rendered 'May it never happen!' elsewhere in Romans (6:2, 6:15, 7:7, 7:13, 11:1, 11:11).

old: The Saints Greek Critical Text reads the hortatory subjunctive echomen ("let us have"), supported by the earliest manuscripts, rather than the indicative echomen ("we have").
new: The Saints Greek Critical Text reads the hortatory subjunctive echōmen ("let us have"), supported by the earliest manuscripts, rather than the indicative echomen ("we have").
reason: The note transliterated ἔχωμεν and ἔχομεν identically, so the contrast it describes was invisible; mark the long vowel of the subjunctive.

old: For if we have become united with Him in the likeness of His death, we shall certainly also be united with Him in the likeness of His resurrection,
new: For if we have become united with the likeness of His death, we shall certainly also be united with the likeness of His resurrection,
reason: σύμφυτοι takes the dative τῷ ὁμοιώματι ('united with the likeness'); 'with Him' is supplied twice and fixes one disputed construal of the dative.

old: For in this hope we were saved; yet hope that is seen is not hope, for why does anyone hope for what he sees?
new: For in this hope we were saved; yet hope that is seen is not hope, for who hopes for what he sees?
reason: The Greek is ὃ γὰρ βλέπει τίς ἐλπίζει, 'who hopes for what he sees?'; 'why' follows the variant τί καὶ ἐλπίζει, not this text.

old: But if we hope for what we do not see, we eagerly await it through perseverance.
new: But if we hope for what we do not see, we eagerly await it through endurance.
reason: ὑπομονή is 'endurance' everywhere else in Romans (2:7, 5:3-4, 15:4-5); 'persevering' is used for προσκαρτερέω (12:12).

old: What then will we say to these things? If God is for us, who is against us?
new: What then shall we say to these things? If God is for us, who is against us?
reason: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν is 'What then shall we say' in 3:5, 4:1, 6:1, 7:7, 9:14, 9:30.

old: Just as it stands written, "For Your sake we are being put to death all day long; we were reckoned as sheep for slaughter."
new: Just as it is written, "For Your sake we are being put to death all day long; we were reckoned as sheep for slaughter."
reason: καθὼς γέγραπται is 'just as it is written' throughout Romans (1:17, 2:24, 3:4, 3:10, 4:17, 9:13, etc.).

old: who are Israelites, to whom belong the adoption as sons, the glory, the covenants, the giving of the law, the sacred service, and the promises;
new: who are Israelites, to whom belong the adoption, the glory, the covenants, the giving of the law, the sacred service, and the promises;
reason: υἱοθεσία is rendered simply 'adoption' in 8:15 and 8:23; 'as sons' is an expansion.

old: And not only this, but also Rebekah, having conceived by one man, our father Isaac--
new: And not only this, but also Rebekah, having conceived by one man, our father Isaac—
reason: Double hyphen is a typographic error; the edition uses the em dash.

old: not from works but from Him who calls--it was said to her, "The older will serve the younger,"
new: not from works but from Him who calls—it was said to her, "The older will serve the younger,"
reason: Double hyphen is a typographic error; the edition uses the em dash.

old: What then shall we say? Is there unrighteousness with God? Let it never be!
new: What then shall we say? Is there unrighteousness with God? May it never happen!
reason: μὴ γένοιτο is rendered 'May it never happen!' elsewhere in Romans (6:2, 6:15, 7:7, 7:13, 11:1, 11:11).

old: and in order to make known the riches of His glory upon vessels of mercy, which He prepared beforehand for glory--
new: and in order to make known the riches of His glory upon vessels of mercy, which He prepared beforehand for glory—
reason: Double hyphen is a typographic error; the edition uses the em dash.

old: Rather, what does it say? "The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart"--that is, the word of faith that we proclaim:
new: Rather, what does it say? "The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart"—that is, the word of faith that we proclaim:
reason: Double hyphen is a typographic error; the edition uses the em dash.

old: Literally "whom they have not heard" (taking the genitive relative pronoun as the direct object of hearing), indicating that Christ Himself is heard in the proclamation of the gospel.
new: Literally "whom they have not heard," taking the genitive relative pronoun as the direct object of hearing.
reason: The closing clause is a theological inference, not an explanation of the Greek; keep only the grammatical point.

old: λογικὴν λατρείαν literally means "rational/reasonable cultic service" (often rendered "spiritual worship"); "rational service of worship" preserves both the philosophical sense of λογικός (engaging the mind, picked up in 12:2) and the sacrificial sense of λατρεία.
new: λογικὴν λατρείαν literally means "rational/reasonable cultic service" (also understood as "spiritual worship"); "rational service of worship" preserves both the philosophical sense of λογικός (engaging the mind, picked up in 12:2) and the sacrificial sense of λατρεία.
reason: "Often rendered" is a claim about other translations; restate it as an alternative sense of λογικός.

old: Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but give place to wrath; for it stands written, "Vengeance belongs to Me; I will repay," says the Lord.
new: Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but give place to wrath; for it is written, "Vengeance belongs to Me; I will repay," says the Lord.
reason: γέγραπται γάρ is 'for it is written' elsewhere in Romans (14:11).

old: Let every person submit to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except from God, and the ones that exist have been appointed by God.
new: Let every person submit to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except by God, and the ones that exist have been appointed by God.
reason: This text reads εἰ μὴ ὑπὸ θεοῦ ('by God', as in the next clause); 'from God' follows the variant ἀπὸ θεοῦ.

old: For to this end Christ died and came to life again, so that He might be Lord of both the dead and the living.
new: For to this end Christ died and came to life, so that He might be Lord of both the dead and the living.
reason: ἔζησεν is simply 'lived/came to life'; 'again' has no basis here and echoes the variant ἀνέζησεν ('revived').

old: and thus making it my ambition to proclaim the gospel not where Christ was already named, so that I might not build upon another's foundation,
new: and thus making it my ambition to proclaim the gospel not where Christ had been named, so that I might not build upon another's foundation,
reason: ὠνομάσθη is just 'was named'; 'already' is an added intensifier, and the past perfect conveys the prior naming without it.

old: but just as it is written, "Those who were never told about Him will see, and those who have not heard will understand."
new: but just as it is written, "Those who were not told about Him will see, and those who have not heard will understand."
reason: Οἷς οὐκ ἀνηγγέλη has plain οὐκ 'not'; 'never' intensifies the negation.

old: The closing doxology (16:25-27) is positioned at different places in various ancient manuscripts (such as after 14:23 or 15:33), though the earliest witnesses place it at the end of the letter.
new: The closing doxology (16:25-27) is positioned at different places in ancient manuscripts (after 14:23, after 15:33, or at the end of the letter); this text prints it here and also, in double brackets, after 14:23.
reason: The earliest manuscript (P46) places the doxology after 15:33, so 'the earliest witnesses place it at the end' is inaccurate; state the facts neutrally, including this text's own bracketed 14:24-26.

old: Paul, called as an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, and our brother Sosthenes,
new: Paul, called as an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, and Sosthenes the brother,
reason: Σωσθένης ὁ ἀδελφός is "Sosthenes the brother"; "our" has no Greek basis (cf. 16:12 "Apollos the brother").

old: The Greek construction links righteousness, sanctification, and redemption closely together as an unfolding of how Christ became wisdom from God for believers.
new: The particles te kai ... kai bind righteousness, sanctification, and redemption closely together; they may explain "wisdom from God" or stand alongside it.
reason: The note presented one exegesis of the τε καί ... καί series as a fact about the Greek; rewritten to state the construction and its two possible readings.

old: For whenever someone says, "I am of Paul," and another, "I of Apollos," are you not merely human?
new: For whenever someone says, "I am of Paul," and another, "I of Apollos," are you not human beings?
reason: οὐκ ἄνθρωποί ἐστε is "are you not human beings?"; "merely" is an added qualifier with no Greek basis.

old: The critical Greek text reads "merely human" (literally "human beings") rather than "fleshly," which appears in some later manuscripts under the influence of verse 3.
new: The critical Greek text reads "human beings" rather than "fleshly," which appears in some later manuscripts under the influence of verse 3.
reason: Brought into line with the corrected verse; the Greek ἄνθρωποι has no word for "merely."

old: For I am aware of nothing against myself, yet I am not acquitted by this; the One who examines me is the Lord.
new: For I am aware of nothing against myself, yet I am not justified by this; the One who examines me is the Lord.
reason: δεδικαίωμαι is from δικαιόω, rendered "justify" throughout this edition (e.g. 6:11 "you were justified").

old: So then let us observe the festival, not with old leaven nor with the leaven of malice and evil, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
new: So then let us observe the feast, not with old leaven nor with the leaven of malice and evil, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
reason: NT-wide consistency pass (ἀμὴν λέγω "Truly I say to you"; μὴ γένοιτο; ἑορτή "feast"; μύρον "perfume"; λῃστής "robber"; οἱ δώδεκα; γέγραπται; ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς in Matthew).

old: I speak to your shame. Is it really so that there is not one wise person among you who will be able to decide between his brothers,
new: I speak to your shame. Is it so that there is not one wise person among you who will be able to decide between his brothers,
reason: οὕτως is simply "so"; the intensifier "really" has no Greek basis.

old: The two Greek terms malakoi ("effeminate men") and arsenokoitai ("men who lie with males") denote respectively the passive and active partners in male same-sex intercourse in the Greco-Roman world.
new: Greek malakoi (literally "soft ones") and arsenokoitai (a compound of "male" and "bed") are commonly understood as the passive and active partners in male same-sex intercourse, though their precise sense is debated.
reason: The note stated a debated lexical interpretation as settled fact; rewritten to give the literal sense and the common reading neutrally.

old: And some of you were these very things; yet you were washed, yet you were sanctified, yet you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and in the Spirit of our God.
new: And some of you were these things; yet you were washed, yet you were sanctified, yet you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and in the Spirit of our God.
reason: ταῦτα is "these things"; the intensifier "very" has no Greek basis.

old: Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? Should I then take the members of Christ and make them members of a prostitute? By no means!
new: Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? Should I then take the members of Christ and make them members of a prostitute? May it never happen!
reason: NT-wide consistency pass (ἀμὴν λέγω "Truly I say to you"; μὴ γένοιτο; ἑορτή "feast"; μύρον "perfume"; λῃστής "robber"; οἱ δώδεκα; γέγραπται; ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς in Matthew).

old: Literally "Every sin," without adding "other"; some interpreters read the first clause as another Corinthian slogan Paul refutes, while others take it as Paul's own statement highlighting the unique bodily union of sexual immorality.
new: Literally "Every sin"; some interpreters read the first clause as another Corinthian slogan that Paul refutes, while others take it as Paul's own statement.
reason: Removed the implied comment on other translations ("without adding 'other'") and the interpretive gloss; kept the factual alternatives.

old: for you were purchased at a price. Glorify God, then, in your body.
new: for you were bought with a price. Glorify God, then, in your body.
reason: ἠγοράσθητε γὰρ τιμῆς is the same Greek as 7:23 ("You were bought with a price"); ἀγοράζω is "buy" in this book (cf. 7:30).

old: Yet if the unbeliever separates, let him separate. The brother or the sister is not bound in such cases; rather, God has called us to peace.
new: Yet if the unbeliever separates, let him separate. The brother or the sister is not bound in such cases; rather, God has called us in peace.
reason: ἐν εἰρήνῃ κέκληκεν is "has called in peace" (ἐν, not εἰς); "to peace" changes the relation.

old: Now concerning things sacrificed to idols, we know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge inflates, but love builds up.
new: Now concerning things sacrificed to idols, we know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.
reason: φυσιοῖ is from φυσιόω, rendered "puffed up" elsewhere in this book (4:6, 4:18, 4:19, 5:2, 13:4).

old: Numbers 25:9 records a total of 24,000 dead in the plague; Paul's figure of 23,000 falling 'in a single day' likely reflects either a rounded number or those who fell on one day.
new: Numbers 25:9 gives the number of those who died in the plague as 24,000.
reason: Removed speculative harmonization (and a misquote of the verse's "in one day"); kept the factual cross-reference.

old: for the earth belongs to the Lord, and all its fullness.
new: for the earth belongs to the Lord, and its fullness.
reason: τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτῆς is "its fullness"; "all" has no Greek basis.

old: For there must indeed be factions among you, so that those who are approved may also become evident among you.
new: For there must also be factions among you, so that those who are approved may also become evident among you.
reason: δεῖ γὰρ καὶ αἱρέσεις: καί is "also" (factions in addition to the σχίσματα of v. 18), not an intensifier "indeed".

old: And God has appointed in the church, first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then miracles, then gifts of healings, helps, administrations, and kinds of tongues.
new: And God has appointed some in the church: first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then miracles, then gifts of healings, helps, administrations, and kinds of tongues.
reason: οὓς μὲν ἔθετο ("some/those whom He appointed") was not represented.

old: Greek τὸ τέλειον ('what is complete' or 'the perfect') contrasts directly with τὸ ἐκ μέρους ('what is in part') and is widely understood as the full maturity realized at Christ's return.
new: Greek τὸ τέλειον ('what is complete' or 'the perfect') contrasts directly with τὸ ἐκ μέρους ('what is in part').
reason: The referent of τὸ τέλειον is disputed; the note's interpretive claim decides it and is removed, keeping the lexical contrast.

old: and that He appeared to Cephas, then to the Twelve.
new: and that He appeared to Cephas, then to the twelve.
reason: NT-wide consistency pass (ἀμὴν λέγω "Truly I say to you"; μὴ γένοιτο; ἑορτή "feast"; μύρον "perfume"; λῃστής "robber"; οἱ δώδεκα; γέγραπται; ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς in Matthew).

old: The Greek term ektrōmati (with the definite article) literally denotes a miscarriage or an abnormally early birth, underscoring the sudden, irregular, and humbling character of Paul's call as an apostle.
new: The Greek term ektrōmati (with the definite article) literally denotes a miscarriage or an abnormally early birth.
reason: Removed interpretive commentary; kept the lexical explanation of ἐκτρώματι.

old: Then comes the end, when He hands over the kingdom to God the Father, once He has abolished every rule and every authority and power.
new: Then comes the end, when He hands over the kingdom to the God and Father, once He has abolished every rule and every authority and power.
reason: τῷ θεῷ καὶ πατρί is "to the God and Father"; καί was dropped.

old: The phrase "baptized on behalf of the dead" (hyper tōn nekrōn) is famously debated, with proposals ranging from vicarious baptism for deceased persons to baptism undertaken in hope of rejoining dead believers. Paul cites the practice simply to expose the inconsistency of denying the resurrection, without explaining or endorsing it.
new: The phrase "baptized on behalf of the dead" (hyper tōn nekrōn) is famously debated, with proposals ranging from vicarious baptism for deceased persons to baptism undertaken in hope of rejoining dead believers.
reason: The second sentence is a confessional judgment ("without ... endorsing it") not stated by the Greek; removed.

old: Sober up properly and stop sinning, for some have no knowledge of God; I speak this to your shame.
new: Sober up properly and stop sinning, for some have no knowledge of God; I speak to your shame.
reason: πρὸς ἐντροπὴν ὑμῖν λαλῶ has no object "this"; matches the same phrase in 6:5 ("I speak to your shame").

old: Greek psychikon literally means "soulish" (pertaining to the psychē, natural mortal life), contrasted with pneumatikon ("spiritual"), meaning a resurrection body animated by the Spirit rather than an immaterial body.
new: Greek psychikon literally means "soulish" (pertaining to the psychē, natural mortal life), contrasted with pneumatikon ("spiritual").
reason: Removed a theological interpretation of σῶμα πνευματικόν that the Greek does not state; kept the lexical contrast.

old: who rescued us from so great a death and will rescue us; on Him we have set our hope that He will continue to rescue us still further,
new: who rescued us from so great a death and will rescue us; on Him we have set our hope that He will rescue us yet again,
reason: καὶ ἔτι ῥύσεται is simply "will also yet rescue"; "continue to ... still further" renders ἔτι twice and expands it.

old: The verb καταργέω (also in vv. 11, 13, 14) means "render inoperative," "bring to an end," or "do away with," implying in context the fading and superseding of the old covenant's glory.
new: The verb καταργέω (also in vv. 11, 13, 14) means "render inoperative," "bring to an end," or "do away with."
reason: The added clause about "fading and superseding" is a theological interpretation, not lexis; καταργέω does not mean "fade."

old: Therefore we do not lose heart; even though our outer person is decaying, still our inner person is being renewed day by day.
new: Therefore we do not lose heart; but even though our outer person is decaying, still our inner person is being renewed day by day.
reason: The first ἀλλʼ (after οὐκ ἐγκακοῦμεν) is unrepresented; only the second ἀλλʼ is rendered by "still."

old: Now the One who prepared us for this very purpose is God, who gave us the pledge of the Spirit.
new: Now the One who prepared us for this very purpose is God, who gave us the down payment of the Spirit.
reason: τὸν ἀρραβῶνα τοῦ πνεύματος is rendered "the down payment of the Spirit" in 1:22 (with a note) and Eph 1:14; same phrase, same sense.

old: Greek "eidos" denotes visible appearance or outward form, often rendered "sight" in contrast to faith.
new: Greek "eidos" denotes visible appearance or outward form, here contrasted with faith.
reason: Removes a claim about how other translations render the word; keeps the lexical point.

old: namely, that in Christ God was reconciling the world to Himself, not counting their trespasses against them, and having committed to us the word of reconciliation.
new: namely, that God was in Christ reconciling the world to Himself, not counting their trespasses against them, and having committed to us the word of reconciliation.
reason: θεὸς ἦν ἐν Χριστῷ κόσμον καταλλάσσων is ambiguous (periphrastic "was reconciling" or "was in Christ, reconciling"); following the Greek order keeps both readings instead of deciding for one.

old: Greek "hamartia" ("sin") here may carry the sense of "sin offering" (as often in the Septuagint) or denote Christ's substitutionary identification with human sin.
new: Greek "hamartia" ("sin") here may carry the sense of "sin offering" (as often in the Septuagint).
reason: "Christ's substitutionary identification with human sin" is a doctrinal formulation, not a note on the Greek.

old: for He says, "At an acceptable time I listened to you, and on a day of salvation I helped you." Look, now is the truly favorable time; look, now is the day of salvation—
new: for He says, "At an acceptable time I listened to you, and on a day of salvation I helped you." Look, now is the acceptable time; look, now is the day of salvation—
reason: εὐπρόσδεκτος is "acceptable" elsewhere in the edition (Rom 15:16, 15:31; 2 Cor 8:12) and here echoes δεκτῷ "acceptable" in the quotation; "truly" is the edition's rendering of ἀμήν.

old: indeed, the signs of an apostle were carried out among you with all perseverance, by signs and wonders and works of power.
new: indeed, the signs of an apostle were carried out among you with all endurance, by signs and wonders and works of power.
reason: ὑπομονή is "endurance" in 1:6 and 6:4 of this letter and in nearly all of the edition.

old: for I fear that somehow when I come I may not find you such as I wish, and I may be found by you such as you do not wish—that somehow there may be strife, jealousy, outbursts of anger, selfish rivalries, slanders, whisperings, arrogant conceits, disorders;
new: for I fear that somehow when I come I may not find you such as I wish, and I may be found by you such as you do not wish—that somehow there may be strife, jealousy, outbursts of rage, selfish ambitions, slanders, whisperings, arrogant conceits, disorders;
reason: The same θυμοί, ἐριθεῖαι are "outbursts of rage, selfish ambitions" in Gal 5:20; ἐριθεία is "selfish ambition" throughout the edition (Rom 2:8; Phil 1:17; 2:3; Jas 3:14, 16).

old: For we are not able to do anything against the truth, but only on behalf of the truth.
new: For we are not able to do anything against the truth, but on behalf of the truth.
reason: ἀλλὰ ὑπὲρ τῆς ἀληθείας has no word for "only."

old: Paul pairs two Greek words for 'another' across verses 6-7 (heteros and allos), highlighting that this rival message is a different kind of message rather than another legitimate version of the gospel.
new: Paul uses two Greek words for 'other' across verses 6-7: heteros ('different,' v. 6) and allos ('another,' v. 7).
reason: States the lexical fact neutrally; the claim about a "different kind" versus a "legitimate version" is interpretive.

old: And I was still unknown by face to the churches of Judea that are in Christ;
new: And I was unknown by face to the churches of Judea that are in Christ;
reason: ἤμην δὲ ἀγνοούμενος has no ἔτι; "still" is supplied.

old: But if, while seeking to be justified in Christ, we ourselves were also found to be sinners, is Christ then a servant of sin? May it never be!
new: But if, while seeking to be justified in Christ, we ourselves were also found to be sinners, is Christ then a servant of sin? May it never happen!
reason: NT-wide consistency pass (ἀμὴν λέγω "Truly I say to you"; μὴ γένοιτο; ἑορτή "feast"; μύρον "perfume"; λῃστής "robber"; οἱ δώδεκα; γέγραπται; ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς in Matthew).

old: This compressed statement is widely debated; Paul contrasts the law, which involved a mediator representing multiple parties, with God's direct, unilateral promise.
new: This compressed statement is widely debated; it is commonly read as contrasting the law, which involved a mediator representing multiple parties, with God's direct, unilateral promise.
reason: The note calls the verse debated but then states one interpretation as fact; it now presents that reading as an interpretation.

old: Is the law then against the promises of God? Certainly not! For if a law had been given that was able to impart life, then righteousness would indeed have been from the law.
new: Is the law then against the promises of God? May it never be! For if a law had been given that was able to impart life, then righteousness would indeed have been from the law.
reason: μὴ γένοιτο is optative and is rendered "May it never be!" in 2:17; "Certainly not!" loses the mood.

old: Is the law then against the promises of God? May it never be! For if a law had been given that was able to impart life, then righteousness would indeed have been from the law.
new: Is the law then against the promises of God? May it never happen! For if a law had been given that was able to impart life, then righteousness would indeed have been from the law.
reason: NT-wide consistency pass (ἀμὴν λέγω "Truly I say to you"; μὴ γένοιτο; ἑορτή "feast"; μύρον "perfume"; λῃστής "robber"; οἱ δώδεκα; γέγραπται; ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς in Matthew).

old: For if someone thinks himself to be something while being nothing, he deceives his own mind.
new: For if someone thinks himself to be something while being nothing, he deceives himself.
reason: The object of φρεναπατᾷ is ἑαυτόν, "himself"; "his own mind" reads the verb's etymology into the object.

old: The neuter pronoun "this" (touto) points to the entire statement of salvation by grace through faith rather than to "faith" (feminine in Greek) alone.
new: The pronoun "this" (touto) is neuter, while "grace" and "faith" are feminine; it may refer to the whole preceding clause.
reason: Note asserted one side of a disputed interpretation; rewritten to state only the grammatical fact neutrally.

old: that at that time you were apart from Christ, estranged from the citizenship of Israel and foreigners to the covenants of the promise, not having hope and without God in the world.
new: that at that time you were apart from Christ, alienated from the citizenship of Israel and foreigners to the covenants of the promise, not having hope and without God in the world.
reason: ἀπηλλοτριωμένοι is rendered "alienated" in Eph 4:18 and Col 1:21 in the same sense.

old: And having come, He proclaimed peace to you who were far away and peace to those who were near;
new: And having come, He proclaimed good news of peace to you who were far away and peace to those who were near;
reason: εὐηγγελίσατο εἰρήνην is "proclaimed good news of peace" (cf. Acts 10:36 in this edition); "proclaimed" alone drops the good-news sense.

old: to me, less than the least of all saints, this grace was given—to proclaim to the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ,
new: to me, less than the least of all saints, this grace was given—to proclaim to the Gentiles the good news of the unsearchable riches of Christ,
reason: εὐαγγελίσασθαι means to proclaim as good news; edition renders εὐαγγελίζομαι + object as "proclaim the good news of".

old: Therefore, having put off falsehood, let each one speak truth with his neighbor, because we are members of one another.
new: Therefore, having put off falsehood, speak truth, each one of you, with his neighbor, because we are members of one another.
reason: λαλεῖτε is a second-person plural imperative with ἕκαστος in apposition; "let each one speak" shifts it to a third-person jussive.

old: Let no corrupt word come out of your mouth, but only whatever is good for building up according to the need, so that it may give grace to those who hear.
new: Let no corrupt word come out of your mouth, but whatever is good for building up according to the need, so that it may give grace to those who hear.
reason: ἀλλʼ εἴ τις ἀγαθός has no word for "only"; the intensifier is added.

old: "Of Christ and God" places a single Greek article before both nouns, which many grammarians understand as identifying Christ as God ("of Him who is Christ and God").
new: A single Greek article governs both nouns (tou Christou kai theou); the construction may denote one referent or two closely joined ones.
reason: Note steered a doctrinal reading of the article construction; rewritten to state the Greek neutrally.

old: The phrase en aphtharsia literally means "in incorruptibility" (or "imperishability"), conveying an undying, uncorrupted love for Christ; the earliest manuscripts omit "Amen."
new: The phrase en aphtharsia literally means "in incorruptibility" (or "imperishability"); the earliest manuscripts omit "Amen."
reason: The phrase could attach to "grace" or to "love"; the note's interpretive gloss decided the attachment and was removed.

old: for even in Thessalonica you sent to me more than once for my need.
new: for even in Thessalonica you sent to me both once and twice for my need.
reason: καὶ ἅπαξ καὶ δίς is a clear idiom kept literal as "both once and twice" in 1 Thess 2:18; "more than once" paraphrases.

old: "Firstborn of all creation" denotes preeminence and supreme rank over all creation rather than being the first created being, as v. 16 immediately explains.
new: Greek prōtotokos ("firstborn") can denote priority in time or preeminence in rank.
reason: Note made a doctrinal assertion; rewritten to give only the lexical range of πρωτότοκος.

old: because God was pleased for all the fullness to dwell in Him,
new: because in Him all the fullness was pleased to dwell,
reason: The Greek has no "God"; εὐδόκησεν πᾶν τὸ πλήρωμα κατοικῆσαι is rendered as it stands, with the alternative given in the note.

old: "God" is supplied as the implied subject of "was pleased," confirmed by the masculine participle "having made peace" in v. 20; alternatively, "all the fullness" may be taken as the grammatical subject ("in Him all the fullness was pleased to dwell").
new: The Greek has no separate subject for "was pleased"; "all the fullness" may be the subject, or "God" may be understood ("God was pleased for all the fullness to dwell in Him").
reason: Updated to match the verse change and to state the ambiguity without claiming one reading is confirmed.

old: and through Him to reconcile all things to Himself, having made peace through the blood of His cross—through Him, whether the things on the earth or the things in the heavens.
new: and through Him to reconcile all things to Him, having made peace through the blood of His cross—through Him, whether the things on the earth or the things in the heavens.
reason: The text prints εἰς αὐτόν (not reflexive αὑτόν), "to Him," as in v. 16 "for Him"; "Himself" assumed the reflexive and the supplied subject "God".

old: "What is lacking in the afflictions of Christ" does not imply a deficiency in Christ's atoning work, but refers to ongoing missionary sufferings endured in union with Him for the sake of His church.
new: The genitive in "the afflictions of Christ" may denote afflictions Christ Himself endured or afflictions borne for Him or in union with Him.
reason: Note made a doctrinal assertion; rewritten to describe the Greek genitive neutrally.

old: Therefore let no one judge you in food and in drink, or with regard to a festival or a new moon or Sabbaths,
new: Therefore let no one judge you in food and in drink, or with regard to a feast or a new moon or Sabbaths,
reason: NT-wide consistency pass (ἀμὴν λέγω "Truly I say to you"; μὴ γένοιτο; ἑορτή "feast"; μύρον "perfume"; λῃστής "robber"; οἱ δώδεκα; γέγραπται; ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς in Matthew).

old: and not holding fast to the Head, from whom the whole body, being supplied and knit together through the joints and ligaments, grows with a growth from God.
new: and not holding fast to the head, from whom the whole body, being supplied and knit together through the joints and ligaments, grows with a growth from God.
reason: κεφαλή for Christ is lowercase "head" elsewhere in this edition (Col 1:18; 2:10; Eph 1:22; 4:15; 5:23).

old: Many later manuscripts add "upon the sons of disobedience" (likely influenced by Ephesians 5:6); the earlier critical text omits the phrase.
new: The Greek text here lacks "upon the sons of disobedience," which many manuscripts add (compare Ephesians 5:6).
reason: Removed speculation and the unclear "earlier critical text"; stated the reading of this Greek factually.

old: Do not lie to one another, since you have stripped off the old man together with his practices,
new: Do not lie to one another, since you have stripped off the old self together with its practices,
reason: τὸν παλαιὸν ἄνθρωπον is "the old self" in Rom 6:6 and Eph 4:22 in this edition.

old: and have put on the new man, who is being renewed to full knowledge according to the image of the One who created him,
new: and have put on the new self, which is being renewed to full knowledge according to the image of the One who created it,
reason: Matches "the new self, which was created" for the same expression in Eph 4:24, following the change in v. 9.

old: Walk in wisdom toward those outside, making the most of the time.
new: Walk in wisdom toward those outside, redeeming the opportunity.
reason: τὸν καιρὸν ἐξαγοραζόμενοι is rendered "redeeming the opportunity" in Eph 5:16; same phrase, same sense.

old: hindering us from speaking to the Gentiles so that they may be saved, so as always to fill up their sins. But wrath has come upon them completely.
new: hindering us from speaking to the Gentiles so that they may be saved, so as always to fill up their sins. But the wrath has come upon them completely.
reason: ἡ ὀργή has the article, pointing to the specific wrath of 1:10 ("the wrath that is coming").

old: For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, in the same way God will also bring with Him those who have fallen asleep through Jesus.
new: For if we believe that Jesus died and rose, in the same way God will also bring with Him those who have fallen asleep through Jesus.
reason: ἀνέστη is simply "rose"; "again" has no Greek basis.

old: not to be quickly shaken from your reason nor to be alarmed, whether by a spirit, or by a word, or by a letter as if through us, to the effect that the day of the Lord is already present.
new: not to be quickly shaken from your reason nor to be alarmed, whether by a spirit, or by a word, or by a letter as if through us, to the effect that the day of the Lord has come.
reason: ἐνέστηκεν is simply "has come/is present"; "already" has no basis in the Greek.

old: And now you know what restrains him, so that he will be revealed in his own time.
new: And now you know what restrains, so that he will be revealed in his own time.
reason: τὸ κατέχον οἴδατε has no object; "him" is supplied and decides what is restrained.

old: The optative verbs "encourage" and "establish" are grammatically singular in Greek despite the compound subject of Christ and God the Father in 2:16, highlighting their unified action.
new: The optative verbs "encourage" and "establish" are grammatically singular in Greek despite the compound subject of Christ and God the Father in 2:16.
reason: "Highlighting their unified action" is theological interpretation, not a statement about the Greek.

old: Trustworthy is this saying and worthy of complete acceptance, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners—of whom I am the first.
new: Trustworthy is this saying and worthy of all acceptance, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners—of whom I am the first.
reason: πάσης ἀποδοχῆς ἄξιος is rendered "worthy of all acceptance" in the identical formula at 1 Tim 4:9.

old: By setting these things before the brothers, you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus, continually nourished on the words of the faith and of the good teaching that you have closely followed.
new: By setting these things before the brothers, you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus, being nourished on the words of the faith and of the good teaching that you have closely followed.
reason: ἐντρεφόμενος is a plain present participle; "continually" is an added intensifier.

old: "The reading" (τῇ ἀναγνώσει) with the definite article refers to the public reading of Scripture in the assembled church.
new: "The reading" (τῇ ἀναγνώσει) most likely refers to the public reading of Scripture in the assembled church.
reason: All three nouns in the verse carry the article, so the article does not mark this one out; the identification is an interpretation and should be hedged.

old: Now she who is truly a widow and has been left all alone has fixed her hope on God and continues in petitions and prayers night and day,
new: Now she who is truly a widow and has been left alone has fixed her hope on God and continues in petitions and prayers night and day,
reason: μεμονωμένη is "left alone"; "all" is an added intensifier.

old: Therefore I desire younger widows to marry, to bear children, to manage their households, and to give the adversary no opportunity for slander;
new: Therefore I desire younger women to marry, to bear children, to manage their households, and to give the adversary no opportunity for slander;
reason: The Greek has only νεωτέρας ("younger women"); "widows" is supplied from context and narrows the referent.

old: "Those who partake of the benefit" refers to the believing masters who benefit from the faithful service of their Christian slaves.
new: "Those who partake of the benefit" most likely refers to the believing masters who benefit from the faithful service of their Christian slaves.
reason: The referent of οἱ τῆς εὐεργεσίας ἀντιλαμβανόμενοι is debated; the note should not state one reading as certain.

old: Greek omits the definite article before "root," indicating that the love of money is a root from which all kinds of evil grow.
new: Greek has no definite article before "root" (ῥίζα), so the phrase may be read as "a root" or "the root" of all evils.
reason: An anarthrous predicate noun before the verb does not by itself mean "a root," and "all kinds of evil" misstates πάντων τῶν κακῶν ("all evils").

old: which He will display at His own times—the blessed and only Sovereign, the King of those who reign and Lord of those who rule,
new: which He will display at the proper times—the blessed and only Sovereign, the King of those who reign and Lord of those who rule,
reason: καιροῖς ἰδίοις is "at the proper times" (Titus 1:3; cf. 1 Tim 2:6); capitalized "His own" decides the referent of ἰδίοις.

old: which some have professed and so missed the mark regarding the faith. Grace be with you all.
new: which some have professed and so missed the mark regarding the faith. Grace be with you.
reason: Ἡ χάρις μεθʼ ὑμῶν has no πάντων; the plural is explained in the note (cf. 2 Tim 4:22 "with you").

old: But avoid irreverent empty chatter, for they will advance further into ungodliness,
new: But avoid profane empty chatter, for they will advance further into ungodliness,
reason: τὰς βεβήλους κενοφωνίας is rendered "profane empty chatter" in the identical phrase at 1 Tim 6:20 (and βέβηλος "profane" at 1 Tim 4:7).

old: And a servant of the Lord must not quarrel, but be gentle toward all, able to teach, patient when wronged,
new: And a slave of the Lord must not quarrel, but be gentle toward all, able to teach, patient when wronged,
reason: The Greek is δοῦλον κυρίου; δοῦλος is "slave" in this edition (cf. Titus 1:1 "a slave of God").

old: The pronoun "whom" (tinon) is plural in Greek, encompassing Timothy's mother and grandmother (1:5) as well as Paul.
new: The pronoun "whom" (tinon) is plural in Greek, probably including Timothy's mother and grandmother (1:5) as well as Paul.
reason: τίνων is plural, but who is included is an inference; the note should not state it as fact.

old: in hope of eternal life, which God, who never lies, promised before eternal ages,
new: in hope of eternal life, which God, who never lies, promised before eternal times,
reason: πρὸ χρόνων αἰωνίων is "before eternal times" at 2 Tim 1:9; χρόνος is "time," not "age."

old: and at the proper times manifested His word through the proclamation with which I was entrusted according to the command of God our Savior,
new: but at the proper times manifested His word through the proclamation with which I was entrusted according to the command of God our Savior,
reason: ἐφανέρωσεν δέ contrasts the manifestation with the promise made before eternal times; adversative δέ is lost with "and."

old: Remind them to submit to rulers and authorities, to be obedient, to be ready for every good work,
new: Remind them to submit to rulers, to authorities, to be obedient, to be ready for every good work,
reason: This Greek reads ἀρχαῖς ἐξουσίαις without καί; "and" follows the variant ἀρχαῖς καὶ ἐξουσίαις.

old: The word is trustworthy, and concerning these things I want you to insist confidently, so that those who have believed in God may be careful to devote themselves to good deeds. These things are good and profitable for people.
new: The saying is trustworthy, and concerning these things I want you to insist confidently, so that those who have believed in God may be careful to devote themselves to good deeds. These things are good and profitable for people.
reason: The formula πιστὸς ὁ λόγος is rendered with "saying" everywhere else in the Pastorals (1 Tim 1:15; 3:1; 4:9; 2 Tim 2:11).

old: For to which of the angels has He ever said, "You are My Son; I have fathered You today," and again, "I will be to Him a Father, and He will be to Me a Son"?
new: For to which of the angels has He ever said, "You are My Son; today I have fathered You," and again, "I will be to Him a Father, and He will be to Me a Son"?
reason: Identical Greek ἐγὼ σήμερον γεγέννηκά σε is rendered "today I have fathered You" in Heb 5:5 and Acts 13:33, which also follows the Greek order.

old: Greek βραχύ τι ("a little") can express either degree ("a little lower," as in Psalm 8:5) or duration ("for a little while," highlighting Christ's temporary humiliation in 2:9).
new: Greek βραχύ τι ("a little") can express either degree ("a little lower," as in Psalm 8:5) or duration ("for a little while"); the same phrase recurs in 2:9.
reason: Removes theological commentary ("Christ's temporary humiliation"); keeps the lexical point.

old: For it is impossible for those who have once been enlightened, and have tasted the heavenly gift, and have become partakers of the Holy Spirit,
new: For it is impossible, in the case of those who have once been enlightened, and have tasted the heavenly gift, and have become partakers of the Holy Spirit,
reason: τοὺς ... φωτισθέντας is the object of the active infinitive ἀνακαινίζειν (6:6), not the subject of a passive; restructured so 6:6 can keep the active voice.

old: and have fallen away, to be renewed again to repentance, since they crucify the Son of God again for themselves and expose Him to public disgrace.
new: and have fallen away, to renew them again to repentance, since they crucify the Son of God again for themselves and expose Him to public disgrace.
reason: πάλιν ἀνακαινίζειν is active ("to renew again"), not passive "to be renewed".

old: The Greek infinitive anakainizein is active (literally "to renew [them] again to repentance"). Greek anastaurountas can mean either "crucifying again" or simply "crucifying," and its force may be causal ("since") or temporal ("while").
new: Greek anastaurountas can mean either "crucifying again" or simply "crucifying," and its force may be causal ("since") or temporal ("while").
reason: The English now renders ἀνακαινίζειν actively, so the first sentence explaining the passive rendering is no longer needed.

old: And those of the sons of Levi who receive the priestly office have a commandment to collect a tenth from the people according to the Law, that is, from their brothers, even though they have come from the loins of Abraham.
new: And those of the sons of Levi who receive the priestly office have a commandment to collect a tenth from the people according to the law, that is, from their brothers, even though they have come from the loins of Abraham.
reason: νόμος is "the law" (lowercase) throughout the edition, including Heb 10:1, 10:8, 10:28 and James; Heb 7-9 alone capitalizes it.

old: Now if perfection were through the Levitical priesthood (for on the basis of it the people received the Law), what further need would there be for another priest to arise according to the order of Melchizedek, and not be designated according to the order of Aaron?
new: Now if perfection were through the Levitical priesthood (for on the basis of it the people received the law), what further need would there be for another priest to arise according to the order of Melchizedek, and not be designated according to the order of Aaron?
reason: Edition-wide lowercase "law" for νόμος (cf. Heb 10:1, 10:8, 10:28).

old: (for the Law made nothing perfect), and on the other hand, the bringing in of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
new: (for the law made nothing perfect), and on the other hand, the bringing in of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
reason: Edition-wide lowercase "law" for ὁ νόμος (cf. Heb 10:1).

old: For the Law appoints men who have weakness as high priests, but the word of the oath, which came after the Law, appoints a Son who has been made perfect forever.
new: For the law appoints men who have weakness as high priests, but the word of the oath, which came after the law, appoints a Son who has been made perfect forever.
reason: Edition-wide lowercase "law" for ὁ νόμος (cf. Heb 10:1).
