old: Now if He were on earth, He would not even be a priest, since there are those who offer the gifts according to the Law;
new: Now if He were on earth, He would not even be a priest, since there are those who offer the gifts according to the law;
reason: Same κατὰ νόμον is "according to the law" in Heb 10:8; edition uses lowercase.

old: The Greek text reads γενομένων ("that have come") rather than the variant μελλόντων ("to come"), emphasizing blessings already realized through Christ.
new: The Greek text reads γενομένων ("that have come") rather than the variant μελλόντων ("to come").
reason: Removes theological interpretation; the textual fact stands on its own.

old: In verses 16-17, the Greek noun διαθήκη ("covenant") shifts to its legal sense of "will" or "testament," playing on the dual meaning of the term to explain the necessity of Christ's death.
new: In verses 16-17, the Greek noun διαθήκη ("covenant") shifts to its legal sense of "will" or "testament," playing on the dual meaning of the term.
reason: Removes doctrinal commentary ("to explain the necessity of Christ's death"); keeps the lexical explanation.

old: for a will is confirmed only upon death, since it is never in force while the one who made it is alive.
new: for a will is confirmed upon death, since it is never in force while the one who made it is alive.
reason: ἐπὶ νεκροῖς βεβαία has no "only"; the restriction is expressed by the following ἐπεί clause.

old: For when every commandment according to the Law had been spoken by Moses to all the people, he took the blood of the calves and the goats, with water and scarlet wool and hyssop, and sprinkled both the scroll itself and all the people,
new: For when every commandment according to the law had been spoken by Moses to all the people, he took the blood of the calves and the goats, with water and scarlet wool and hyssop, and sprinkled both the scroll itself and all the people,
reason: Edition-wide lowercase "law" for νόμος (cf. Heb 10:8 "according to the law").

old: And according to the Law nearly everything is cleansed with blood, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.
new: And according to the law nearly everything is cleansed with blood, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.
reason: Edition-wide lowercase "law" for νόμος (cf. Heb 10:8 "according to the law").

old: And every priest stands day by day ministering and repeatedly offering the same sacrifices, which can never completely remove sins.
new: And every priest stands day by day ministering and repeatedly offering the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins.
reason: περιελεῖν is "take away" (as for περιαιρέω in 2 Cor 3:16); "completely" is an added intensifier.

old: Greek anti here is most commonly rendered "for the sake of" the joy awaiting Him, though some take it as "instead of" the joy He relinquished.
new: Greek anti here may mean "for (the sake of)" the joy set before Him or "instead of" a joy He gave up.
reason: Removes a claim about how the word is commonly rendered by translations; states the two senses of ἀντί neutrally.

old: The meaning of "altar" here is debated, variously understood as Christ's sacrifice on the cross, Christ Himself, or the heavenly sanctuary, contrasted with the Levitical tabernacle service.
reason: θυσιαστήριον is rendered literally as "altar"; the note is a survey of theological interpretations, not an explanation of the Greek or of a translation choice.

old: For the bodies of those animals whose blood is brought into the holy places by the high priest for sin are burned up outside the camp.
new: For the bodies of those animals whose blood is brought into the sanctuary by the high priest for sin are burned up outside the camp.
reason: εἰς τὰ ἅγια with the high priest bringing blood is "into the sanctuary" in Heb 9:12, 9:25 (cf. 8:2, 9:8, 10:19).

old: So then, let us go out to Him outside the camp, bearing His disgrace.
new: So then, let us go out to Him outside the camp, bearing His reproach.
reason: τὸν ὀνειδισμὸν αὐτοῦ echoes τὸν ὀνειδισμὸν τοῦ Χριστοῦ, rendered "the reproach of Christ" in 11:26 (cf. "reproaches" 10:33).

old: Know this, my beloved brothers: every person must be quick to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger,
new: Know this, my beloved brothers. And every person must be quick to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger,
reason: The Greek has a full stop after ἀγαπητοί and a new clause with δέ (ἔστω δὲ πᾶς ἄνθρωπος); the colon made the exhortation the content of Ἴστε and dropped δέ.

old: If, however, you are truly fulfilling the royal law according to the Scripture, "You shall love your neighbor as yourself," you are doing well.
new: If, however, you are fulfilling the royal law according to the Scripture, "You shall love your neighbor as yourself," you are doing well.
reason: μέντοι is already rendered by "however"; "truly" renders it a second time and adds emphasis.

old: And the tongue is a fire; as the world of unrighteousness, the tongue is placed among our members, staining the entire body and setting ablaze the wheel of existence, while itself being set ablaze by hell.
new: And the tongue is a fire; as the world of unrighteousness, the tongue is placed among our members, staining the entire body and setting ablaze the wheel of existence, while itself being set ablaze by Gehenna.
reason: γέεννα is rendered "Gehenna" in this edition.

old: "The wheel of existence" (ton trochon tes geneseos) is a vivid metaphor for the whole cycle of human life; "hell" translates Greek Gehenna.
new: "The wheel of existence" (ton trochon tes geneseos) is literally "the wheel of origin (or birth)," a metaphor for the whole course of human life.
reason: The verse now reads "Gehenna," so the second clause is obsolete; the literal sense of γενέσεως is added to explain the rendering.

old: "Unspiritual" translates psychike, literally "soulish" or "merely natural," describing wisdom operating on a purely human level apart from God's Spirit.
new: "Unspiritual" translates psychike, literally "soulish" or "natural."
reason: Removes interpretive theological commentary ("apart from God's Spirit"); keeps the lexical explanation of ψυχική.

old: In this regard, they are surprised that you do not run together with them into the same flood of reckless dissipation, slandering you;
new: In this regard, they are surprised that you do not run together with them into the same flood of reckless dissipation, and they speak abusively;
reason: βλασφημοῦντες has no expressed object; supplying "you" decides a referent the Greek leaves open (the readers, God, or the Christian way).

old: Likewise, you younger ones, submit to the elders. And all of you, clothe yourselves in humility toward one another, because "God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble."
new: Likewise, you younger ones, be subject to the elders. And all of you, clothe yourselves in humility toward one another, because "God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble."
reason: ὑποτάγητε is the identical form rendered "Be subject" in 2:13 (cf. 2:18; 3:1, 5); keep the same English.

old: But these people, like unreasoning animals, born by nature for capture and destruction, reviling things of which they are ignorant, will also be destroyed in their own destruction,
new: But these people, like unreasoning animals, born by nature for capture and destruction, reviling things of which they are ignorant, will also be destroyed in their destruction,
reason: ἐν τῇ φθορᾷ αὐτῶν is "in their destruction"; "own" has no Greek basis and decides that αὐτῶν refers to the people rather than the animals.

old: Beloved, this is already the second letter I am writing to you, in both of which I am awakening your sincere mind through a reminder,
new: Beloved, this is already the second letter I am writing to you, in both of which I am stirring up your sincere mind by way of reminder,
reason: διεγείρω ... ἐν ὑπομνήσει deliberately repeats 1:13 (διεγείρειν ὑμᾶς ἐν ὑπομνήσει), rendered there "stir you up by way of reminder".

old: The neuter relative pronoun "What" (Greek ho) and the phrase "the Word of life" embrace both the gospel message proclaimed by the eyewitnesses and the personal Christ who embodies life.
new: The neuter relative "What" (Greek ho) refers broadly to what was heard, seen, and touched; "the Word of life" (tou logou tes zoes) may denote the proclaimed message of life, Christ as the Word, or both.
reason: Old note asserted an interpretation in devotional terms ("the personal Christ who embodies life"); rewritten to state the options neutrally.

old: The Greek noun hilasmos ("propitiation," matching 4:10) refers to an atoning sacrifice that turns away divine wrath and removes sin; it is also variously rendered "atoning sacrifice" or "expiation."
new: Greek hilasmos (also in 4:10) denotes a means of atonement for sin; whether it stresses turning away wrath (propitiation) or removing sin (expiation) is debated.
reason: Old note asserted one side of a disputed theological sense and made a claim about other renderings; rewritten neutrally.

old: The Greek hilasmos ('propitiation') refers to an atoning sacrifice that removes sin and turns away divine wrath.
new: On hilasmos ("propitiation"), see the note at 2:2.
reason: Old note asserted a contested theological definition of hilasmos; point to the neutral note at 2:2 instead.

old: The earliest Greek manuscripts read simply 'We love' without a direct object; later manuscripts add 'Him'.
new: This text reads simply 'We love' without a direct object; other manuscripts add 'Him' or 'God'.
reason: "The earliest Greek manuscripts" overstates the evidence (early witnesses also add 'God'); state what this text reads and the variants neutrally.

old: In this way we know that we love God's children: whenever we love God and keep His commandments.
new: By this we know that we love God's children: whenever we love God and keep His commandments.
reason: ἐν τούτῳ γινώσκομεν is rendered "By this we know" everywhere else in the letter (2:3, 5; 3:24; 4:13).

old: The shift from the perfect participle ('everyone who has been born of God') to the aorist participle ('the One who was born of God') with the object 'him' (auton) in the earliest manuscripts points to Christ guarding the believer; later manuscripts read 'keeps himself' (heauton).
new: The shift from the perfect participle ('everyone who has been born of God') to the aorist participle ('the One who was born of God') with the object 'him' (auton), as this text reads, is commonly taken to refer to Christ guarding the believer; other manuscripts read 'keeps himself' (heauton).
reason: Old note's "earliest" vs. "later" manuscripts claim is inaccurate (heauton is also attested early); state the text's reading and the variant neutrally.

old: Grammatically, 'This One' (houtos) can refer either to the nearest antecedent, Jesus Christ, or back to 'the True One' (God the Father); many interpreters see an intentional affirmation of Christ's full deity.
new: Grammatically, 'This One' (houtos) can refer either to the nearest antecedent, Jesus Christ, or back to 'the True One' (God the Father).
reason: Removed the doctrinal clause "many interpreters see an intentional affirmation of Christ's full deity"; the grammatical explanation remains.

old: May mercy, peace, and love be multiplied for you.
new: May mercy, peace, and love be multiplied to you.
reason: The formula πληθυνθείη with ὑμῖν is rendered "be multiplied to you" in 1 Peter 1:2 and 2 Peter 1:2.

old: The earliest and strongest manuscripts read "Jesus" (Ἰησοῦς) as the one who saved Israel out of Egypt, whereas other manuscripts read "the Lord" (κύριος) or "God" (θεός).
new: This text reads "Jesus" (Ἰησοῦς) as the one who saved a people out of Egypt; other manuscripts read "the Lord" (κύριος) or "God" (θεός).
reason: "The earliest and strongest manuscripts" is an evaluative and debatable claim; state the text's reading and the variants neutrally.

old: and angels who did not keep their own sphere of authority, but left their own dwelling, He has kept under deep gloom in eternal bonds for the judgment of the great day;
new: and angels who did not keep their own sphere of authority, but left their own dwelling, He has kept under gloom in eternal bonds for the judgment of the great day;
reason: ὑπὸ ζόφον is "under gloom" (ζόφος = "gloom" in v. 13); "deep" has no Greek basis.

old: These are the hidden reefs in your love feasts as they feast with you, shepherding themselves without fear; waterless clouds swept along by winds; late-autumn trees without fruit, twice dead, uprooted;
new: These are the hidden reefs in your love feasts as they feast together, shepherding themselves without fear; waterless clouds swept along by winds; late-autumn trees without fruit, twice dead, uprooted;
reason: This Greek has συνευωχούμενοι without ὑμῖν (contrast 2 Peter 2:13); "with you" follows the reading with ὑμῖν.

old: These are grumblers, malcontents, walking according to their own desires; and their mouth speaks boastful things, flattering people for the sake of advantage.
new: These are grumblers, malcontents, walking according to their desires; and their mouth speaks boastful things, flattering people for the sake of advantage.
reason: κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας αὐτῶν has the plain pronoun αὐτῶν (not ἑαυτῶν as in v. 18); "own" is added.

old: These are the ones who cause divisions, merely natural people, not having the Spirit.
new: These are the ones who cause divisions, natural people, not having the Spirit.
reason: ψυχικοί is simply "natural"; "merely" is an added qualifier with no Greek basis.

old: The revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave to Him to show His servants the things that must happen soon; and He signified it by sending it through His angel to His servant John,
new: The revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave to Him to show His slaves the things that must happen soon; and He signified it by sending it through His angel to His slave John,
reason: δούλοις / δούλῳ: the edition renders δοῦλος as "slave" (as in 6:11, 19:2, 19:5 here).

old: The Greek deliberately places the divine title "the One who is and who was and who is coming" in the nominative case after the preposition "from" (which normally takes the genitive), treating it as an indeclinable divine name echoing Exodus 3:14. "The seven spirits" is variously understood as the sevenfold fullness of the Holy Spirit (cf. Isaiah 11:2) or seven heavenly spirits before God's throne.
new: The Greek places the title "the One who is and who was and who is coming" in the nominative case after the preposition "from" (which normally takes the genitive), treating it as indeclinable. "The seven spirits" is variously understood as the sevenfold fullness of the Holy Spirit (cf. Isaiah 11:2) or seven heavenly spirits before God's throne.
reason: Removes claims of authorial intent ("deliberately") and an interpretive intertextual assertion; keeps the grammatical explanation.

old: "The Lord's day" (he kyriake hemera) is the sole occurrence of this phrase in the New Testament and is widely understood as Sunday, the weekly commemoration of Christ's resurrection, though some interpreters view it as a reference to the eschatological Day of the Lord.
new: "The Lord's day" (he kyriake hemera) uses the adjective kyriakos ("belonging to the Lord"); the phrase occurs only here in the New Testament.
reason: Replaces interpretive/devotional comment with a neutral lexical note on κυριακῇ ἡμέρᾳ.

old: Do not fear at all the things you are about to suffer. Look, the devil is about to throw some of you into prison so that you may be tested, and you will have affliction for ten days. Prove yourself faithful until death, and I will give you the crown of life.
new: Do not fear at all the things you are about to suffer. Look, the devil is about to throw some of you into prison so that you may be tested, and you will have affliction for ten days. Be faithful until death, and I will give you the crown of life.
reason: γίνου πιστός is simply "be faithful"; "prove yourself" adds a nuance not in the Greek.

old: And to the angel of the church in Pergamum write: "This is what the One who has the sharp two-edged sword says:
new: And to the angel of the church in Pergamum write: "This is what the One who has the sharp double-edged sword says:
reason: ῥομφαία δίστομος ὀξεῖα is "sharp double-edged sword" in 1:16; same Greek, same English.

old: And to the angel of the church in Thyatira write: "This is what the Son of God says, the One who has His eyes like a flame of fire, and His feet are like burnished bronze:
new: And to the angel of the church in Thyatira write: "This is what the Son of God says, the One who has His eyes like a flame of fire, and His feet are like fine bronze:
reason: χαλκολιβάνῳ is rendered "fine bronze" in 1:15 (whose note cross-references 2:18); same Greek, same English.

old: Greek chalkolibanos ("burnished bronze") is a rare word denoting an uncertain luminous metal alloy, likely fine bronze or brass glowing in a furnace.
new: Greek chalkolibanos ("fine bronze") is a rare word denoting an uncertain luminous metal alloy, likely fine bronze or brass glowing in a furnace.
reason: Note gloss aligned with the verse rendering "fine bronze" (cf. 1:15).

old: But I have this against you: you tolerate the woman Jezebel, who calls herself a prophetess, and she teaches and misleads My servants to commit sexual immorality and to eat things sacrificed to idols.
new: But I have this against you: you tolerate the woman Jezebel, who calls herself a prophetess, and she teaches and misleads My slaves to commit sexual immorality and to eat things sacrificed to idols.
reason: τοὺς ἐμοὺς δούλους: the edition renders δοῦλος as "slave".

old: And to the angel of the church in Sardis write: "These things says the One who has the seven Spirits of God and the seven stars: I know your works, that you have a name that you are alive, and you are dead.
new: And to the angel of the church in Sardis write: "This is what the One who has the seven spirits of God and the seven stars says: I know your works, that you have a name that you are alive, and you are dead.
reason: Τάδε λέγει is "This is what ... says" in 2:1, 2:8, 2:12, 2:18; τὰ ἑπτὰ πνεύματα is lowercase "seven spirits" in 1:4 and 5:6, and capitalizing here silently decides a disputed referent.

old: The one who conquers will thus be clothed in white garments, and I will by no means erase his name from the book of life, and I will acknowledge his name before My Father and before His angels.
new: The one who overcomes will thus be clothed in white garments, and I will by no means erase his name from the book of life, and I will acknowledge his name before My Father and before His angels.
reason: ὁ νικῶν in the letters is "the one who overcomes" in 2:7, 2:11, 2:17, 2:26 (and 21:7).

old: And to the angel of the church in Philadelphia write: "These things says the Holy One, the True One, the One who has the key of David, the One who opens and no one will shut, and who shuts and no one opens:
new: And to the angel of the church in Philadelphia write: "This is what the Holy One, the True One, the One who has the key of David, the One who opens and no one will shut, and who shuts and no one opens, says:
reason: Τάδε λέγει is rendered "This is what ... says" in 2:1, 2:8, 2:12, 2:18.

old: The one who conquers, I will make him a pillar in the temple of My God, and he will by no means go outside anymore, and I will write on him the name of My God, and the name of the city of My God, the new Jerusalem, which comes down out of heaven from My God, and My new name.
new: The one who overcomes, I will make him a pillar in the temple of My God, and he will by no means go outside anymore, and I will write on him the name of My God, and the name of the city of My God, the new Jerusalem, which comes down out of heaven from My God, and My new name.
reason: ὁ νικῶν in the letters is "the one who overcomes" in 2:7, 2:11, 2:17, 2:26.

old: And to the angel of the church in Laodicea write: "These things says the Amen, the faithful and true witness, the beginning of the creation of God:
new: And to the angel of the church in Laodicea write: "This is what the Amen, the faithful and true witness, the beginning of the creation of God, says:
reason: Τάδε λέγει is rendered "This is what ... says" in 2:1, 2:8, 2:12, 2:18.

old: The one who conquers, I will grant him to sit with Me on My throne, just as I also conquered and sat down with My Father on His throne.
new: The one who overcomes, I will grant him to sit with Me on My throne, just as I also overcame and sat down with My Father on His throne.
reason: ὁ νικῶν in the letters is "the one who overcomes" (2:7, 2:11, 2:17, 2:26); ἐνίκησα follows the same verb in the same verse.

old: And from the throne proceed flashes of lightning and voices and peals of thunder; and seven torches of fire are burning before the throne, which are the seven Spirits of God,
new: And from the throne proceed flashes of lightning and sounds and peals of thunder; and seven torches of fire are burning before the throne, which are the seven spirits of God,
reason: τὰ ἑπτὰ πνεύματα is lowercase "seven spirits" in 1:4 and 5:6 (capitalizing silently decides a disputed referent); φωναί with lightning and thunder is "sounds" in 8:5 and 11:19.

old: Greek ἦσαν καὶ ἐκτίσθησαν ("they existed and were created") has a notable textual history (some manuscripts read "they are" or "they did not exist"); the order likely expresses that all things have their being and were brought into creation solely by God's will.
new: Greek ἦσαν καὶ ἐκτίσθησαν ("they existed and were created") has a notable textual history; some manuscripts read "they are" or "they did not exist."
reason: Removes theological interpretation ("solely by God's will"); keeps the textual fact.

old: And I saw in the right hand of the One sitting on the throne a scroll written inside and on the back, sealed tightly with seven seals.
new: And I saw on the right hand of the One sitting on the throne a scroll written inside and on the back, sealed up with seven seals.
reason: ἐπὶ τὴν δεξιάν is "on the right hand" (cf. 1:20); κατεσφραγισμένον is "sealed up", "tightly" is an added intensifier.

old: Greek "epi ten dexian" is literally "upon the right hand," picturing the scroll resting on the open palm; a scroll written inside and on the back (an opisthograph) suggests complete, unalterable contents.
reason: The verse now renders ἐπί literally; the remainder of the note is interpretive ("complete, unalterable contents").

old: And I heard every created thing that is in heaven and on the earth and under the earth and on the sea, and all things in them, saying, "To the One sitting on the throne and to the Lamb be the blessing and the honor and the glory and the dominion forever and ever."
new: And I heard every created thing that is in heaven and on the earth and under the earth and on the sea, and all things in them, saying, "To the One sitting on the throne and to the Lamb be the blessing and the honor and the glory and the might forever and ever."
reason: τὸ κράτος in the doxology is "the might" in 1:6; same Greek, same English.

old: The summons "Come!" (Greek erchou) here and in verses 3, 5, and 7 is addressed to the emerging horsemen rather than to John; later manuscripts add "and see," which is absent from the earliest witnesses.
new: The critical text has only "Come!" (Greek erchou) here and in verses 3, 5, and 7; later manuscripts add "and see," which is absent from the earliest witnesses.
reason: Removes an interpretive claim about the addressee, which the Greek does not specify; keeps the textual fact.

old: saying, "Do not harm the earth, nor the sea, nor the trees, until we have sealed the servants of our God on their foreheads."
new: saying, "Do not harm the earth, nor the sea, nor the trees, until we have sealed the slaves of our God on their foreheads."
reason: τοὺς δούλους: the edition renders δοῦλος as "slave" (cf. 6:11, 19:5).

old: And I said to him, "My lord, you know." And he said to me, "These are the ones coming out of the great tribulation, and they have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.
new: And I said to him, "My lord, you know." And he said to me, "These are the ones coming out of the great affliction, and they have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.
reason: θλῖψις is "affliction" throughout Revelation (1:9, 2:9, 2:10, and θλῖψιν μεγάλην "great affliction" in 2:22); "the great tribulation" imports a loaded technical term.

old: "Will spread His tent over them" renders skenosei ep' autous, literally "will tabernacle (or pitch a tent) over them," recalling God's sheltering presence with Israel in the wilderness.
new: "Will spread His tent over them" renders skenosei ep' autous, literally "will tabernacle (or pitch a tent) over them."
reason: Removes interpretive commentary; keeps the lexical explanation of σκηνώσει.

old: A single Greek definite article governs "hour and day and month and year," pointing to one exact, divinely appointed moment rather than a span of time.
new: A single Greek definite article governs "hour and day and month and year," pointing to one exact moment rather than a span of time.
reason: "Divinely appointed" is an interpretive addition; the Greek has only the passive participle ἡτοιμασμένοι, which the verse already renders.

old: but in the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when he is about to blow the trumpet, then the mystery of God will be completed, just as He announced the good news to His own servants the prophets.
new: but in the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when he is about to sound the trumpet, then the mystery of God will be completed, just as He announced the good news to His own slaves the prophets.
reason: τοὺς ἑαυτοῦ δούλους: the edition renders δοῦλος as "slave"; σαλπίζειν is "sound" the trumpet elsewhere in Revelation (8:6-13, 9:1, 9:13).

old: And the seventh angel blew his trumpet, and there were loud voices in heaven, saying, "The kingdom of the world has become our Lord's and His Christ's, and He will reign forever and ever."
new: And the seventh angel sounded his trumpet, and there were loud voices in heaven, saying, "The kingdom of the world has become our Lord's and His Christ's, and He will reign forever and ever."
reason: ἐσάλπισεν is "sounded his trumpet" for the other six angels (8:7-12, 9:1, 9:13).

old: Unlike 1:4, 1:8, and 4:8, the critical Greek text omits "and who is to come" after "who is and who was," since God's reign has now arrived; the aorist ebasileusas ("begun to reign") is ingressive.
new: Unlike 1:4, 1:8, and 4:8, the title here has no "and who is coming" after "who is and who was" (some later manuscripts add it); the aorist ebasileusas ("begun to reign") is ingressive.
reason: Removes an interpretive explanation ("since God's reign has now arrived") and aligns the quoted phrase with the edition's rendering "who is coming".

old: And the nations were enraged, and Your wrath came, and the time for the dead to be judged, and to give the reward to Your servants the prophets and to the saints and to those who fear Your name, the small and the great, and to destroy those who destroy the earth."
new: And the nations were enraged, and Your wrath came, and the time for the dead to be judged, and to give the reward to Your slaves the prophets and to the saints and to those who fear Your name, the small and the great, and to destroy those who destroy the earth."
reason: τοῖς δούλοις σου: the edition renders δοῦλος as "slave".

old: The preposition διά with the accusative strictly expresses cause ("because of"), though many translations render it instrumentally ("by") in this context.
new: The preposition διά with the accusative strictly expresses cause ("because of").
reason: Removes a claim about what other translations do; keeps the grammatical point.

old: And the beast that I saw was like a leopard, and its feet were like those of a bear, and its mouth was like a lion's mouth. And the dragon gave to it its power and its throne and great authority.
new: And the beast that I saw was like a leopard, and its feet were like those of a bear, and its mouth was like a lion's mouth. And the dragon gave to it his power and his throne and great authority.
reason: τὴν δύναμιν αὐτοῦ καὶ τὸν θρόνον αὐτοῦ are the dragon's; "its ... its" reads as the beast's own, and the edition calls the dragon "he/his" in ch. 12.

old: and they worshiped the dragon because it gave the authority to the beast, and they worshiped the beast, saying, "Who is like the beast, and who is able to wage war with it?"
new: and they worshiped the dragon because he gave the authority to the beast, and they worshiped the beast, saying, "Who is like the beast, and who is able to wage war with it?"
reason: The subject of ἔδωκεν is the dragon, referred to as "he" throughout ch. 12 (12:4, 12:9, 12:13, 12:18); keeps it distinct from the beast ("it").

old: And it opened its mouth in blasphemies against God, to blaspheme His name and His dwelling, those who dwell in heaven.
new: And it opened its mouth in blasphemies against God, to blaspheme His name and His tabernacle, those who dwell in heaven.
reason: σκηνή is rendered "tabernacle" in the NT in this edition.

old: And I saw another angel flying in midheaven, having an eternal gospel to proclaim to those who dwell on the earth, and to every nation and tribe and tongue and people,
new: And I saw another angel flying in midheaven, having an eternal gospel to proclaim to those who dwell on the earth, and to every nation and tribe and language and people,
reason: γλῶσσα in this list is "language" elsewhere in Revelation (5:9, 7:9, 10:11, 11:9, 13:7, 17:15).

old: "Mixed undiluted" preserves the deliberate Greek oxymoron κεκερασμένου ἀκράτου: because ancient wine was ordinarily mixed with water, wine mixed at full strength signifies unmitigated divine judgment.
new: "Mixed undiluted" preserves the Greek oxymoron κεκερασμένου ἀκράτου; ancient wine was ordinarily mixed with water.
reason: Removes interpretive/theological commentary ("signifies unmitigated divine judgment"); keeps the lexical explanation.

old: One thousand six hundred stadia equals roughly 184 miles (about 296 kilometers), while the number itself (4 × 4 × 100) also functions symbolically to suggest complete extent.
new: One thousand six hundred stadia equals roughly 184 miles (about 296 kilometers).
reason: Removes speculative symbolic interpretation not grounded in the Greek.

old: And I saw another sign in heaven, great and marvelous: seven angels having seven plagues, the last ones, because in them the wrath of God is completed.
new: And I saw another sign in heaven, great and marvelous: seven angels having seven plagues, the last ones, because in them the fury of God is completed.
reason: θυμὸς τοῦ θεοῦ is "the fury of God" in 14:10, 14:19, 16:1, keeping it distinct from ὀργή "wrath" (cf. 16:19 "the fury of His wrath").

old: And they sing the song of Moses, the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb, saying, "Great and marvelous are Your works, Lord God, the Almighty; righteous and true are Your ways, King of the ages.
new: And they sing the song of Moses, the slave of God, and the song of the Lamb, saying, "Great and marvelous are Your works, Lord God, the Almighty; righteous and true are Your ways, King of the ages.
reason: τοῦ δούλου τοῦ θεοῦ: the edition renders δοῦλος as "slave".

old: The critical text has no explicit object ("You") after "fear" (φοβηθῇ), though some manuscripts add σε; ὅσιος ("holy") emphasizes God's devout purity and faithfulness.
new: The critical text has no explicit object ("You") after "fear" (φοβηθῇ), though some manuscripts add σε.
reason: Removes an interpretive gloss on ὅσιος; keeps the textual fact.

old: And after these things I looked, and the sanctuary of the tent of testimony in heaven was opened,
new: And after these things I looked, and the temple of the tabernacle of testimony in heaven was opened,
reason: ναός is "temple" elsewhere in Revelation (e.g. 11:19, 14:15, 14:17); σκηνή is "tabernacle" in this edition's NT.

old: and the seven angels having the seven plagues came out of the sanctuary, clothed in pure, bright linen and wrapped around their chests with golden sashes.
new: and the seven angels having the seven plagues came out of the temple, clothed in pure, bright linen and belted around their chests with golden sashes.
reason: ναός is "temple" elsewhere in Revelation; περιεζωσμένοι ... ζώνας χρυσᾶς matches "belted around His chest with a golden sash" in 1:13.

old: While an early textual variant reads λίθον ("stone," as in a precious stone), the critical text reads λίνον ("linen"), evoking priestly attire.
new: While an early textual variant reads λίθον ("stone," as in a precious stone), the critical text reads λίνον ("linen").
reason: Removes interpretive comment; keeps the textual fact.

old: And one of the four living creatures gave the seven angels seven golden bowls filled with the wrath of God, the One who lives forever and ever.
new: And one of the four living creatures gave the seven angels seven golden bowls filled with the fury of God, the One who lives forever and ever.
reason: τοῦ θυμοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ is "the fury of God" in 14:10, 14:19 and 16:1 ("the seven bowls of the fury of God").

old: And the sanctuary was filled with smoke from the glory of God and from His power, and no one was able to enter the sanctuary until the seven plagues of the seven angels were completed.
new: And the temple was filled with smoke from the glory of God and from His power, and no one was able to enter the temple until the seven plagues of the seven angels were completed.
reason: ναός is "temple" elsewhere in Revelation (11:19, 14:15, 14:17, 21:22).

old: And I heard a loud voice out of the sanctuary saying to the seven angels, "Go and pour out the seven bowls of the fury of God onto the earth."
new: And I heard a loud voice out of the temple saying to the seven angels, "Go and pour out the seven bowls of the fury of God onto the earth."
reason: ναός is "temple" elsewhere in Revelation.

old: And the second poured out his bowl into the sea, and it became blood like that of a dead person, and every soul of life died, everything in the sea.
new: And the second poured out his bowl into the sea, and it became blood like that of a dead person, and every living soul died, everything in the sea.
reason: This Greek reads πᾶσα ψυχὴ ζῶσα ("every living soul"), not ψυχὴ ζωῆς ("soul of life") as in other editions.

old: Greek reads "every soul of life" (pasa psyche zoes, a Semitic genitive of quality meaning "every living creature"; compare Gen 1:30 LXX), and places the neuter plural phrase "the things in the sea" (ta en te thalasse) in apposition to the feminine singular noun, a characteristic grammatical irregularity in Revelation.
new: The Greek places the neuter plural phrase "the things in the sea" (ta en te thalasse) in apposition to the feminine singular "every living soul" (pasa psyche zosa), a characteristic grammatical irregularity in Revelation.
reason: The note's claim that the Greek reads psyche zoes is false for this text (ψυχὴ ζῶσα); keeps the valid grammatical point.

old: The divine title "the One who is and who was" omits the third element "and who is to come" (cf. Rev 1:4, 8; 4:8), signaling that the final judgment has now arrived.
new: The title "the One who is and who was" lacks the third element "and who is coming" found in 1:4, 1:8, and 4:8.
reason: Removes interpretive inference ("signaling that the final judgment has now arrived") and aligns the quoted phrase with the edition's "who is coming".

old: And the seventh poured out his bowl into the air—and a loud voice came out of the sanctuary from the throne, saying, "It is done!"—
new: And the seventh poured out his bowl into the air—and a loud voice came out of the temple from the throne, saying, "It is done!"—
reason: ναός is "temple" elsewhere in Revelation.

old: and there were flashes of lightning and voices and peals of thunder, and a great earthquake occurred, such as had not occurred since people came to be on the earth, an earthquake so immense, so great.
new: and there were flashes of lightning and sounds and peals of thunder, and a great earthquake occurred, such as had not occurred since people came to be on the earth, an earthquake so immense, so great.
reason: φωναί with lightning and thunder is "sounds" in 8:5 and 11:19.

old: The clause "and they are seven kings" appears at the end of verse 9 in the Greek text (placed in verse 10 in some translations) and can also be rendered "and there are seven kings."
new: The clause "and they are seven kings" stands at the end of verse 9 in the Greek text and can also be rendered "and there are seven kings."
reason: Removes a claim about what other translations do.

old: because from the wine of the passion of her sexual immorality all the nations have fallen, and the kings of the earth committed sexual immorality with her, and the merchants of the earth grew rich from the power of her luxury."
new: because from the wine of the fury of her sexual immorality all the nations have fallen, and the kings of the earth committed sexual immorality with her, and the merchants of the earth grew rich from the power of her luxury."
reason: The identical phrase τοῦ οἴνου τοῦ θυμοῦ τῆς πορνείας αὐτῆς is "the wine of the fury of her sexual immorality" in 14:8.

old: The verb ἐβασίλευσεν ("has begun to reign") is an ingressive aorist, highlighting the decisive inauguration of God's universal reign rather than merely an ongoing state.
new: The verb ἐβασίλευσεν ("has begun to reign") is taken as an ingressive aorist.
reason: Removes theological commentary ("decisive inauguration of God's universal reign"); keeps the grammatical point.

old: The verb ποιμανεῖ ("will shepherd") echoes Psalm 2:9 in the Septuagint, where shepherding with an iron rod represents stern, decisive authority over hostile nations.
new: The verb ποιμανεῖ ("will shepherd") echoes Psalm 2:9 in the Septuagint.
reason: Removes interpretive commentary; keeps the factual allusion.

old: And I saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, descending out of heaven from God, prepared like a bride adorned for her husband.
new: And I saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, descending out of heaven from God, prepared like a bride adorned for her husband.
reason: Ἰερουσαλὴμ καινήν is "the new Jerusalem" (lowercase adjective) in 3:12.

old: And I heard a loud voice from the throne saying, "Look, the dwelling of God is with people, and He will dwell with them, and they will be His peoples, and God Himself will be with them,
new: And I heard a loud voice from the throne saying, "Look, the tabernacle of God is with people, and He will dwell with them, and they will be His peoples, and God Himself will be with them,
reason: ἡ σκηνή is rendered "tabernacle" in this edition's NT.

old: And there will be no curse any longer. And the throne of God and of the Lamb will be in it, and His servants will serve Him,
new: And there will be no curse any longer. And the throne of God and of the Lamb will be in it, and His slaves will serve Him,
reason: οἱ δοῦλοι αὐτοῦ: the edition renders δοῦλος as "slave" (cf. 19:2, 19:5).

old: Greek katathema (a New Testament hapax) can mean either "curse" or "accursed thing" (cf. Zech 14:11). The singular pronouns "His" and "Him" refer jointly to God and the Lamb sharing one throne.
new: Greek katathema (a New Testament hapax) can mean either "curse" or "accursed thing" (cf. Zech 14:11). The singular pronouns "His" and "Him" follow the mention of both God and the Lamb.
reason: The Greek αὐτοῦ/αὐτῷ does not specify a joint referent; the note should not decide it.

old: And he said to me, "These words are faithful and true, and the Lord, the God of the spirits of the prophets, sent His angel to show His servants the things that must happen soon;
new: And he said to me, "These words are faithful and true, and the Lord, the God of the spirits of the prophets, sent His angel to show His slaves the things that must happen soon;
reason: τοῖς δούλοις αὐτοῦ: the edition renders δοῦλος as "slave".

old: And he said to me, "Do not do that! I am a fellow servant of yours and of your brothers the prophets and of those who keep the words of this book. Worship God."
new: And he said to me, "See that you do not! I am a fellow slave of yours and of your brothers the prophets and of those who keep the words of this book. Worship God."
reason: Identical Greek in 19:10 (Ὅρα μή· σύνδουλός σού εἰμι) is rendered "See that you do not! I am a fellow slave of yours".

old: Let the one who acts unjustly still act unjustly, and let the filthy one still be defiled, and let the righteous one still do righteousness, and let the holy one still be made holy."
new: Let the one who acts unjustly still act unjustly, and let the filthy one still be made filthy, and let the righteous one still do righteousness, and let the holy one still be made holy."
reason: ὁ ῥυπαρὸς ῥυπανθήτω repeats the same root like the other three clauses; "be made filthy" keeps the Greek repetition.

old: And the Spirit and the bride say, "Come." And let the one who hears say, "Come." And let the one who is thirsty come; let the one who desires take the water of life freely.
new: And the Spirit and the bride say, "Come." And let the one who hears say, "Come." And let the one who is thirsty come; let the one who desires take the water of life without cost.
reason: δωρεάν with the water of life is "without cost" in 21:6; "freely" can be misread as "without restraint".
